# Of the Jews’ Unbridled Doctrine of God the Father.
<margin>D 2</margin>
<meta>catchword: (or</meta>

<note>original: "אמר רבי עקיבא אלולי הדבר כתוב אי אפשר לאומרו אמרו ישראל לפני השמים לטוהר. הקדוש ברוך הוא עצמך פדית"</note> Rabbi Akiva said: "If the matter were not written in Scripture, it would be impossible to say it. Israel said before the pure Heavens: 'The Holy One, blessed be He—You have redeemed Your own Self.'" That is: You find that at all times in which the Israelites were placed into servitude, the Divine Majesty was subjected to servitude along with them, as is said in Exodus 24, verse 10: **And they saw the God of Israel, and there was under His feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone.** <note>The author is referencing a Rabbinic tradition where the "sapphire work" represents the bricks the Israelites were forced to make in Egypt, suggesting God felt their burden.</note> However, after they were redeemed, what does the Scripture say of it? (It speaks immediately following the previous words:) **And as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.** Rabbi Akiva said that if this matter were not written in the Holy Scripture, one would not dare to say it. The Israelites said to the holy, blessed God: "You have redeemed Yourself." Thus, the aforementioned words, *asher paditha lecha mimmizraim* <note>original: "אשר פדית לך ממצרים" — "whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt"</note>, according to such a foolish opinion, must be interpreted thus: "You who have redeemed Yourself out of Egypt," just as if the little word *lecha* <note term="lecha">In Hebrew, 'lecha' usually means 'to you' or 'for you,' but the author argues the Jewish interpretation treats it as a reflexive accusative, 'Yourself.'</note> signified the accusative "Yourself" and not the dative "for You."

# Concerning the Unseemly Teaching of the Jews regarding God the Father.
## D 3

<note>original Hebrew: "לגרום שוכה ושובם ממנו הסוד אמרם ז"ל אין חבוש מתיר עצמו מבית האסורים והגאולה ביד ישראל שהיא התשובה"</note>
<note>This Hebrew passage explains a mystical "secret": "A prisoner cannot release himself from the house of prisoners," implying God cannot free Himself from exile without Israel's help.</note>
That is: **"The holy and blessed God does not enter the upper Jerusalem until He first enters the lower Jerusalem,"** (which words also appear in the little book *Tuv HaAretz* <note>original: "Tuf haaretz" — *The Goodness of the Land*, a 17th-century Kabbalistic work by Nathan Shapira.</note> folio 38, column 4, though slightly altered). The redemption, however, is delayed (and postponed) through the sins of Israel, because the **Divine Majesty** <term>Shekhinah: The presence of God residing in the world.</term> is with them in captivity, for "the mother does not leave her children." She is also with them in all places to which they have been led away captive. Just as those same causes <note>meaning the sins of the people</note> were the reason that both She (namely, the Divine Majesty) and they themselves were driven among the nations into misery—which is a prison—so too must they be a cause for Her and them to come back out of it. And this is the secret of that which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say: **"A prisoner does not release himself from prison."** <note>A common Talmudic maxim meaning that one who is bound depends on another for liberation.</note> The redemption of the same (meaning the Divine Majesty), therefore, stands in the hand of Israel, namely, through penance and conversion.

What is the cause? 'The birds of the heavens, together with the beasts, have taken flight and gone away.'"** <note>Quoting Jeremiah 9:10.</note> And the word **Behemah** <note>original: "בהמה" — beast or cattle.</note> through **Gematria** <note>A system of Jewish numerology where letters represent numbers.</note> (when it is calculated as a number) makes fifty-two (which number is intended to signify the aforementioned fifty-two years). <note>In Hebrew, B=2, H=5, M=40, H=5, totaling 52.</note> Following this, it continues further: <note>original Hebrew: "א"ר חנינא ברבי אבהו שבע מאות מיני דגים טהורים ושמנה מאות מיני חגבים טהורים ועופות לאין מספר וכולן גלו עם ישראל לבבל וכשחזרו חזרו עמהם חוץ מדג אחד ששמו שיבוטא ודגים איך גלו ר' חונא בשם ר' יוסי אמר דרך התום גלו ודרך התום חזרו"</note> That is: **"Rabbi Chanina, the son of Rabbi Abhu, says: There were seven hundred species of clean fish and eight hundred species of clean locusts, and birds without number, all of which went with the Israelites into misery in Babylon. When they came to him, they said: "Just as you prayed that it should rain, so pray now that it should stop." But he said to them: "Go out and see if the **Stone of the Strayers** <term>Even HaToim: A high stone in ancient Jerusalem where people would stand to announce lost or found items.</term> (which was a large upright stone in Jerusalem) is covered."

# Concerning the Jews’ Unseemly Teaching of God the Father.

...so that **God** might not have wished to reveal to the angels that wicked people would also descend from Adam, so that they would not be a hindrance to his creation.

In such a way, the ministering angels wanted to prevent **God** from accepting and receiving King Manasseh—who was carrying regret and penance for the sins he had committed—into grace. Regarding this, it is written in the book *Schené luchóth habberíth* (or *Schené lúchos hábberis*) <note>original: "שני לוחות הברית" — *The Two Tablets of the Covenant*, a famous 17th-century work of Jewish law and mysticism by Isaiah Horowitz, often called the *Shelah* after its acronym.</note> on folio 180, column 2:

<note>original Hebrew: "ר' יהושע אומר תדע לך כח התשובה , בא וראה במנשה בן חזקיה שעשה כל התועבות רעות שבעולם והרבה לעשות הרע בעיני ה' להכעיסו וכו' עד ובאו שרי גדודי אשור והורידו אותו בבלה וכו' ושם קרא לכל אלהים אחרים שזבח להם ואין אחד מהם קורא אותו ולא עונה אותו ומצילו אמר אקרא לאלהי אבותי בכל לבי אולי יעשה ה' לי ככל נפלאותיו וכשקרא לאלהי אבותיו ונעתר לו ושמע תפלתי שנאמר ויתפלל אליו ויעתר לו וכו' באותה שעה עמדו מלאכי השרת וסתמו כל החלונות של מעלה ואמרו לפניו רבונו של עולם אדם שהעמיד צלם בהיכל אתה מקבל בתשובה וכו' אמר להם אם איני מקבלו בתשובה הריני נועל דלת בפני כל בעל תשובה מה עשה הקב"ה חתר לו חתירה מתחת כסא כבודו ממקום שאין מלאך יכול לשלוט שם וכו' הה"ד ויתפלל אליו ויעתר וישמע תפלתו ותחנונו :"</note>

That is: Rabbi Yehoshua (or Joshua) says: Know the power of repentance, and consider it in the case of **Manasseh**, the son of **Hezekiah**, who committed all the evil abominations that exist in the world, and (as seen in **2 Chronicles 33:6**) committed much evil in the sight of **God** to provoke Him, *etc.* until (the words in verse 11): *Then the captains of the host of the King of Assyria came and brought him to Babylon,* *etc.* There he called upon all the foreign gods to whom he had sacrificed, but not one of them called back to him, or answered him, or saved him. Then he said: "I will call upon the God of my fathers with all my heart; perhaps the **Lord** will deal with me according to all His wonders." When he then called upon the God of his fathers, He allowed Himself to be entreated and heard his prayer (as read in verse 13). At that same hour, the ministering angels stood up and stopped up all the windows above <note>Refers to the "windows of heaven" through which prayers were believed to pass to reach God.</note> and spoke before Him (namely, **God**): "O You **Lord** of the world, will You receive a man in repentance who set up an idol in the Temple?" *etc.* Then He answered them: "If I do not receive him in his repentance, behold, I close the door to all those who are penitent." What did **God** do? He dug a hole under the Throne of His Glory <margin>But **God** made a hole under His Throne and accepted his repentance.</margin> in a place where no angel can have power. That is what is written (in verse 13): *And he prayed to him; and he allowed himself to be entreated by him, and heard his prayer and his supplication.* 

This is taken from the Talmudic tractate *Sanhédrin* <note>The section of the Talmud dealing with high courts and criminal law.</note> folio 103, column 1, where the words read thus: <note>original Hebrew: "אמר ר' יוחנן משום ר' שמעון בן יוחי מאי דכתיב וישמע אליו ויחתר לו ויעתר לו מיבעי ליה" — Translation: "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Simeon ben Yohai: What is the meaning of that which is written [in 2 Chronicles 33:13]: 'And He heard him and He tunneled for him'? # The First Chapter of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.

<note>original Hebrew: ליה, מלמד שעשה לו הק"בה כמין מחתרת ברקיע כדי לקבלו בתשובה מפני מדת הדין</note> This means: **Rabbi Jochanan** said in the name of **Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai**: What is the meaning of that which is written in 2 Chronicles 33:13, *vaye'atér lo* <note>original: "ויעתר לו" — and He was entreated by him</note>? It should have said *vaye'atér lo* <note>The author is noting a play on words between 'atar (to entreat) and chatar (to dig)</note>, for *vaye'chatér* <note>original: "ויחתר"</note> means "and a hole was dug for him." From this, the Jews also have a prayer in their large daily Prayer-Book—which they call the "thick **Tephilla**" <note>A colloquial term for a comprehensive Siddur or prayer book.</note>—on folio 37, columns 2 and 3, under the title **Schacharith** (or Shacharis) <note>The morning prayer service.</note>, which reads as follows: <note>original Hebrew: אנא יי' אלהי שמע אל תפלת עבדך ואל תחנוני וקבל את תשובתי ותחנוני ובקשתי ויהיו לפני כסא כבודך מליצי יושר להליץ בעדי לפניך ולהכניס תפלתי באזניך. ואם בעוונותי הרבים אין מליץ בעדי ואין מלמד עלי זכות התור נא לי מחתת כסא כבודך ולא אשוב ריקם מלפניך כי אתה שומע תפלה</note> This is: I beseech you, **Lord my God**, hear the prayer of Your servant and his supplication, and accept my repentance, my prayer, and my request, and let them be right advocates before the **Throne of Your Glory**, to speak for me before You and to make my prayer enter Your ears. But if, because of my many sins, there is no advocate for me, and no one to justify me, then **dig me a hole under the Throne of Your Glory**, and let me not return from You in vain; for You hear prayer.

Upon this God went immediately to her and said to her: why are you so troubled and morose? From this, our Sages learn: for the sake of peace, one may indeed say what is false.

<margin>XI. They teach that God was made ritually impure when he buried Moses.</margin>
Eleventhly, they teach that God was made ritually impure when he buried Moses, and that he washed away such impurity in fire. Concerning this, in the Talmudic tractate *Sanhedrin*, folio 39, column 1, it is written thus:
<note>original Hebrew: אמר ליה ההוא מינא לרבי אבהו אלהיכם כהן הוא דכתיב ויקחו לי תרומה כי קבריה למשה במאי טביל וכי תימא במיא והכתיב מי מדד בשעלו מים אמר ליה בנורא טביל דכתיב כי הנה ה' באש יבא ומי סלקא טבילותא בנורא אמר ליה אדרבה עקר טבילותא בנורא הוא דכתיב כל אשר לא יבא באש תעבירו במים</note> **That is: A certain heretic <note>original: *min*, often referring to early Christians or those outside mainstream Jewish practice</note> said to Rabbi Abhu: "Your God is a priest, for it is written (Exod. 25:2): 'That they may bring me a heave-offering.' Since He buried Moses (and through touching the corpse, according to Num. 19:11, 13, became ritually impure), with what did He wash Himself? If you say with water, is it not written (Isa. 40:12): 'Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand?' (Suggesting He could not have washed Himself entirely in them, because the water is too small.)" Then he answered him: "He washed Himself in fire, as it is written (Isa. 66:15): 'For behold, the Lord will come with fire.'" "What!" (said the heretic), "is a washing performed in fire?" To this, Rabbi Abhu said: "On the contrary, the primary purification is done in fire, as it is written (Num. 31:23): 'Everything that does not pass through the fire (that is, what does not burn but endures it), you shall let pass through the water.'"**

The angels beat the kettledrums (or drums) and danced like women, as it is said (in the same passage, Ezekiel 28:13): "On the day you were created, your drumming and piping had to be ready there with you."**

<margin>God will also dance in the future.</margin> That He will also dance with the Jews in the future is written in the book *Midrash Tillim* <note>A homiletic commentary on the Book of Psalms.</note>, folio 29, column 2, regarding the 48th Psalm: <note>original Hebrew: "עתיד הק"בר לעשות חולה לצדיקים לעתיד לבא..."</note> **In the future, God will arrange a dance for the righteous and dance with them, and they will point to Him with their finger, as it is said (Isaiah 25:9): "Behold, this is our God, for whom we have waited."** This is also found—though with slightly different words—in the Talmudic tractate *Ta'anit* <term>Ta'anit: A volume of the Talmud focusing on fast days and prayers for rain.</term>, folio 31, column 1. Likewise, in the book *Rabboth* (or *Rabbos*) in *Vajikra Rabbah* <note>A Midrashic commentary on the Book of Leviticus.</note>, in the eleventh *Parashah* <term>Parashah: A designated section or chapter of the text.</term> folio 145, column 2, it reads: <note>original Hebrew: "עתיד הק"בה להיות ראש חולה לצדיקים לעתיד לבא..."</note> **In the future, the holy and blessed God will be the leader of the dance for the righteous, and this is what is written (Psalm 48:14): "Set your heart to *lechela*," that is, to her bulwark (or her fortress); but it is written as *lechola*, which means "to the dance."** <note>This is a play on the Hebrew word 'HL', which can be read as 'Cheyl' (fortress) or 'Chol' (dance) depending on the vowels used.</note> In the commentary or explanation of this, which is called *Mattenot Kehunnah* <note>A famous 16th-century commentary on the Midrash Rabbah.</note>, this is explained as follows: <note>original Hebrew: "הוא ילך ויחול בראשם ונהיגם"</note> **He (namely God) will go and dance at their head and lead them.** This same thing is also read in *Shir ha-Shirim Rabbah* <note>Midrash on the Song of Songs.</note> folio 172, column 4, and in *Midrash Kohelet* <note>Midrash on Ecclesiastes.</note> folio 13, column 3.

# Concerning the Jews' Improper Doctrine of GOD the Father. #

<margin>Deuteronomy 32:9.</margin> **"For the LORD's portion is his people."** They <note>The author is referring to Jewish commentators or Kabbalistic authors.</note> wish to say that the souls of the [other] nations are from the outermost powers, the powers of the <term>Kelifoth</term> <note>original: "Kelifoth" or "Kelifós"; in Kabbalistic tradition, these are the "husks" or "shells" that represent the forces of evil or impurity that conceal the divine light.</note> (that is, the shells or rinds, by which the unclean spirits and devils are understood). For this reason, He has distributed them and given them as an inheritance to the upper princes (that is, the devils who rule in the air, as will be demonstrated below in the 18th chapter of this first part). But the souls of the Israelite people flow from the emanation of the blessed God; **"For the Lord's portion is his people,"** His actual portion, His actual children. In the third column or page, however, concerning the words (Genesis 2:7), **"And he breathed into his nostrils the breath of life,"** it is written as follows: <note>original Hebrew: כיון שהק"בה בעצמו ובכבודו נפח באפיו של אדם הראשון נשמת חיים אם כן נשמתו מעצמותו</note> <gloss>that is,</gloss> Because God Himself, in His own person and glory, blew the soul of life into the nostrils of the first man, it follows that his soul is from God's substance or essence. And in that very same column it follows further: <note>original Hebrew: פירוש: למעלה שהנשמה היא חלק אלוה ממעל ומעצמותו כבן מעצמותו של א</note> <gloss>that is,</gloss> We have explained above that the soul is a part of God from above, and of His substance and His essence, just as a son is of the substance and essence of his father.

<margin>How it comes to pass that the damned can endure such great torment.</margin> This is said to be the reason why the damned can endure such terrifyingly great torments, of which one reads in the book *Emek hammelech* <note>The "Valley of the King," a 17th-century work of Lurianic Kabbalah by Naphtali Herz ben Jacob Elhanan.</note>, folio 15, column 3, under the title *Sha'ar tikkune hatteshuvah* <note>The Gate of the Rectifications of Repentance.</note>, in the first chapter, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: אתה בני המעיין בספר זה אל תתמה שיש לרשעים כל כך כח להעונשים האלה הלא או המדרש הנעלם כשם שהק"בה נותן כח בצדיקים לקבל טובתם כך נותן הק"בה כח ברשע לקבל פורענותם וכל זהו מפני שיש בהם ניצוץ קדושה נשמת אלוה ממעל שהיא נצח שנאמר ויפח באפיו נשמת רוח חיים ואז"ל כל הנופח מעצמותו הוא נופח ונאמר כי חלק עמו</note> <gloss>that is,</gloss> You, my son, who are making your contemplations in this book, do not wonder that the godless have such great strength to endure such punishments (of which mention was made previously). Is it not written in the <term>Midrash Neelam</term> <note>The "Hidden Midrash," part of the Zohar, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note> that just as GOD grants the righteous strength to receive their good, so He also gives the godless strength to receive (and endure) their punishment? And all this happens because there is in them a spark of glory, the soul of GOD from above, which is eternal, as is said (Genesis 2:7): **"And he breathed into him the living breath."** Our Rabbis of blessed memory have also said that everyone who blows, blows from his own substance and his own essence. And (Deuteronomy 32:9) it is said: **"The Lord's portion..."**

"Law" refers to the Law, the Prophets, and the Writings; "Statutes" refers to the legal rulings and oral reports; "Judgments" refers to the narratives and additions; and all of these were spoken to Moses at Sinai. <gloss>that is /</gloss> Why is he (the angel Metatron) also called **Segan-fagel**? <note>original: "Segánfagel"; likely a corruption of a title for the angel Metatron as a "Prince" (Segan) or "Deputy."</note> Because all the treasures of wisdom have been placed into his hand / all of which were revealed to **Moses** from the mountain (Sinai) / so that he was instructed therein during the 40 days / while he stood upon the mountain. It follows therefore from this nonsensical teaching of the stubborn Jews / that God taught Moses all sorts of little tales / lies / indeed even shameful obscenities on Mount Sinai / for much of the same is found in the **Talmud** / as will be proven in detail below in the eighth chapter of this first part;

# Chapter I of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked. #

<margin>The Jews are bound to believe the Rabbinic fables as much as the Law of Moses.</margin>be said; which is highly blasphemous to say of God. Notwithstanding this, a Jew is bound and held to give credence to such foolish little tales and gross lies, however absurd they may be, which is clearly to be seen in the book **Menorat Ha-Maor** <note>original: "Menoráth hammáor"; The Candelabrum of Light, a popular 14th-century work on Jewish ethics and ritual by Isaac Aboab</note>, folio 12, column 4, under the title *Ner Sheni, Kelal Rishon, Chelek Sheni*, in the 2nd Chapter, where it is taught thus: <note>original Hebrew: כל מה שאמרו ז"ל במדרשות ובהגדות חייבין אנו להאמין בו כמו בתורת מר"עה וכו׳</note> **"Everything that our Rabbis of blessed memory have said in the Midrashim** <note>original: Medraschóth; these are homiletic or allegorical interpretations of the Hebrew Bible</note> **(including those tales which have been brought forward from the Rabbot) and in the Haggadot** <note>original: Haggadóth; the non-legalistic, narrative, and legendary parts of the Talmud and Midrash</note> **we are bound to believe, just as much as the Law of Moses our Teacher, upon whom be peace. And if something is found therein which appears to us strange or unnatural, we must attribute such a defect to our own meager understanding, and not to their speech. Whoever ridicules any single thing of all that our Rabbis of blessed memory have said shall be punished, as we learn in the Talmudic tractate Eruvin, in the 2nd Chapter, folio 21, column 2, where it is written: Rav Papa says in the name of Rava, the son of Rav Ulla: Everyone who ridicules the words of the Sages is punished in boiling filth (which is said to be a certain place in Hell, as will be shown below in the 8th Chapter of the second part)."**

<margin>How he who ridicules them is punished.</margin>

<margin>Objection that the Haggadot are not to be understood literally.</margin>But someone might object and say that the above-mentioned **Haggadot** are not understood by the Jews according to the letter, or literally as the words sound, but are interpreted otherwise. To this I answer that I well know that various Rabbis have exerted themselves greatly to make these understood in another way, and one has devised and written this interpretation, while another has devised that one, as can be seen in the books **Caphtor Upherach**, **Netzach Yisrael**, **Beer Ha-Golah**, and others. I am also aware that Rabbi **Moshe bar Maimon** <note>also known as Maimonides (1138–1204), one of the most influential Torah scholars of the Middle Ages</note>, in his book **Moreh Nevochim** <note>The Guide for the Perplexed</note>, in the first part, in the 70th Chapter, folio 52, column 2, mentions that the Haggadot are not to be understood according to the letter, where he writes of them thus: <note>original Hebrew: והסתכל איך אלו העניינים המופלאים האמיתיים וכו׳</note> "And observe how these wonderful, true matters, which have reached the contemplation of the most excellent philosophers, are recounted in the Midrashim; when a wise man who does not acknowledge the truth first looks at them, he laughs at them because of what they appear to be in their literal sense: namely, vanity."

<margin>Answer to that.</margin>

## Of the Jews' improper teaching regarding God the Father. ##

<note>original Hebrew: מההבדל מאמתת המציאות ועלת זה כולו דברם בחידות באלה הענינים לרוחם מהבנת ההמון :; "Regarding the deviation from the truth of reality, and the cause of all this is their speaking in riddles in these matters, according to their spirit, away from the understanding of the common folk."</note>

That is: **Consider also how these wonderful and true things, which the most excellent philosophers have reflected upon, are scattered in the <term>Midrashim</term> <note>original: Medraschóth or Medróschos; homiletic and allegorical interpretations of the Hebrew Bible</note> (that is, allegorical interpretations), at which a clever man—who does not acknowledge the truth—laughs right at the beginning of his consideration; for he sees them, according to their literal sense, to be separated from the truth. The entire reason for this is that they (our Sages) have spoken through riddles about such things that the common people cannot grasp.** These are the words of <term>Rabbi Moses bar Maimon</term> <note>also known as Maimonides (1138–1204), one of the most influential Torah scholars and philosophers of the Middle Ages</note>. 

Be that as it may, it is entirely godless and blasphemous that such mocking, belittling, and highly offensive things are reported and taught concerning the most perfect and holy Divine Majesty. No matter how one might wish to explain and interpret them, God is thereby dishonored to the highest degree, and His holy Word is shamefully twisted and perverted, as the examples provided more than sufficiently prove. When one also carefully examines everything brought forward in the aforementioned books to explain the godless teachings of the old Rabbis concerning God, one finds that they are nothing but absurd fantasies. 

Indeed, if one were to teach such unseemly things about God and then try to excuse them by saying they are to be understood *metaphorically* <note>original Latin: metaphoricè; figuratively</note> and *anthropopathically* <note>original Greek: ἀνθρωποπαθῶς; attributing human passions or physical forms to God</note>—just as the Holy Scripture ascribes eyes, hands, and the like to God the Lord in a human way of speaking—then there would be nothing so absurd, so shameful, or so terrifying that it could not be written about God and excused in such a manner.

<margin>Most Jews understand these things literally, and not in an allegorical way.</margin>
Although Rabbi Moses bar Maimon did not understand these things according to the letter, and others who were made wiser by him have wanted them interpreted differently than the words suggest; nevertheless, most Jews believe them literally. Even many among their scholars, who consider themselves very clever and understanding, are of the opinion that everything is to be understood according to the literal meaning the words provide. Concerning this, the aforementioned Rabbi Moses bar Maimon laments in his book, which he called <term>Bábe Móse</term> <note>original: באב מוסר; correctly *Bab al-Mursid* or *Porta Mosis* ("The Gate of Moses"), an influential commentary on the Mishnah</note>, pages 144 and 145. He writes there mostly in the Arabic language using Hebrew characters <note>This is Judeo-Arabic, the common literary language for Sephardic Jews of that era</note> as follows:

<note>original Judeo-Arabic: וממא יגב אן תעלמה אן כלאם החכמים ע"ה אנקסמו אלנאס פיה תלת פרק אלפרקה אלאולי והי אכתר מן ראיתה ומן ראית תואלפה ומן סמעת בה תחמלה עלי טאהרה ולא תתאולה בוגה ותציר ענדהא אלממתנעאת כלהא ואגבה אלוגוד ואנמא פעלוהא דלך לגהלהם</note>
"And of that which you must know, the words of the Sages—peace be upon them—are divided among people into three groups. The first group—and they are the majority of those I have seen, and whose compositions I have seen, and of whom I have heard—take their words according to their literal meaning and do not interpret them allegorically in any way. Thus, things that are impossible become, in their minds, necessary existence; and they have done this only because of their ignorance..."

### Of the First Part of *Judaism Unmasked*, the First Chapter. ###

<note>The following passage is written in Judeo-Arabic—Arabic language using Hebrew characters—and represents the original text of Maimonides being discussed.</note>

...due to their ignorance of the sciences and their distance from various fields of knowledge. They do not possess the perfection required to be alerted [to the truth] by themselves, nor have they found anyone else to alert them. Consequently, they believe that the Sages, in all their wise sayings, intended nothing other than what they [the readers] understand from them, and that these sayings are to be taken literally—even when the literal sense of some of their words is absurd. If a person of sound judgment were to examine these things closely, he would say: "How can there be anyone in the world who imagines such things and considers them a correct opinion?" He would certainly find no reason to praise them. This wretched group is to be pitied for their ignorance, for they believe they are exalting the Sages, when in fact they are lowering them to the lowest depths, though they do not realize it. By God, this group destroys the beauty of religion and darkens its splendor, making the law of God appear contrary to what was intended. For God says in the clear Revelation <note>original: Al-Tanzil; referring to the Torah</note>: "Who shall hear all these statutes, etc." <note>Deuteronomy 4:6</note>. Yet this group recites the literal words of the Sages in such a way that when other nations hear them, they say: "Surely this small nation is a foolish and senseless people." Most who do this are the <term>Darshanim</term> <note>preachers or lecturers who interpret the scriptures</note>, who explain to the people what they themselves do not understand. If only they would remain silent since they do not understand! As it is said: "O that you would altogether hold your peace! And it should be your wisdom" <note>Job 13:5</note>. Or they should say: "We do not know what the Sages intended by this statement."

<margin>
This is testified by **Rabbi Moses bar Maimon**. <note>Also known as Maimonides, the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note>
</margin>

That is: As for what you must necessarily know, it is this: that men, regarding the words of the Sages—upon whom be peace—(with respect to their interpretation) divide themselves into three <term>Sects</term> <note>original: Secten or Rotten; meaning groups or factions</note>. The **first sect** (to which most of those I have seen, whose writings have come before my eyes, or of whom I have heard, belong) consists of those who want the words understood outwardly and according to the letter. They do not interpret them at all, so that all impossible things appear to them as if they were actually present. However, they have done this because they are entirely ignorant in the sciences and removed from the disciplines; they also lack the perfection to admonish themselves, nor have they found anyone who might have admonished them. Thus, they hold that the Sages, in all their clever statements, intended nothing other than what they understand from them, and that these are to be understood according to their outward nature (and proper sense), even though the outward appearance of some of their statements is entirely nonsensical. So much so, that if they were to be closely examined according to what they seem to indicate, one might say: "How can there be anyone in the world who would imagine this and hold it to be a true opinion?" Far be it from him to praise it. The ignorance of this wretched sect is to be lamented; for while they intend to exalt the Sages, they instead cast them down entirely and do not even know it. Indeed, certainly, this faction robs religion of its honor, obscures its brilliance, and twists the Law of God into something entirely contrary to its intent. For when God says in the Law (Deuteronomy 4, verse 6):

v. 14, 15 and Jeremiah 7:26, 17:23, 19:15, Malachi 3:7, and Acts 7:51, as can also be clearly seen in 2 Corinthians 3:14. He was even seized by the priests and false prophets because he showed them that which was commanded of him by God, and they said to him that he must die (Jeremiah 26:7-8). Subsequently, he was again beaten by the princes and placed in prison (Jeremiah 37:15-16) and, because of his prophecy, thrown into the mud <note>This refers to the "miry pit" or cistern where Jeremiah was imprisoned</note>, and the princes wanted him to be put to death (Jeremiah 38:2-4, 6). The Prophet Micah was struck on the cheek because he had advised King Ahab against going to Ramoth in Gilead (1 Kings 22:24). Amos was regarded as a rebel when he prophesied against King Jeroboam (Amos 7:10). One of the disciples of the prophets, who was sent by the Prophet Elisha to Jehu, was called a madman (2 Kings 9:11).

<margin>Yes, even killed.</margin>
Indeed, they put many of them to death, for Uriah was killed because he prophesied against Jerusalem (Jeremiah 26:20, 23). They stoned Zechariah because he exhorted the people in Jerusalem to return to God (2 Chronicles 24:19-21). Likewise, many other prophets have also come to lose their lives (1 Kings 18:4, 13; Matthew 23:34, 37; and Luke 13:34).

<margin>In this way, and even worse, they treated Christ.</margin>
In just such a manner—indeed much worse—the obdurate <term>meaning stubborn or hardened in heart</term> godless Jews treated the Son of God, our most precious Savior Jesus Christ, the highest Prophet and Teacher. For when He, in the fullness of time, took upon Himself human nature to complete the work of redemption and wished to lead them out of the spiritual Egypt and the power of the hellish Pharaoh, and also wanted to show them the way to the heavenly Canaan through His faithful exhortations and instructions in the divine Word and will—alongside zealous punishment of all the sins that were then prevalent <note>original: "im Schwang gegangen"</note>—they became His bitter enemies. The Pharisees and scribes grumbled against Him because He received sinners (Luke 15:2). Others who followed Him also grumbled that He had stayed with a sinner (Luke 19:7).

## Chapter II of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.

<margin>What the purpose of this chapter consists of.</margin> In this chapter, all the mocking names which the godless Jews give to Christ the Lord shall be shown; thereby, many terrible blasphemies against the same dear Christendom will simultaneously be revealed. If they only called him *Notzeri* <note>original: נוצרי</note> or *Ha-Notzeri* <note>original: הנוצרי</note>, that is, the <term>Nazarene</term> <note>A title derived from Jesus's hometown of Nazareth</note>, or *Yeshua Ha-Notzeri* <note>original: ישוע הנוצרי</note>, that is, Jesus the Nazarene, as happens in several of their books, we would have no reason to complain about them; for he himself is called a <term>Nazarene</term> <note>original Latin: Nazarenus</note> in Matthew 2:23, and in Matthew 21:11, Mark 1:24, Acts 2:22, and in many other places, he is called Jesus of Nazareth. However, they give him many other, and indeed shameful, names, and call him:

<margin>Christ is called Jeschu or Jischu, and the reason for this is shown.</margin> Firstly, *Jeschu* <note>original: ישו</note> or *Jischu*. In the Hebrew language, Jesus is called *Yeshua* <note>original: ישוע</note>, that is, a Savior and Redeemer; but the godless Jews leave out the last letter, the <term>Ayin</term> <note>The 16th letter of the Hebrew alphabet, 'ע'</note>, and maliciously call him *Jeschu*, or rather *Jischu*, which they do for five reasons.

<margin>The first reason.</margin> The first reason is reported by Rabbi Elias <note>Elijah Levita, a famous 16th-century Hebrew scholar</note> in his *Tishbi* <note>A dictionary of Talmudic Hebrew</note>, under the word *Jeschu*, with these words: <note>original Hebrew: לפי שהיהודים אינם מודים שהוא היה המושיע לפיכך אינם רוצים לקראו ישוע והפילו העין וקורין לו ישו</note> "Because the Jews do not admit that he was the Savior and Redeemer (namely, the promised Messiah), they therefore do not want to call him *Yeshua*, but rather they drop the letter *Ayin* and call him *Jeschu*."

<margin>The second reason.</margin> The second reason is indicated by Rabbi Abraham Perizol <note>Abraham Farissol, a 15th-century scholar and polemicist</note> in his book *Maggen Abraham* [The Shield of Abraham], in the 59th chapter, where he writes thus: <note>original Hebrew: היה שמו ישוע כמו שכתב הרמ"בם ז"ל בהלכות תשובה ובהלכות מלכים ואע"פ שבכל התלמוד לא נמצא אלא ישו שמא בכוונה חיסרו העין כיון שלא הושיע את עצמו</note> "His name was *Yeshua*, as Rabbi Moses, the son of Maimon <note>Maimonides, the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in his [book] *Jad Chasaka* [The Strong Hand] or *Mishneh Torah* in the tractate on Repentance, as well as in the tractate on Kings; although in the entire Talmud only *Jeschu* is found. However, they perhaps intentionally omitted the letter *Ayin* because he did not save himself (from the hands and power of his enemies)."

<margin>The third reason. It is permitted to mock false gods.</margin> The third reason is because they are not only allowed to mock the false gods (which they consider Christ to be), but are even commanded to change their names and call them shameful things. That it is permitted for them to mock false gods is taught by the Talmud in the tractate *Megilla*, folio 25, column 2, with these words: <note>original Hebrew/Aramaic: כל ליצנותא אסירא בר מליצנותא דעבודה</note> "All mockery is forbidden, except for mockery of foreign worship [idolatry]."

Likewise, regarding the name *Marcolis* (the idol Mercury), it was called *Killus* by those who served it, which is a word of praise and honor; but our Rabbis of blessed memory changed it to the name *Marcolis*, where *Mar* is a term for substitution and change. Thus they have changed *Killus* (which is called praise) into *Kolis*, which signifies mockery and disgrace.** This is also read in the Talmudic tractate *Bava Metzia* (or *Bovo Mezio*), folio 25, column 2, in the *Tosafot* <note>Supplemental commentaries on the Talmud</note> regarding the word *Marcolis*. From this, it can be clearly seen that the godless villain, Rabbi Salman Zevi, in his little book filled with lies, the aforementioned *Jewish Theriac*—which he wrote against the book of the convert Samuel Friedrich Brenz, titled *The Jewish Stripped-off Snake-skin*—reported in the first chapter, number 2, against his better knowledge and conscience, that it means nothing wrong when our Savior is called *Jeschu* by the Jews. And that, on the contrary, the convert Ferdinand Heß, in the third part, chapter 3 of his *Jewish Scourge*, shows the pure truth when he says: "When they (the Jews) are among others, they may call our Savior *Jeschu*, but they always say these two words along with it: *jimmach schemó*, that is, **May his name be blotted out.**"

This blasphemy was also uncovered and revealed in truth to Christendom by the convert Dieterich Schwabe in his *Jewish Cloak*, second part, chapter 14, page 141; by Anthonius Margarita <note>a Jewish convert to Christianity who wrote an influential critique of Jewish practice in 1530</note> in his little book called *The Whole Jewish Faith*, page 309; and by the baptized Johann Adrian in his *Epistle of Sending and Warning*, page 29. # On the Shameful Names that the Jews Give to Christ.

<sig>I 2</sig>

already mentioned Kabbalistic method, which is called <term>Notaricon</term> <note>a system of creating acronyms from the first letters of words</note>, stands for three entire words, namely *jimmach shemó vezikhronó* <note>original Hebrew: ימח שמו וזכרו</note>, that is, **May his name and memory be blotted out.** For this reason, in the blasphemous little book <term>Toledoth Jeschu</term> <note>The "History of Jesus," a medieval Jewish work that parodies the Gospel narrative; Eisenmenger attributes its content to the Devil</note>, on page 6, it is read: *Vayikre’u shemó Yeshu, ráshe tevot yimmach shemó vezikhronó* <note>original Hebrew: ויקראו שמו יש"ו ראשי תיבות ימח שמו וזכרו</note>, that is: "And they (those in the High Council at Jerusalem) called him *Yeshu*, which are the first letters of the three words *yimmach shemó vezikhronó*," that is (as already mentioned): **May his name and memory be blotted out.** The very same is also found in the written manuscripts of Rabbi Moshe bar Maimon’s <note>known as Maimonides, a preeminent medieval Jewish scholar</note> book *Yad Chazakah* <note>The "Strong Hand," a code of Jewish law</note>, in the treatise on Kings, in the eleventh chapter—which has been omitted from the printed editions out of fear of the Christians. <margin>Jeschu or Jischu means: May his name and memory be blotted out.</margin>

From this, it is clearly to be seen that the godless villain, Rabbi Salman Zevi, in his booklet filled with lies, the aforementioned *Jewish Theriac*—which he wrote against the book of the convert Samuel Friedrich Brenz, titled *The Jewish Sloughed-Off Snake Skin*—reports in the first chapter, number 2, against his better knowledge and conscience, that it means nothing wrong when our Savior is called *Yeshu* by the Jews. And that, on the contrary, the convert Ferdinand Heß, in the third part, chapter 3, of his *Jewish Scourge*, displays the pure truth when he says: "When they (the Jews) are among others, they indeed call our Savior *Yeshu*, but they always say these two words alongside it: *yimmach shemó* <note>original Hebrew: ימח שמו</note>, that is, **May his name be blotted out.**" This blasphemy was also uncovered and truthfully revealed to Christendom by the convert Dieterich Schwabe in his *Jewish Mask*, in the second part, chapter 14, page 141; by Anthonius Margarita in his booklet called *The Entire Jewish Faith*, page 309; and by the baptized Johann Adrian in his *Epistle and Warning Letter*, page 29. ## Chapter II of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.

GOD and an abomination: which is not to be wondered at, because they consider him to be a false god, and both the word *Schéker* <note>original: שקר (Sheker), meaning a lie or falsehood</note> and *Toéfa* <note>original: תועבה (To’evah), meaning abomination</note> sometimes signify an idol. Just as the word *Schéker* is taken in this sense in Rabbi Jacob Phidánki’s <note>Jacob Fidanque, a 17th-century scholar</note> explanation of Abarbenel’s <note>Isaac Abarbanel, a famous 15th-century statesman and philosopher</note> commentary or interpretation of the Second Book of Kings, on folio 66, column 2, where he writes as follows: *Avodah zarah hu sheker kemo she-emar vayomeru ach sheker nichalu avoteinu* <note>original Hebrew: עבודה זרה הוא שקר כמ"ש ויאמרו אך שקר נחלו אבותינו</note>; that is: **An idol is called *Schéker*, as the Scripture (Jeremiah 16:19) reports: "And they shall say, our fathers have had (Schéker, that is) false gods."** The word *Toéfa*, however, which properly signifies an abomination and a loathsome thing (Deuteronomy 32:16, Isaiah 44:19, Ezekiel 11:21, and other places), also means a false god which one should abhor. Therefore, in the little book *Othioth* (or *Ofios*) *Rabbi Akkiva* <note>The "Letters of Rabbi Akiva," an ancient midrashic text on the Hebrew alphabet</note>, on folio 16, column 3, it is read: *Ein to’evah ela avodah zarah shen-emar lo tavi to’evah el beitecha* <note>original Hebrew: אין תועבה אלא עבודה זרה שנ' לא תביא תועבה אל ביתך</note>; that is: **The word *Toéfa* signifies nothing other than an idol, as is said (Deuteronomy 7:26): "You shall not bring any *Toéfa* (that is, any abomination or idol) into your house."**

<margin>The Jews more often call Christ *Jishu* than *Jéschu*.</margin>
To return, however, to the previous words, *jimmach schemó vesichronó* <note>May his name and memory be blotted out</note>: the Jews do not readily say *Jéschu* <note>Yeshua/Jesus</note>, but for the most part—as I have often heard myself, indeed, among them whenever they mention Christ—they always say <term>Jishu</term> <note>ישו</note>, so that the "j" <note>the Hebrew letter Yod</note> in the word *jimmach* may be clearly understood thereby. This was also indicated by the aforementioned author in the place cited above. Therefore, in the *Sépher amanáh* (or *amunóh*) <note>The "Book of Faith"</note>, page 24, number 14, it is read: *Chachameinu kor’in oto bileshon katzar derech bizayon veketzef rotzeh lomar Jishu* <note>original Hebrew: חכמינו קוראין אותו בלשון קצר דורך בזיון וקצף ר"ל ישו</note>; that is: **Our sages call him by a shortened name (namely without the letter Ayin) in a contemptuous and angry manner, that is, *Jishu*, so that they may blaspheme and curse him.**

<margin>The Jews are commanded to curse the godless.</margin>
Now, if someone should ask whether such cursing is permitted to them? I give the answer that it is certainly not only allowed but even commanded, as is read in the book *Médrasch Schmúel* <note>Midrash on the Book of Samuel</note> folio 50, column 1, and in the *Jalkut Schimóni* <note>A major medieval anthology of midrashic interpretations</note> on the five books of Moses, folio 24, column 2, number 82, as well as in <term>Bereshíth rábba</term> <note>Genesis Rabbah, a collection of ancient rabbinical homilies on Genesis</note>, folio 44, column 1, at the beginning of the forty-ninth *Parascha* <note>a weekly section of the Torah</note>: *Kol hamazkir rasha ve’eino mekallelo over be’aseh shen-emar veshem resha’im yirkav* <note>original Hebrew: כל המזכיר רשע ואינו מקללו עובר בעשה שנ' ושם רשעים ירקב</note>; that is: **Whoever mentions a godless person and does not curse him transgresses a positive commandment, as is said (Proverbs 10:7): "The name of the godless must rot."** On the other hand, it is also read in the same place: *Kol mi shehu mazkir tzaddik ve’eino mevarecho over be’aseh dechetiv zecher tzaddik livrachah* <note>original Hebrew: כל מי שהוא מזכיר צדיק ואינו מברכו עובר בעשה דכתיב זכר צדיק לברכה</note>; that is: **Whoever mentions a righteous person and does not bless him transgresses a positive commandment, as is (also Proverbs 10:7) written: "The memory of the righteous..."**

<margin>Formulas of the Jews, how they are accustomed to curse those whom they hate. The first formula of cursing.</margin>
Since the Jewish practice of cursing is mentioned here, I do not consider it unnecessary to indicate what formulas the Jews have for cursing those whom they hate; and it should be known that there are five of them. The first consists of the words already mentioned from Proverbs 10:7, **The name of the wicked must rot**; the use of this against the godless is commanded in the Talmudic tractate *Taanith*, folio 28, column 1. In this manner, some are cursed in the *Yalkut Shimoni* <note>A medieval midrashic compilation on the Hebrew Bible</note> regarding the Proverbs of Solomon, folio 136, column 3, number 946, where it follows: *Mai ve-shem resha'im yirqav? <margin>The second curse formula.</margin>
The second curse formula is contained in the aforementioned words *jimmach sche-mó* <note>original Hebrew: ימח שמו</note>, which they often use against Christians, as Ferdinand Heß reports in the first part, fourth chapter of his book *The Jews' Scourge*. <margin>The third curse formula.</margin>
The third curse formula is called, when speaking of only one person, *tippach rúcho* <note>original Hebrew: תיפח רוחו</note>, that is, **May his spirit burst or shatter.** But when two or more are mentioned, it is *tippach rúchan* <note>original Hebrew: תיפח רוחן</note>, that is, **May their spirit burst.** In the *Book of Genealogies* <note>original Hebrew: "Sépker júchasin"</note>, folio 158, column 1, where the author mentions King Herod with praise, this curse is used against the Emperor Titus Vespasianus, where the words read as follows: <note>Eisenmenger provides a long Hebrew passage here concerning Herod's reign and Titus's destruction of the Temple</note> that is, **He (Herod) was also a brave hero and successful in his reign; he waged war against all his enemies, and Israel found rest in his days. He also renewed the structure of the Temple for honor and glory, and his sons and grandsons reigned after him for a long time, until the Temple was devastated by the godless Titus—may his spirit burst and his soul be in Hell.** Against those who search for the time of the Messiah, or when he shall come, it is written in the book *City of Heroes* <note>original Hebrew: "Ir gibbórim"</note>, folio 28, column 1, number 54: <note>original Hebrew: אסור לחקור ולדרוש אחר ביאת הגואל כא"ל תיפח רוחן של מחשבי קצין</note> that is, **It is forbidden to investigate and search for the coming of the Redeemer; as our Rabbis of blessed memory have said: May the spirit of those who calculate the end burst.** This is also found in the previously mentioned book *The Fiery Darts of Satan*, in the *Old Victory* <note>original Hebrew: "Nizzáchon"</note>, page 46, regarding the words of Numbers 17:23.

# Of the shameful names which the Jews give to Christ.

...he [writes], following others on Numbers 17:8 <note>Eisenmenger cites verse 8, though in English Bibles the account of Aaron's rod is in Numbers 17:8</note>, "And behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi had sprouted": <note>original Hebrew: אומרים המינים שזה רמז על חריא ר"ל מריה שהיתה בתולה כשילדה את ישו תיפח רוחם כי טח מראות עיניו</note> that is: "The heretics (namely the Christians) say that these words refer to *Charja*—I mean Mary—claiming she was a virgin when she gave birth to Jesus. <margin>The fifth curse formula.</margin>

With the words *Schechik timmája*, the Emperor Hadrian is cursed in the *Great Midrash* <note>original Hebrew: "Rabboth"</note> on Genesis <note>original Hebrew: "Bereshith" or "Bereshis rabba," in the 78th section, folio 70, column 3</note>, where it is written: <note>original Hebrew: אדרינוס שחיק טמיא שאל את רבי יהושע בן חנינה אמר ליה אתם אומרים אין כת של מעלה מקלסת ושונה אלא בכל יום ויום הק"ב בורא כת של מלאכים חדשים והן אומרין שירה לפניו והולכין להן</note> That is: "Hadrian, may his bones be crushed, asked Rabbi Joshua ben Hananiah, saying to him: 'You say that the heavenly host does not praise and repeat [the song], but that every single day the Holy One, blessed be He, creates a new host of angels who sing a song before Him and then pass away...'"

## Chapter II of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked

...the son of Channina <note>Likely Rabbi Hanina ben Teradyon, a scholar often depicted in dialogues with Roman authorities.</note>, and spoke to him: "You say that up there (in heaven) no host (of angels) praises (God) twice, but rather the holy and blessed God creates a host of new angels every day, who sing before Him and then perish again," etc. The same can also be found in the book *Pesikta Rabbati* <note>A collection of midrashic homilies</note>, folio 36, column 1. With the words *Shechak Atzamot* (or *atzomos*) <note>original Hebrew: שחיק עצמות; literally "may his bones be ground to dust"</note>, however, the Emperor Hadrian is also cursed in *Bereishit Rabbah* <note>The Great Midrash on Genesis</note>, folio 70, column 3, in the seventy-eighth *parashah* (section), as well as in *Eicha Rabbati* (The Great Midrash on Lamentations), folio 306, column 2, and King Nebuchadnezzar is cursed in the *Midrash Megillah*. Instead of these, however, in the *Sefer Yuchasin* (Book of Lineage), folio 131, column 2, as well as in the booklet *Kabbalah* (or *Kabbolos*) of the *Ravad* <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David</note>, folio 78, column 1, against a Jew named Abulpharag <note>A Jewish convert to another faith or a sectarian leader</note>, who was placed under the ban as a heretic, the words <note>original Hebrew: ישתחקו עצמותיו בגיהנם</note> *yishthachaku atzmotav* (or *atzmosav*) *be-gehinnom* are read, which mean: **May his bones be crushed in Hell.** These words are also reported from another source in the book *Nishmat Chayim* (The Breath of Life), folio 89, column 2, in the 27th chapter of the second *ma'amar* (treatise). That the bones of the godless shall be crushed in Hell is discussed in the book *Nishmat Chayim*, folio 32, column 2, in the 12th chapter of the first treatise, regarding the words of Ezekiel 32, verse 27: **"Shall they not lie with the mighty that are fallen of the uncircumcised?"** etc. <margin>The bones of the godless shall be crushed in Hell.</margin> "Their iniquity is upon their bones," it is read thus: <note>original Hebrew: ראה איך אחר מיתתם אומר שעדין חטאתם ועונשם תהיה על עצמותם שישתחקו בגיהנם</note> that is: **"See how he (namely the Prophet) says that after their death (the uncircumcised), their sin and their punishment shall also come upon their bones, in that they shall be crushed in Hell."**

<margin>How, on the other hand, the Jews are accustomed to bless someone and wish them well.</margin>

On the other hand, however, when they wish someone well, they say after mentioning their name: <note>original Hebrew: זכרונו לברכה</note> *Zichrono livracha* (or *livrocho*), that is, **May his memory be for a blessing, or be blessed:** Or they say <note>original Hebrew: זכור לטוב</note> *Zachur letov*, that is, **Whose memory is for good:** Or they speak <note>original Hebrew: זכרונו לחיי העולם הבא</note> *Zichrono le-chaye ha-olam haba*, that is, **May his memory be for the life of the world to come (that is, for eternal life):** Or they say <note>original Hebrew: זכר צדיק לברכה</note> *Zecher Tzaddik livracha* (or *livrocho*), that is, **The memory of the righteous be for a blessing (that is, blessed):** Or they speak <note>original Hebrew: עליו השלום</note> *alav hashalom*, that is, **Upon whom be peace:** Or they also say <note>original Hebrew: נוחו עדן</note> *Nucho Eden*, that is, **May his rest be Paradise;** OR <note>original Hebrew: נשמתו עדן</note> *Nishmatho* (or *Nishmoso*) *Eden*, that is, **May his soul be** <note>The text cuts off here, continuing with the catchword "be" on the next page.</note>

# Concerning the shameful names which the Jews give to Christ.
<sig>K</sig>
<meta>catchword: this</meta>

...be in Paradise; or <note>original Hebrew: נוחו תהא בגן עדן, nuchato tehe be-gan eden</note> **May his rest be in the Garden of Eden:** or also <note>original Hebrew: נפשו תהיה בגן עדן, nafsho tihyeh be-gan eden</note> **May his soul be in the Garden of Eden/** as can be seen here and there in their books.

<margin>II. Christ is called the God of the uncircumcised.</margin>
**Secondly**, Christ is called <note>original Hebrew: אלהי הערלים, Elohe ha-arelim</note> **the God of the uncircumcised**, and by the "uncircumcised," the Christians are understood, as will be proven below in the 16th chapter of this first part. This is read, however, in Rabbi Aben Ezra's <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167), a celebrated Spanish rabbi, philosopher, and biblical commentator.</note> commentary on the words of the prophet Daniel, chapter 11, verse 14: **"Also some rebels (or breakers-through) from your people shall rise up"/** where he writes as follows: <note>original Hebrew: אלה היו בימי אדם שהוא אלוהי הערלים</note> **These (rebels or breakers-through) existed in the time of that man who is the God of the uncircumcised.** By the "breakers-through," however, he understands the holy Apostles, as will be proven in the 7th chapter of this first part.

<margin>III. He is called the God of Edom.</margin>
**Thirdly**, he is called <note>original Hebrew: אלהי אדום, Elohe Edom</note> **the God of Edom** or the **Edomite God**, as can be seen in Abarbanel's <note>Isaac Abarbanel (1437–1508), a Portuguese Jewish statesman and theologian who wrote extensively on the messiah.</note> commentary or explanation on Isaiah 34:9, folio 53, column 2, where he mentions the destruction of the city of Rome (which he understands as Bozrah, the former capital city of Edom) and writes: <note>original Hebrew: במקום שבצרה היא רומי היתה קדושת אלהי אדום ועצביהם תהיה עתה מקום שדים ורוחות</note> **Instead of Bozrah—that is, Rome—being the sanctuary of the Edomite God and their idols, it will now become a place for demons and impure spirits.** The same can be seen in the book *Mashmia Yeshuah* <note>meaning "The Proclaimer of Salvation," a work by Abarbanel focused on messianic prophecies.</note>, folio 18, column 1. By "Edom," however, Christendom is understood, as can be read extensively below in the 18th chapter of this first part.

<margin>IV. He is called a foreign God.</margin>
**Fourthly**, they call him <note>original Hebrew: אלהי נכר, Elohe nechar</note> **a foreign god.** This is read in the little book *Avkat Rochel* <note>meaning "The Merchant's Powder," a work containing Jewish legends about the end of the world.</note> at the end of the third part, where, through a Kabbalistic method called <term>Gematria|A system of interpretation that calculates the numerical value of Hebrew letters to find hidden meanings or connections between words.</term>, it is foolishly attempted to prove that Christ is a foreign god; there it is written: <note>original Hebrew: אלהי נכר בגימטריא ישו, Elohe nechar begemátria Yeshu</note> **The words "Elohe nechar" (foreign god) amount to the same as "Yeshu" (Jesus) through Gematria—namely, 316.** For "Elohe nechar" makes 316, and "Yeshu" makes just as much. So too writes Abarbanel in his book *Ma'yene ha-Yeshu'ah* <note>meaning "Fountains of Salvation," a commentary on the Book of Daniel.</note>, folio 75, column 4, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: אמרו בעלי גימטריאות שרמזו באמרו אלהי נכר הארץ אמונת ישו ומרים שאלהי נכר עולה בגימטריא ישו והארץ מרים ודבריהם אמת</note> **Those who understand Gematria say that through the words (Deuteronomy 31:16) "Elohe nechar ha-aretz"—that is, foreign gods of the land—the faith in Jesus and Mary is signified...**

# Chapter 1 of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.
<sig>K</sig>
<meta>catchword: because</meta>

...since <note>original Hebrew: אלהי נכר, Elohé néchar</note> **foreign gods** amounts to as much as **Jesus** (namely, 316) and <note>original Hebrew: הארץ, haá-rez</note> **the land** makes as much as **Mary** (namely, 296) in number; and they consider these words to be true.

<margin>The Jewish proof through Gematria is foolish and invalid.</margin>
It is indeed not to be denied that false gods are called <term>Elohé néchar <gloss>foreign gods</gloss></term> in Holy Scripture, as can be seen in Genesis 35:2, Joshua 24:20, Jeremiah 5:19, and many other places; however, Jesus is not a "foreign" but a true God, as will be proven in what follows. But as for the proof through <term>Gematria <gloss>a Kabbalistic method of interpreting the Hebrew Bible by calculating the numerical value of words</gloss></term>, the foolish Jews are often accustomed to bringing something forward in such a manner; however, the same is entirely inconsistent and ridiculous, which shall be confirmed here with only a few examples. In the book *Yalkut Chadash* <note>A 17th-century collection of Jewish homiletic and mystical teachings</note> it is written on page 140, column 2, 3, number 313, under the title *Moshe*, from the book *Megalleh Amukoth* <note>Meaning "Revealer of Depths," a famous Kabbalistic work by Nathan Nata Spira</note> page 14, column 4: **"Moses was ordained from the creation of the world to receive the Law, and that is what the Scripture (Genesis 1:4) says: 'And God saw <note>original Hebrew: את האור, eth ha-or</note> the light,' that is, the light; for 'the light' makes as much in number through Gematria as <note>original Hebrew: משה רבינו, Moshe Rabbenu</note> Moses our teacher (namely, 613), which number contains the 613 commandments. And the word 'Moshe' [Moses] makes just as much when it is written out in its full form: Mem, Shin, He."** In the aforementioned *Yalkut Chadash*, it is further stated on page 128, column 2, number 47, under the title *Shabbat* as follows: **"On the evening of the Sabbath, when the Bride (that is, the Sabbath, which is called a Bride by the Jews) arrived, the wedding feast of Leah was held; for Jacob was married to her on Sabbath evening. This is signified by the word <note>original Hebrew: משתה, mishteh</note> 'feast' (which means a meal), because through Gematria it makes as much in number as <note>original Hebrew: שבת גדול, Shabbat Gadol</note> the Great Sabbath (namely, 745)."** Such foolish proofs are also found in the Talmud, in its tractate *Yoma*, page 76, column 1, where it is written: **"The cup of David in the world to come holds two hundred and twenty-one measures, as it is said (Psalm 23:5): 'My cup <note>original Hebrew: רויה, revayah</note> is full [overflowing]'; for the word 'revayah' makes that much (namely, 221) through Gematria."** Are these not great weaknesses, that one [brings forward] such foolish...

# On the shameful names that the Jews give to Christ.
<sig>K 2</sig>
<meta>catchword: is</meta>

<margin>Aben Ezra rejects such a proof.</margin>...can a proof be brought forth, at which every person who has sound reason must justly laugh? For this reason, Rabbi Aben Ezra <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167) was a distinguished Spanish Jewish scholar, poet, and biblical commentator known for his rationalist approach.</note> also rejects them quite rightly in his commentary on Daniel 11:31, where he writes as follows: <note>original Hebrew: המלות או האותיות בחשבון גימטריא הכל הבל ורעות רוח</note> that is, **"All those who calculate words or letters through Gematria according to numbers are doing a vain thing that plagues the spirit."** <note>This is a play on the phrase "vanity and vexation of spirit" from Ecclesiastes.</note>

However, if the Jews wish to believe that this manner of proving something is valid, then it is easily demonstrated to them that JESUS Christ is the true promised Messiah—and not a stranger, but the eternal God. For in the book *Zerór hammór* <note>meaning "A Bundle of Myrrh," a popular 15th-century Torah commentary by Abraham Saba</note> it is written on folio 37, column 2, in the portion *Vajéze*, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: מלת משיח עולה במנין ש"נה וכו' כלול ש"לה שהוא עולה ה"שם</note> that is, **"The word <term>Mashiach <gloss>Messiah</gloss></term> amounts to the number 358, and within it is contained the word <term>Shiloh <gloss>a title from Genesis 49:10 interpreted as the Messiah</gloss></term>, which amounts to the same number as <term>HaShem <gloss>literally 'The Name,' used by Jews to refer to God</gloss></term> (which among the Rabbis also signifies God, namely 345)."** In such a way, it could also be claimed that by the aforementioned word *Shiloh* in Genesis 49:10, Jesus is to be understood, because the words <note>original Hebrew: עד כי יבא שילה</note> *ad ki javo Shiloh*, that is, **"until the Shiloh or the Hero comes,"** amount to exactly the same number as <note>original Hebrew: ישוע בן דוד</note> *Jeschúa ben David*, that is, **"Jesus the son of David,"** namely 462. Furthermore, the words in Isaiah 9:6, <note>original Hebrew: פלא יועץ אל גבור</note> *Pele, joëz, El gibbor*, that is, **"Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God,"** signify JESUS Christ because they have the same number (as the words <note>original Hebrew: ישוע בן אלהים</note> *Jeschúa ben Elohim*, that is, **"Jesus, the Son of God"**), which consists of 529. Likewise, the words in Psalm 72:17, <note>original Hebrew: ינון שמו</note> *Jinnon Schemó*, that is, **"His name shall be continued from child to child,"** point to Christ, because their number, namely 462, matches the number of the aforementioned words *Jeschúa ben David*, that is, **"Jesus the son of David."** Many more such examples could be set down here against the Jews. But just as they do not accept these as binding and irrefutable, so too should their proofs, which they bring forth in such a manner against the Christian religion, be held in little regard.

<margin>Christ is called Taüth, that is, an idol.</margin>Fifthly, they call Christ <term>Taüth <gloss>or Toüs</gloss></term>, that is, an idol. This word comes from <term>taáh <gloss>a Hebrew root</gloss></term>, which in the Hebrew language means **"to err,"** and additionally in the Chaldean <note>referring to Aramaic, the common language of the Talmud</note> language means **"to commit adultery"** and **"to forget,"** and an idol or false god is called *Taüth* because he who serves it errs, commits spiritual adultery, and forgets the true God. Because they now [call] Christ [this], despite Him being the Lord from heaven, as in 1 Corinthians 15:47...

Jeschúa ben David: Hebrew for Jesus, son of David. Taüth: A Hebrew/Aramaic term meaning error, straying, or an idol. Abgott: German for "idol" or "false god." <meta>catchword: matter</meta>

to be seen / and **has created heaven and earth**, as is to be read in John 1:3 and Hebrews 1:2 / [they] hold him for a false **God** / so they also give him this mocking name / as can be seen in the commentary of Rabbi Salomon Jarchi <note>Commonly known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval French commentator on the Torah and Talmud.</note> on Isaiah 9:7 (which verse we interpret as referring to our Savior and Redeemer /) according to the evidence of the Bible printed in Venice in the year 285—that is, by our count, 1525—in folio, with the commentaries of several Rabbis / where he writes thus: <note>original Hebrew: ולתשובת המינים האומרים שם לטעותם יש להשיבם מהו מעתה הלא לא בא אותו טעות עד לסוף שלש מאות שנה</note> that is, **"But to the heretics / who interpret these words as referring to their <term>Ta’ut <gloss>error or idol</gloss></term> (that is, JESUS), one must answer: did that same <term>Ta’ut <gloss>idol</gloss></term> not first come at the end of 300 years?"** Likewise, in the little book *Rosch amana* (or *amono*) <note>*Rosh Amanah* (The Pinnacle of Faith) by Isaac Abarbanel, a 15th-century work on the Jewish articles of faith.</note> folio 15, column 1, it is read concerning the Christians: <note>original Hebrew: כל עוד שיאמינו בטעותם ובאמונה הכוזבת הם מינים וכופרים ואין להם חלק לעולם הבא</note> that is, **"As long as they believe in their <term>Ta’ut <gloss>idol</gloss></term> and persist in that false faith / they are heretics and deniers of God / and have no portion in the world to come / that is, in eternal life."**

<margin>VI. He is called Jirah, which is also an idol.</margin>
**Sixthly**, they call him יראה <term>Jirah <gloss>fear or awe</gloss></term> (or *Jiroh*), which word properly means a "fear," but improperly signifies an "idol" / which is honored and feared in an unbecoming manner: And thus it is used in the *Jalkut Schimoni* <note>A major medieval midrashic anthology on the Hebrew Bible.</note> on the Psalms, folio 127, column 3, number 879, where it is read: <note>original Hebrew: אומות העולם עושים יראתם של כסף ושל זהב</note> **"The nations of the world make their <term>Jirah <gloss>idol</gloss></term> out of gold and silver."** So it also stands in Rabbi Moshe bar Maimon’s <note>Maimonides (1138–1204), one of the most influential Torah scholars of the Middle Ages.</note> *Sepher Mizvoth* (or *Mizvos*) <note>The "Book of Commandments."</note> folio 82, column 4, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: לא תשביעו הגוי ביראתו והוא אמרו יתעלה ושם אלהים אחרים לא תזכירו</note> that is, **"You shall not let a heathen swear by his <term>Jirah <gloss>idol</gloss></term>, and that is what the praised God (Exodus 23:13) says: You shall not mention the names of other gods."** In the same way, the word <term>Jirah <gloss>object of fear</gloss></term> is used in the aforementioned Rabbi Moshe bar Maimon’s book *Jad chasaka* (or *chasoko*) <note>The *Mishneh Torah*, Maimonides’ code of Jewish law.</note> in the first part, in the treatise on Idolatry, chapter 5, number 10, and in the Talmud, in the treatise *Sanhedrin*, folio 63, column 2. But the blinded Jews call Christ thus because we / according to their erroneous opinion / honor him in an idolatrous way and fear him as a **God**. Therefore, Rabbi Bechai <note>Bahya ben Asher (1255–1340), a Spanish rabbi and biblical commentator.</note> writes in his book *Cad hakkemach* <note>"The Jar of Flour," a work on ethics and philosophy.</note> folio 34, column 2 and 3, and in his commentary on the 5 Books of Moses, folio 195, column 1, in the portion *Va’etchanan*, on the words of Deuteronomy 6:4, **"Hear, O Israel, the LORD our God is one LORD,"** as follows: <note>original Hebrew: אילו אמר שמע ישראל יי' אחד היה פתחון פה לאומות העולם לומר שעל יראתם אומר הכתוב כן שהוא לדעתם</note> i.e., **"If (namely Moses) had said: Hear, O Israel, the Lord is one / then the nations of the world (the Christians) would have cause..."**

# Of the shameful names / that the Jews give to Christ.
->K 3<-
<meta>catchword: tere-sache (matter/case)</meta>

[they] are able to take occasion to say / that the Scripture speaks of their <term>Yirah <gloss>object of fear or worship</gloss></term>, that is / their idol / which according to their opinion / is called Jehovah or Lord. Thus also in the **Book of Victory** (*Sepher Nizzáchon*) by Rabbi Lipmann, page 151, number 276, concerning the words of Psalm 34:9, **"Taste / and see / how friendly the Lord is /"** it is written thus: <note>original Hebrew: כאן דברו הנוצרים דברים שאי אפשר לשמוע ופרשו טעמו לשון אכילה ואומרים שאוכלים יראתם ואין הדעת סובלתן</note> that is / "Here the Christians speak of things / which are impossible to hear / and they interpret the word *taamú* (taste) / as eating / and say / that they eat their <term>Yirah <gloss>reverence/object of worship</gloss></term>, that is / their idol / which reason cannot bear or suffer." <note>This is a Jewish polemical critique of the Christian doctrine of the Eucharist (Holy Communion), where the bread and wine are believed to be the body and blood of Christ.</note> And in the old *Nizzáchon* <note>A famous anonymous medieval Jewish polemical work against Christianity.</note> on page 135, concerning the words of Isaiah 45:20, **"Those who carry their wooden idols /"** it is read: <note>original Hebrew: זהו שתי וערב ופסל מצוייר עליו והם נושאים את העץ : ומתפללים אל אלוה אשר שתי וערב זה עשוי בדמותו והוא לא יושיע ואין לך לומר שבאומה אחרת שנושאת עץ פסלם ומתפללים לעץ עצמו הכתוב מדבר דאם כן הנושאים עץ פסלם ומתפללים לו היה לו לומר אלא בודאי על אומרו זו של אמונת ישו הכתוב מדבר לפי שהם נושאים העץ והצלם להראות דמות יראתם</note> that is / "This signifies the <term>warp and the woof <gloss>Zettel und Durchschlag</gloss></term> / (that is / the Cross / which the Jews call thus / because the warp and the woof on a cloth are made cross-wise by the weaver /) together with the image / which is formed upon it. Seventhly, they call him עבודה זרה **Avóda sára** (or *Avódo fóro*,) which properly means a "foreign service" / by which a false god is served / and improperly also signifies an idol / in which latter sense it is used in the *Sepher mizvóth* (or *mizvos*) <note>The Book of Commandments</note> of <term>Rabbi Mósche bar Májemon <gloss>Also known as Maimonides (1138–1204), one of the most influential Torah scholars and philosophers of the Middle Ages.</gloss></term> folio 83, column 1, where it is written: <note>original Hebrew: מצוה כ"ב שהזהירנו שלא ליהנות בתכשיטין שיקשטו בהן לעבודה זרה והוא אמרו יתברך לא תחמוד כסף וזהב עליהם</note> that is, **The twenty-second commandment is / that he (namely God) has warned us / that we should not make use of the ornaments with which they decorate an *Avóda sára*, that is / an idol:** And that is / what the blessed God (Deuteronomy 7:25) says: **You shall not covet the silver / or gold / that is on them.** 

That they call Christ *Avóda sára*, however, is clearly to be seen in the book titled *Tela ignea Satanæ* <note>Latin: "The Fiery Darts of Satan," a collection of Jewish anti-Christian polemics published by Johann Christoph Wagenseil in 1681.</note>, in the *Old Nizzáchon*, page 146, regarding the words of Zechariah 14:9, **At that time the Lord shall be unique / and his name unique /** where it is read: <note>original Hebrew: וגם עכשיו הוא הוא אחד אבל שמו איננו אחד שאין הכל קורין אותו יי' המינים הארורים קורין אותו ישו וכן כל אומה ואומה קורין את האלוהות בשם עבודה זרה שלהם</note> that is, **He is certainly unique even now / but his name is not unique / for he is not called Jehovah by everyone / because the cursed heretics (meaning the Christians) call him Yeshu or Jesus: And thus every nation calls the deity according to the name of its *Avóda sára*, or its idol.** 

So also writes <term>Rabbi Salomon Jarchi <gloss>Commonly known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Bible and the Talmud.</gloss></term>, in his interpretation of Exodus 23:14: <note>original Hebrew: לא תעשה שותפות עם כותי שישבע לך בעבודה זרה שלו</note> that is, **You shall not enter into a partnership with a Cuthean <note>Eisenmenger argues that "Cuthean" (traditionally a Samaritan) is a censors' substitute for "Christian" in Jewish texts.</note> (that is / a Christian / as will be proven below in the 16th Chapter) / lest he swear to you by his *Avóda sára*, or his idol (namely / Jesus).** 

And in the book *Emek hammélech* <note>"The Valley of the King," a 1648 Kabbalistic work by Naphtali Herz ben Jacob Elhanan.</note> it is reported on folio 20, column 4, in the 32nd Chapter / under the title *Scháar ólam hattóhu*: <note>original Hebrew: אותו האיש עשה עצמו עבודה זרה</note> that is, **That same man (namely / Jesus / who was mentioned there previously) made himself into an *Avóda sára* or an idol.** Beyond this, it is written in the said book *Emek hammélech*, folio 135, column 4, in the 19th Chapter / under the title *rescha dife ánpin*, concerning the soul of Christ: <note>original Hebrew: היא ממש עבודה זרה אל אחר לכן עשה עצמו עבודה זרה</note> that is, **It is actually the *Avóda sára*, or the idol / the other (or foreign) God / therefore he made himself into an *Avóda sára* / or an idol.** In the very same way, Christ is also named in the Talmud / where in the tractate...

# Of the shameful names / which the Jews give to Christ.

The ruler of the kingdom (that is / Christendom / as is indicated below in the 17th chapter of this first part / under the nineteenth name / which the Jews give to it /) has the government over them (namely the Israelites) / until the kingdom (of the Messiah) shall shine forth. Thus they also pray further in the aforementioned *Machsor* <note>A Jewish prayer book containing the festival liturgy.</note> folio 31, column 2 of the first part / in a prayer / which begins / <note>original Hebrew: אנסיכה מלכי</note> *Ansicha malki* <note>Translated: "I will enthrone my King."</note>, under the title *Musaph shel Rosh Hashanah yom rishon* <note>The "Additional Service" for the first day of the Jewish New Year.</note>: <note>original Hebrew: הבל המומלך על מה מלך וגו׳</note> that is / **Why does the Bel rule, to whom the royal government is given?** And in the commentary upon it / it is taught: <note>original Hebrew: הבל המומלך כלומר מלכות הרשעה שעובדת עבודה זרה שנקראת בל</note> that is / **By the Bel, to whom the government is given / is to be understood the *Malchuth ha-resha'ah* <note>The "wicked kingdom," a common term in medieval Jewish literature often used as a code for the Roman Empire or Christendom.</note>, that is / the godless kingdom / (that is / Christendom / as is indicated below in the 17th chapter of this first part / under the ninth name / which the Jews give to Christendom /) which serves the idol / which is called Bel.**

As for what concerns the shameful name **Baal Peor** <note>A biblical idol (Numbers 25:3) associated with shameful or obscene rites.</note> / it is so named in the preface of *Abarbenel* <note>Isaac Abarbenel (1437–1508), a renowned Jewish statesman, philosopher, and biblical commentator.</note> to the book *Ma'yene Yeshu'ah* <note>Translated: "Springs of Salvation," a commentary on the Book of Daniel.</note> folio 5, column 1 / where it is written concerning the Christians in the following manner: <note>original Hebrew: ותחת היותם אויבי פושעים ומורדים פסילי אלהיהם עובדים ולבעל פעור נצמדים והמה מקטרים לבעל כורעים ומשתחוים לאיש לבוש הבדים</note> that is / **Because they are enemies of God / they are transgressors (or sinners) and rebels; they serve the idols of their gods / and cling to Baal Peor; they burn incense to Baal, and bow down before the man / who is clothed in linen.** <note>The "man clothed in linen" is a reference to Daniel 10:5, which the author here interprets as a Jewish reference to Christ or Christian priests.</note>

## Of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked, Chapter II.
<meta>catchword: Synagogue/</meta>

Lot / as their Lot has set <term>etc.</term> <note>This continues a prayer from the previous page, likely the Alenu.</note> Following this are several words against Christ and the Christians which are found in the old prayer books—such as the **Machsor** <note>A festival prayer book.</note> printed in Prague in the year 373 (that is, 1613 by our reckoning), in the 1st part, folio 31, column 1—but which have been omitted from the new versions out of fear of the Christians. In their place, one either finds a blank space, so that the omitted text can be written in by hand, or a small ring appears to indicate that something has been left out. Those same words, however, read as follows: <note>original Hebrew: שהם כורעים ומשתחוים להבל וריק ומתפללים אל אל לא יושיע</note> **That is: "For they bow down and prostrate themselves before the Héfel varík (that is, vanity and emptiness, or the vain and empty one) and pray to a god who cannot save."** Or, as it is read in the aforementioned Prague Machsor: <note>original Hebrew: שהם משתחוים להבל וריק ומתפללים ללא יושיע</note> **That is: "For they bow down before vanity and emptiness, and pray to one who cannot save."**

<margin>What the word Héfel means.</margin>
Regarding the word <term>Héfel</term> <note>Usually transliterated as "Hevel."</note>: it literally means "vanity," but figuratively it signifies an idol, which is a vain thing. In this latter sense, it is used in 2 Kings 17:15, as well as in Jeremiah 2:5, in the words: <note>original Hebrew: וילכו אחרי ההבל</note> **that is, "They walked after Héfel,"** meaning vanity. Regarding this, Rabbi Levi ben Gerson <note>A famous 14th-century philosopher and commentator also known as Gersonides.</note> writes in his commentary: <note>original Hebrew: ההבל היא עבודה זרה</note> **That is: "Héfel signifies as much as Avóda sára"** (which means an idol). Similarly, false gods are called <term>Hafalím</term> (vanities) in Deuteronomy 32:21, where it is said: <note>original Hebrew: כעסוני בהבליהם</note> **that is, "They have provoked me to anger with their Hafalím or vanities"** (namely, their idols). Because they now consider Christ to be a false god, they also give Him this name out of contempt. Therefore, in the handwritten **Selichóth** <note>Penitential prayers.</note> found in the copy located in Nuremberg—as Mr. Wülffer indicates in his notes on the *Jewish Theriack* <note>A reference to Johann Wülffer’s 1681 critique of Zalman Zevi Aufhausen’s "Jüdischer Theriak," a book defending Judaism.</note> on page 40—one reads the following in a prayer for the second day of the New Year, which begins *Jisraël ammechá techinna órechim*: <note>original Hebrew: טמאים האומרים נחלתו לחבל כבודך להמיר ואחר הבלם להתנבל נצר נתעב לאלוה לקבל</note> **That is: "The unclean ones (Christians) intend to destroy your inheritance, to change your glory, and that we should defile ourselves with their Héfel or vanity, and accept the abominable branch (Jesus) as a God."** As for the word <term>Varík</term> <note>Hebrew for "and emptiness."</note>, they understand it—by way of the frequently mentioned Cabbalistic method of <term>Gemátria</term> <note>A system where letters are assigned numerical values to find hidden meanings.</note>—to mean the name <term>Jeschu</term> (JESUS), because both words yield the same number, namely 316.

<margin>Proof that Christ is meant by Héfel.</margin>
That the Jews understand our most worthy Savior by the terms *Héfel varík* is reported not only by the highly learned Buxtorf in his *Jews' Synagogue* <note>Reference to Johannes Buxtorf’s "Synagoga Judaica," a standard 17th-century Christian work on Jewish customs.</note>...
