# Of the shameful names which the Jews give to Christ.
L 2
<meta>catchword: toward /</meta>

<margin>...varik be mentioned.</margin>
School, in the tenth chapter; but it is also unanimously confirmed by several converted Jews, such as Friederich Samuel Brenzen in his *The Jewish Sloughed-off Snakeskin* in Chapter 5, and Dieterich Schwaben in the 14th Chapter of his *The Jewish Cloak*, and Ferdinand Hessen in the 3rd Chapter of the 3rd Part of his *The Jews' Scourge*, as well as Anthonio Margarita in his entire *Jewish Faith*, page 306. It is further indicated by Buxtorf <note>Johannes Buxtorf was a famous 17th-century Christian Hebraist.</note>, as well as against the same Ferdinand Hessen and Anthonio Margarita in the aforementioned places, that when the Jews pronounce the said blasphemous words, they <margin>...and spit at the Christians.</margin> spit out against Christ and his believers.

<margin>Objections against this by Rabbi Salman Zevi.</margin>
However, it could be objected here that Christ is not meant by this, because Rabbi Salman Zevi, in his *Jewish Theriac* <note>original: "Theriack," a term for a medical antidote; here used as a title for a book defending Judaism.</note> in the 5th Chapter, number 4, denies this and accuses Friederich Samuel Brenzen—who wrote this about the Jews in his aforementioned *Jewish Sloughed-off Snakeskin*—of an obvious lie. He also signifies that Joshua composed this prayer against the peoples in the land of Canaan who were given over to idolatry, and that it has nothing at all to do with Christ and the Christians, of whom no one had even thought at that time. He adds further that in the said prayer, it immediately follows: <note>original Hebrew: ומושב יקרו ממעל</note> **"And the seat of his glory [jekarô] is from above (in heaven)."** He argues that the word <term>Jekarô</term> <note>Meaning "His glory."</note> would also have to mean <term>Jéshu</term> <note>A shortened Hebrew name for Jesus, often used polemically.</note>, because, like the latter, it totals 316 according to <term>Gematria</term> <note>A Jewish system of numerology where each letter has a numerical value.</note>. By this, they would be confessing that Jesus is in the highest heaven, which no Jew would do.

# Concerning the Insulting Names which the Jews give to Christ.

L 3

<meta>Catchword: Jesus</meta>

*jekaró* (or *jekóro*) <note>original Hebrew: *yekaro*, meaning "His preciousness" or "His glory"</note>, the words *vekisse kefódo* <note>original Hebrew: *u-khisse khevodo*, meaning "and the throne of His glory"</note>, that is, "and the throne of His glory," are found—as seen in the aforementioned old Prague <term>Mahzor</term> <note>A prayer book containing the liturgy for Jewish festivals</note>, folio 6, column 2, and folio 56, column 1 of the first part; and in the <term>Mahzor</term> printed here in Frankfurt am Main in the year 436 (which is 1676) with a German translation in quarto, folio 13, column 1, and elsewhere—in order that the numerical correspondence might be avoided. Indeed, there are Jews who do not wish for the word *Jekaró* to remain in the prayer, as is reported in the previously mentioned written commentary on the <term>Mahzor</term>, of which the words in Mr. Wülffer’s <note>Johann Wülffer, a 17th-century Christian scholar of Hebrew</note> notes on the *Jewish Antidote* <note>original: *Theriack*; a book by Zalman Zevi defending Judaism</note>, page 311, read as follows: "There are some who take care not to say *u-moshav jekaro* <note>original Hebrew: "and the seat of His preciousness"</note> because it contains the letters of *she-va-rik* <note>Eisenmenger refers to a numerical system where the letters for "His preciousness" and "emptiness" add up to the same value</note>; rather, they say *u-moshav kefódo* <note>original: "and the seat of His glory"</note>." This means: There are people who take care that they do not say *u-moshav jekaro* (or *jekoro*), because *jekoro* makes the same total numerical value as *Varík* <note>Hebrew for "emptiness" or "vanity"</note>, but instead they say *u-moshav kefódo*, which matches the meaning of the words *u-moshav jekoro* in sense, but not in number. This change is made so that, because of the matching numerical values of the words *jekoro* and *varík*, it should not be implied that Jesus is in heaven.

<margin>Response to Rabbi Lipmann’s objection.</margin>
But as for that which Rabbi Lipmann <note>Likely Yom-Tov Lipmann Heller or Lipmann Mühlhausen, famous Jewish scholars</note> gave as an answer to a converted Jew, it is entirely absurd: that Jesus cannot be understood through the word *Varík* because He is not called *Jéschu* <note>original: ישו</note> but rather *Jeschúa* <note>original: ישוע</note>. For it was shown in detail above that Jesus is not called *Jeschúa* by them, but only *Jéschu* out of pure malice, so that indeed *Jéschu* and *Varík* produce the same number <note>In Gematria, both names/words equal 316</note>. It is to be observed, however, that just as Rabbi Lipmann in many other places (which shall be pointed out in this book) has not brought the truth and his real opinion to light, but has only brought forward partly nonsensical and partly subtle evasions to instruct the Jews on what they should answer the Christians when they are called to account by them—so has he also done here. Therefore, after he brought forward as much as possible to cover his untruth, he writes in the cited place: "This answer is useful to tell them regarding all those mocking things said of Jesus in the <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism</note>; tell them that this one (the *Jeschu* mentioned in the Talmud) is not Jesus."

## Chapter II of the First Part of Judaism Unveiled.

<margin>[He] is called a God who cannot save.</margin> JESUS, as can be seen in the old *Nizzáchon* <note>The *Sefer Nizzahon Yashan* (Old Book of Victory), a medieval Jewish apologetic text written to counter Christian missionary arguments</note> page 135, where the cited words of the prophet Isaiah are interpreted; there, the wicked author, Rabbi Mattátja, writes as follows: <note>original Hebrew: "Certainly this scripture speaks of the nation that believes in Jesus, because they carry the wood and the image to show the form of their *Jirah* [reverence/idol], but they do not pray to the wood and the image itself, but to the one after whose image this wood and image was made. Behold, the prophet testifies that he is an *El lo joschia* [a god who cannot save]."</note> that is, **"Certainly the Scripture speaks of the people who believe in Jesus, because they carry the wood and the cross to show the image of their *Jirah* <note>original: *Yirah*; Hebrew for 'fear' or 'reverence,' but used here by the author to disparagingly refer to a Christian object of worship</note>, that is, their idol. Behold, the prophet thus testifies that he (namely, Jesus) is the *El lo joschia* <note>original Hebrew: *El lo yoshia* (Isaiah 45:20)</note>, that is, the GOD who cannot save."** And on page 141 of the said old *Nizzáchon*, it is written: <note>original Hebrew: "Do not trust in Jesus, for he is a son of man and was hung [executed], for he cannot save; for he could not save himself, so how can he save others?"</note> that is, **"Do not rely on Jesus, for he is a child of man and was hanged; he also cannot save. Indeed, he could not save himself; how then should he have the power to save others and to help them?"**

<margin>The Jews, however, err greatly in this.</margin> The obstinate Jews, however, are very much mistaken in imagining that Jesus could not help himself and could not save himself from death at the hands of his enemies. For as the almighty Son of God, he lacked no power to set himself free. However, because it was so determined in the divine counsel that the second person of the most holy Trinity, the eternal Son of God, should—in the fullness of time—assume human nature and perform the work of redemption (of which the prophet Isaiah in the 53rd chapter so clearly prophesied), he willingly submitted himself to the Father’s will in this matter, as seen in Matthew 26:29 <note>likely referring to verse 39: "not as I will, but as thou wilt"</note>, and gladly endured the shameful death of the cross, as read in John 10:17–18, Philippians 2:7–8, and Hebrews 2:2. Therefore, he is also introduced speaking in Psalm 40:7–9: **"Sacrifice and meat offering you do not desire, but my ears you have opened; you require neither burnt offering nor sin offering. Then I said, 'Behold, I come; in the book it is written of me: I delight to do your will, O my God.'"** For otherwise, the poor, sinful human race could not have been saved from Hell. Thus, he did not lack the ability. So he also said to Peter, who (as seen in Matthew 26:51–53) struck off the ear of the High Priest’s servant with a sword, intending to defend him and fight for Christ: **"Do you think that I could not pray to my Father, and he would send me more than twelve legions of angels?"** From all of which it is reasonable to judge that Christ suffered death voluntarily and did not desire to save himself from it.

<meta>This page continues the philological argument from the previous page, where the author asserts that the Hebrew term "Talui" is used by Jewish writers specifically to mock Jesus as "the Hanged One," rather than as a term for "doubt" or "uncertainty" in legal contexts.</meta>

### On the shameful names which the Jews give to Christ.

...[praise]worthy (that is, you, who are the praiseworthy God) to be confused with the *Nithleh* <note>original: "Nikleh" in the text, likely a typo for "Nithleh," meaning the despised or hanged one</note>, that is, the contemptible (Jesus), and to accept him as God instead of you? Here we see clearly that *Talui* and *Nithleh* are understood to have the same meaning, and it cannot be otherwise, for both come from the aforementioned root word *tala* <note>meaning "to hang"</note>. The former is the past participle in the first conjugation, which is called *Kal* <term>Kal: The simplest form of the Hebrew verb, usually active</term>, while the latter is the present participle in the *Niphal* passive <term>Niphal: A Hebrew verb form typically used to express passive or reflexive action</term>. Both signify one who is hanged, and the word *Nithleh* is nowhere found to mean "doubtful."

Thus, Christ is also called *Talui bemagod*, that is, **the one hanged on the nail**, in the Polish *Siddurim* <term>Siddurim: Jewish prayer books containing the daily order of prayers</term> on folio 7, column 1, in a prayer beginning with *Elohai becha echfetz* <note>original Hebrew: "אלהי בך אחבץ", "My God, in You I delight"</note>, under the title *Yotzer le-shabbat revii acher ha-Pesach* <note>A liturgical poem for the fourth Sabbath after Passover</note>.

Furthermore, Rabbi Bechai <term>Rabbi Bechai: Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish rabbi and scholar of Jewish law and mysticism</term> writes in his book *Kad ha-Kemah* <term>Kad ha-Kemah: "The Jar of Flour," an encyclopedic work on Jewish ethics</term> on folio 19, column 4, regarding the words of Psalm 80:14, *Yacharsemennah chazir mi-yaar* <note>original: "יכרסמנה חזיר מיער", meaning "The boar from the forest ravages it [the vine]"</note>, which is to say: "A wild swine shall root it up (namely, the vine)." He writes as follows: **"The letter Ayin is *teluja* <note>meaning "hanging" or "suspended"</note> (in the word *mi-yaar*), because they (namely, the Christians) worship the *Talui*, that is, the Hanged One."** (The letter *Ayin* in this verse is written suspended above the line, rather than in a straight line with the other letters.) From these words, it is clear as day that *Talui* means one who is hanged, and not one who is "doubtful." For here a comparison is made between the letter *Ayin*—which hangs above the other three letters of the word *mi-yaar*—and Christ, the Crucified One. Just as the *Ayin* is suspended, so too was Christ suspended. Just as *teluja* does not mean "doubtful" here, neither can *Talui* be interpreted that way.

Indeed, in the aforementioned Polish *Siddurim*, on folio 71, column 1, under the title *Meorah le-shabbat shenia* <note>A liturgical poem for the second Sabbath</note>, in the commentary on a prayer beginning with *El El chai achannen* <note>original: "אל אל חי אחננן", "To God, the living God, I will pray"</note>, where Christ is also called *Talui*, it is clearly taught: **"The translation of *Talui* is *tsaluv*,"** <note>original: "תרגום תלוי צלוב", an Aramaic/Hebrew equivalence</note> which is to say, *Talui* signifies a crucified or hanged person.

Who then would be so simple-minded as to be persuaded that the godless Jews—who pour out all sorts of blasphemies, shameful, and mocking words against Christ—do not also use it here in a contemptuous sense? Especially since they sometimes use the word *Tzaluf* (or *Tsoluf*) <note>original: "צלוף", a variant of *Tzaluv*, the Crucified One</note>, which signifies one hanged on a cross, instead of the word *Talui*. M 3

<margin>The misdeed and blasphemy of a Jew against Christ.</margin>

As happened in the month of March of the past year 1699 in Zell <note>Zell: likely refers to Celle in Lower Saxony, Germany</note>, when a Jew named Jonas Meyer—having been brought to the gallows to receive his deserved reward for many thefts—had the rope already around his neck. # Chapter II of the First Part of Judaism Discovered.
<meta>catchword: Malice</meta>

"...blot me out," <note>original: מחני *mecheni*; from Exodus 32:32, where Moses asks God to blot him out of His book if He will not forgive the Israelites.</note> by which he intended to mean: "I did not pray at the time of the Flood (namely, for humanity); but now I will give my soul for them." And that is what is written: *mecheni* [blot me out], which contains the same letters as the words *me Noach* <note>original: מי נח; literally "the waters of Noah."</note> which are called the waters of Noah. Is this not a nonsensical proof that Noah's soul entered into Moses, simply because the rearrangement of the letters of the word *mecheni* results in *me Noach*? In the same subtle manner, it is proven in the **Yalkut Chadash** <note>A 17th-century collection of Midrashic and Kabbalistic teachings.</note> folio 139, column 2, number 290, under the title "Moses," that Moses deserved to be driven into exile because he killed the Egyptian, where it is written:

<center>משה שהרג את המצרי היה חטא בידו ונתחייב גלות וזהו אשר ינוס ש"מה אותיות משה</center>

that is, **"Moses sinned because he killed the Egyptian, for which reason he became guilty of exile <note>original Latin: *exilii*</note> or misery; and this is signified by the words (Exodus 21:13) *asher yanus shamma*, that is, 'whither he should flee,' because the word *shamma* [there/thither] (through the transposition of letters) makes the name *Moshe* [Moses]."** From this, one can see how subtle and clever these Rabbinical donkey-heads are.

In such a way, one could also claim that Laban's soul passed into Nabal, and the soul of Shem or Sem (Noah's son) into Mash or Mas (mentioned in Genesis 10:23); and the soul of Meshech (Genesis 10:2) into Shechem (Genesis 34:2); as well as the soul of Nadab (Aaron's son) into Bedan (1 Samuel 12:11); because through the transposition of the letters—which are called consonants—*Laban* can be read as *Nabal*, *Shem* as *Mash*, *Meshech* as *Shechem*, and *Nadab* as *Bedan*. 

So one could also prove that Cain was innocent when he killed his brother Abel, because from the name *Kain* <note>Hebrew: קין</note> the word *naki* <note>Hebrew: נקי</note> (which means "innocent") arises through the same transposition of letters. One could also prove that Lamech was a king, because from *Lemech* <note>Hebrew: למך</note> the word *Melech* <note>Hebrew: מלך; "King"</note> can be made; and no less that Moses was God himself, because the word *Hashem* <note>Hebrew: השם; "The Name," a common substitute for the Tetragrammaton or God's name.</note> and the name *Moshe* [Moses] have the same letters, only transposed. But as foolish and irrational as it would seem to the Jews if one tried to prove to them that Cain was innocent, Lamech was a king, and Moses was God—it is just as nonsensical as what Abarbanel <note>Don Isaac Abarbanel (1437–1508), a famous Jewish statesman and theologian.</note> brings forward concerning *Yeshua* [Jesus] and *Esai* [Esau]. Indeed, it is even more frivolous...

# Of the Shameful Names Which the Jews Give to Christ.

...malice in this, for the word *Esav* <note>Esau</note> is never written with the letter *Yod* (עשו), but is always written without it in the Holy Scripture. Thus, from *Esav* (עשו), the name *Jeschúa* <note>Jesus</note> (ישוע) cannot possibly be derived, as the former has only three letters, while the latter has four.

<margin>The Jewish doctrine of the transmigration of souls is foolish.</margin> As for the transmigration of souls <term>transmigration of souls: known as *Gilgul* in Jewish mysticism, the belief that a soul can inhabit successive bodies</term>, this is a foolish doctrine originating from the pagan philosopher Pythagoras. Its emptiness shall be dealt with more extensively below in the first chapter of the second part. However, concerning the fact that the Jews teach so blasphemously regarding the most holy soul of Jesus Christ—claiming it originated from the high demon Sammael <note>In Jewish lore, Sammael is often identified as the Angel of Death or a prince of demons</note>, was given to Cain, passed from him into Korah and Esau, and finally entered into Jesus—this was prompted in them by the high demon himself, the father of all slanderers and blasphemers and the declared enemy of Christ. He makes the most innocent Jesus hateful to them in this way so that they might not believe in him or recognize him as their Savior. He who is of the devil does the devil's work and makes it his earnest concern to increase the devil's kingdom. Christ, however, led a holy and irreproachable life, as the Jewish historian Josephus himself testifies (which was cited previously on page 94), and he destroyed the devil's kingdom through the conversion of men. Furthermore, the Messiah is called in Isaiah 7:14 "Immanuel," which means "God with us"; and in Isaiah 9:6 "El gibbor" <note>original: אל גבור</note>, which means "Mighty God," and "Abi ad" <note>original: אבי עד</note>, which means "Father of Eternity"; as also in Jeremiah 23:6, where he is called "The Jehovah <note>the LORD</note> who is our Righteousness." How then can they so hideously blaspheme Jesus, who is the true promised Messiah (as shall be proven below in the fifth chapter), and attribute such impurity of soul to him, when he is not only a holy man but also simultaneously God?

<margin>The proof through Notarikon is also entirely absurd.</margin> Likewise, the proof through *Notarikon* <term>Notarikon: a Kabbalistic method of using the letters of a word as initials for other words, or creating an acronym</term>—claiming that the letters of the word "Kain" (K. I. N.) have the aforementioned meaning—is just as foolish and absurd as that which is brought forth through *Gematria* <term>Gematria: a system of assigning numerical values to letters to find hidden meanings</term> or *Temura* <term>Temura: the practice of rearranging or substituting letters to form new words</term>. They claim the letter *Koph* or K represents the names Cain and Korah, while the *Jod* and *Nun* (I and N) represent the words *Jesus Nazarenus* <note>Latin: Jesus the Nazarene</note>. This is based on nothing other than a foolish imagination and fiction. One could just as easily say the *Jod* (or J) in the word Cain refers to the Patriarch Isaac or Jacob, and the *Nun* (or N) refers to Naphtali the son of Jacob, or to Nun, the father of Joshua. But these are nothing but Rabbinical ravings.

Since it can also be seen in the words cited above from Abarbanel's <note>Isaac Abarbanel (1437–1508), a famous Sephardic statesman and philosopher</note> book *Mashmía Jeshúa* <note>original: משמיע ישוע; "The Proclaimer of Salvation"</note> folio 19, column 4, that Jesus supposedly bickered and quarreled with the Pharisees because the soul of Esau had entered into him...

### Chapter II of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.
<meta>Catchword: Books</meta>

...as it should be, so must it also be shown here what is to be found in their books concerning this: it is to be noted that it is taught by them that Christ was born under the planet Mars, whose power and soul is the high demon Sammael, and that those who receive an influence from the said planet are fond of quarreling and wrangling.

<margin>Christ is said to have been born under the planet Mars.</margin>
That Christ was born under Mars is read in the aforementioned Abarbenel’s <note>Don Isaac Abravanel (1437–1508), a prominent Jewish statesman and commentator.</note> commentary on the prophet Isaiah, folio 54, column 4, as well as in his book *Maschmía Jeschúa* <note>original: *Maschmía Jeschúa*, meaning "The Herald of Salvation."</note> folio 19, column 4, in these words: <note>original Hebrew: להיות הנוצרי תחת מאדים היה דמו בראשו ונהרג הוא ותלמידיו ועמים רבים מהנמשכים אחריו</note> which is: Because Jesus the Nazarene was under the planet Mars, his blood was upon his head, and he, along with his disciples, apostles, and many peoples who followed him, was put to death.

<margin>But the soul of Mars is said to be Sammael.</margin>
But that the high demon Sammael is the power and soul of Mars, regarding this Rabbi Bechai <note>Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish rabbi and kabbalist.</note> writes in his commentary on the Five Books of Moses, folio 79, column 4, in the *Parashah Beshalach* <note>The weekly Torah portion "Beshalach," covering Exodus 13:17–17:16.</note> as follows: <note>original Hebrew: אין אומה נופלת עד שהפול שרה תחלה והגלגל הזה הוא גלגל מאדים שבו היו המצריים ראויים לנצח ולהתגבר לולי השם שהיה לנו נלחם לישראל • וכח הגלגל הוא סמ"אל ומלת אופן הוא חסר ו'או כחשבונו</note> that is: No nation falls before its prince falls first (by which is understood that demon who rules over it in the air, as can be seen below in the 18th chapter of this first part): This *sphæra* or sphere is the sphere of Mars, through which the Egyptians would have been capable of overcoming and gaining the upper hand, had God not fought for us Israelites; but the power and strength of this sphere is Sammael, and the word <note>original Hebrew: אפן</note> *Ofan* (which signifies a wheel), when written without the letter *Vav*, makes—through <term>Gematria</term> <gloss>a system where Hebrew letters are assigned numerical values</gloss>—precisely the same number as <note>original Hebrew: סמאל</note> Sammael, namely 131. The same is found in the book *Toledot Yitzchak* <note>The "Generations of Isaac," a commentary by Isaac Caro.</note>, folio 52, column 1, in the said *Parashah Beshalach*.

<margin>Those who are born under Mars are said to be quarrelsome.</margin>
That those who are born under Mars are also quarrelsome is taught in the book *Kad HaKemach* <note>original: *Cad hakkémach*, meaning "The Jar of Flour," a work on ethics by Bahya ben Asher.</note> folio 24, column 3, with these words: <note>original Hebrew: זה המלאך נברא להשטין ולהזיק ואולי כי מאצילות כחו יהא לאדם שטנה כי הוא סבה לכוכבי החרבן והדמים והחרב והמלחמות והמכות והמריבות והפירוד והכלל נפש לגלגל מאדים</note> that is: This angel (Sammael) was created to hate and to do harm, and perhaps because hatred comes to man from the influence of his power: for he is the cause of the stars of destruction, of blood-shedding, of the sword, of wars, of blows, of wounds, of quarrels, and of all division; and to put it briefly, he is the soul of Mars. This is also found, in almost the same words, in the commentary of Rabbi Menachem of Recanati <note>A 14th-century Italian kabbalist.</note> on the Five Books of Moses...

# Concerning the shameful names that the Jews give to Christ.
O

...Books of Moses in the Section *Acharei Mot* (or *Mos*) <note>The Torah portion covering Leviticus 16:1–18:30.</note> folio 141, column 2, 3. <margin>XVIII. Called *Mamser ben hannidda*.</margin>
Eighteenthly, they blasphemously call him *Mamser* <note>original: ממזר</note>, that is, a child of whoredom [bastard], or *Mamser ben hannidda*, that is, a child of whoredom and son of an impure woman, who was conceived by his mother during the time of her female impurity <note>referring to *Niddah*, the laws of ritual impurity regarding menstruation; in this context, it is used as a severe insult to imply the child was conceived in violation of holy law.</note>. This, as well as the cause of such an opinion, is reported in detail in the cursed, hellish little book *Toledoth* (or *Toledos*) *Jeshu* <note>The *Toledot Yeshu* is a medieval Jewish counter-narrative of the life of Jesus, often parodying the Gospels.</note> (which is to be found in its entirety from beginning to end in this, as well as the following third, fourth, and seventh chapters, wherein the devil has poured out all his malice and poison against our Savior), where the words from the beginning to page 6 of the same read as follows:

<margin>Beginning of the devilish little book *Toledoth Jeschu*.</margin>
In the year 3671 of the fourth millennium [approx. 90 BCE], in the days of King Jannai <note>Alexander Jannaeus, a Hasmonean king.</note>, there was a great trouble for the "enemies of Israel" <note>A common Jewish euphemism for Israel itself when describing hardships.</note> because there arose a herder of harlots, an evil man and a scoundrel from the tribe of Judah, and his name was Joseph Pandera. He was of tall stature, a hero in war, and beautiful of form, and most of his days were spent in adultery, lewdness, robbery, and violence. He dwelt in Bethlehem in Judah. Near his house dwelt a widow and her daughter, whose name was Miriam; she is Miriam the women’s hairdresser <note>original: *Miriam Megaddla Nashayya*, a punning reference to Mary Magdalene found in Talmudic polemics.</note> mentioned in the Talmud. When she grew up, her mother betrothed her to a young man named Jochanan, and the young man was humble, lowly in spirit, and God-fearing. 

One day, Joseph passed by Miriam’s door and saw her, and his evil inclination burned within him. He went and returned. She said to him, "Tell me, why are you so lean?" and he answered and said to her, "I love you, Miriam the bride." She said to him, "Do not let your heart be troubled by this, but desire and hold fast to her as you wish." And Joseph Pandera did so; he always went by the door of Miriam’s house but found no opportune time until one Sabbath evening, when he found Miriam sitting at the door of her house. He went into the house with her, into a room near the door, and lay with her, and she thought he was Jochanan her betrothed. She said to him, "Do not touch me, for I have become impure," but he did not listen to her and did as he pleased, then went to his house. 

At midnight, his evil inclination burned in him again, and he rose from his sleep, went the way of Miriam’s house, entered her room, and took hold of her a second time. The girl was greatly terrified and said to him, "What is this, my lord, that you have come to me twice in one night, which I have not experienced since the day you betrothed me?" He doubled his silence and did not answer a word. Miriam said to him, "How long will you add sin to transgression? Did I not already tell you I have become impure?" But he did not listen to her voice and did as he pleased, then went his way. 

After three months, it was told to Jochanan, "Behold, your betrothed is pregnant." Jochanan was greatly terrified and went to Simeon ben Shetach <note>A famous Pharisaic scholar of the 1st century BCE.</note>, his teacher, and told him the matter and asked him what he should do. His teacher said to him, "My son, listen to my advice and be silent; if he came upon her once, it is impossible that he will not come upon her another time. Act with wisdom and place witnesses upon her and bring him to the Great Court." The young man went out and went to his house and mourned greatly. When it became public knowledge that she was pregnant, Jochanan said, "Now they will say she is pregnant by me." Out of great shame and disgrace, he left the Land of Israel and went to Babylon and remained there. And Miriam bore a son and called his name Joshua after her uncle, her mother's brother.

<margin>The Jews do not agree with one another in their testimony regarding Christ.</margin>
Furthermore, because those who deal in frivolous lies are always inconsistent and their fabrications do not align, the same happens here with the godless Jews. # Chapter II of the First Part of Discovered Judaism.
<meta>catchword: ent-</meta>

regarding the first two bans, it is taught in the book *Shulchan Aruch* <note>term: Shulchan Aruch. The "Set Table," a fundamental 16th-century code of Jewish law.</note>, in the section *Yoreh Deah* <note>term: Yoreh Deah. A portion of the Shulchan Aruch dealing with ritual law, including the laws of the ban.</note> number 334, § 2, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: אין נדוי פחות משלשים יום ואם אינו חוזר בו שונים לנדותו : לאחר שלשים יום ואם אינו חוזר בו ממתינים לו עוד שלשים ומחרימין אותו :</note> **that is, The ban *Niddui* lasts no less than thirty days; and if he does not repent, he is placed under such a ban for another thirty days. If he still does not repent, they wait another thirty days, and then he is placed under the *Cherem*, which is a heavier ban than the ban *Niddui*.** Through this ban of *Niddui*—a word derived from *Nada*, that is, to yield or step away, and *Nidda*, that is, to separate and exclude—a person is separated and excluded from human society, so that no one may sit within four cubits <note>term: Cubit. An ancient unit of length, roughly 18 inches or 45 centimeters; the law required physical distancing from the excommunicated person.</note> of him, as can be seen in the cited passage of the book *Yoreh Deah*, and he is excluded from the synagogue. Through the ban of *Cherem*, however, which is heavier than *Niddui*, the transgressor is expelled from the community and the synagogue with curses. But through the ban of *Schammata*, which is the heaviest of all, he is entirely and forever excluded from all human society, both in public life and in the synagogue, and is left to Divine Judgment, in such a way that he can no longer be reconciled with men. What the causes are for which a man may be placed under the ban, and how one is otherwise to proceed with him in such a state, can be sufficiently seen in the aforementioned place in the book *Yoreh Deah*. But let this be enough concerning the ban; we must now return to the previous matter, namely the discord of the Jews in their fictions regarding Jesus.

In ancient times, when the Temple in Jerusalem stood, it was the custom among the Jews—there being twenty-two letters in our alphabet—to have twenty-two priests seated in the Temple. A codex <note>A "codex" refers to a bound book or register, as opposed to a scroll.</note> was kept in the temple, in which was recorded the title of each of the twenty-two priests, as well as the name of his father and his mother. Thus, when one of the priests died, the others would gather in the Temple and, by a common vote, appoint another priest in place of the deceased to complete the number of twenty-two priests. And it was recorded in the codex that on such and such a day, this priest died, the son of so-and-so (father) and so-and-so (mother); and in his place was appointed this person, the son of so-and-so and so-and-so. This custom being held among the nation of the Jews, it happened in those times when Jesus was staying in Judea, that one of the twenty-two priests died, before Jesus began to manifest himself and teach people to believe in him. The remaining priests therefore came together to appoint another priest in place of the deceased; and though each proposed the one he considered worthy to be chosen, the others would reject him as being deficient in the virtue required to be established as a priest. For if he were wise, yet in character and life he was not good...

And I suppose that no man has ever been seen to be such in speech, or in life, or in character, as this man is. And I think this is known and undeniable to all of you who dwell in Jerusalem." 

Upon hearing this speech, the other priests accepted the man and confirmed the nomination, stating that Jesus was suitable above every man for the priesthood. However, some said of him that he was not of the tribe of Levi, but happened to be of the tribe of Judah, supposing him to be the son of Joseph. For thus he was known among the Jews. And all testified that Joseph was descended from the tribe of Judah, not from the tribe of Levi. For this reason, because he appeared not to be from the Levite tribe <note>In Jewish Law, only members of the tribe of Levi, specifically descendants of Aaron, could serve as priests.</note>, they tried to prevent him from becoming a priest. 

But the priest who had nominated him, answering them, said that his lineage was mixed. For long ago, in ancient generations, there was a certain intermixing of the two tribes, and from there the lineage of Joseph was descended. Therefore, hearing this, the other priests consented to the nomination. And by common counsel of all the assembled priests, it seemed good to appoint Jesus in place of the deceased priest.

As it was the custom not only to record the name of the one becoming a priest in the register <note>original: "κώδικι" (kōdiki) - a ledger or book of records</note>, but also that of his father and his mother, some of them said they ought first to call the parents and learn their names from them. They should also take their deposition <note>original: "κατάθεσιν" (katathesin) - formal testimony</note> as to whether the one being appointed to the priesthood was their son. This pleased everyone. 

Then the one who had previously nominated Jesus to become a priest said that Joseph the father had died. They all agreed, therefore, to bring his mother to the Sanhedrin <note>original: "συνέδριον" (synedrion) - the high council or assembly of elders in Jerusalem</note> and learn from her whether she happened to be the mother of Jesus, and if she herself bore him; and to hear the name of her husband, by whom she bore Jesus. 

And indeed, this pleasing everyone, they called the mother of Jesus and said to her: "Since a certain priest has died—the son of so-and-so and so-and-so—and we wish to make your son Jesus priest in his place, and as it is the custom to record the name of the father and the mother, tell us if Jesus is your son, and if you bore—"

Now, the word *Jichum* actually means an inflammation or heating, and Isaac is called "the heating of his (Abraham’s) old age" (*Jichum zekunav*) in the first part of the old Prague <term>Machsor</term> <note>a prayer book for Jewish festivals</note>, folio 118, column 2, in the prayer beginning with *Ammiz Koach* <note>original: אמיץ כח, "Mighty in Power"</note> under the heading <term>Musaf</term> <note>the additional service</note> of <term>Yom Kippur</term> <note>the Day of Atonement</note>, because Abraham fathered him in his old age. And in the commentary or explanation of it, it is explained by *Chimmum hassera* <note>original: חימום הזרע</note>, that is, a heating of the seed. Both of these aforementioned blasphemous names are found in the often-mentioned Nuremberg manuscript of the <term>Machsor</term>, in the prayer which begins: "The nations are considered as nothing and vanity before You" <note>original: הגוים אפס ותוהו נגדך חשובים, *Hagoyim efes vatochu negdecha chashuvim*</note>, under the title <term>Shacharit</term> <note>the morning prayer</note> of <term>Yom Kippur</term>, or <term>Yotzer</term> <note>a type of liturgical poem</note> for <term>Yom Kippur</term>. ->The nations are considered as nothing and vanity before You.<-
->Like vinegar to the teeth, they are not counted among Your people.<-

### On the Shameful Names which the Jews Give to Christ. ###

> <note>The following is a translation of the Hebrew poem provided in the source text:</note>
> The nations are like nothingness; they have exchanged your holiness for a child of vice.
> Those carried by you [Israel] are abhorred; the lineage of the woman of shame.

> The nations call to one who does not save or profit.
> Your friends lean on You, who teaches what is profitable.
> The nations—their libation is a lie, and there is no faith in them.
> Your perfect ones, established in your faith, speak when they assemble.

That is: The <term>Gôjim</term> <note>meaning the Christians</note> are considered as nothing before you. Your proven ones <note>that is, the Jews</note> are set apart (from them) and are not counted among them. The <term>Gôjim</term> are (to you) a disgust because of their erroneous and vain works. But we, who cling to you, are separated from those who bow before a wooden block. The <term>Gôjim</term> seek craftsmen to prepare images; but your pious ones declare (and recount) early and late your unity <note>that you alone are GOD</note>. 

The <term>Gôjim</term> prepare their gold as a covering (or clothing) for cast images. But we, who tremble at your word, are ready to serve you with fear. The <term>Gôjim</term> carry upon their backs that wood which remains from what they use for roasting (in the kitchen) <note>referring to the image carved from wood, whose chopped-off shavings are thrown into the fire; see Isaiah 44:14-17</note>. But we, your acquaintances, bow before you with the bending of the joints of the spine <note>that is, deeply, and with a very bent and stooped body</note>. 

The <term>Gôjim</term> plate their wooden idols with silver. But those whom you have accepted (as your people) place their trust in the secret of your strength. The <term>Gôjim</term> give the name of your holiness <note>that is, the name Jehovah, and God</note> to the child of vice <note>by which the godless Jews understand Christ</note>. Your sustained ones <note>that is, the Israelites, of whom Isaiah 46:3 says: "You who are carried from the womb"</note> have an abomination for the conception of the woman of vice <note>that is, for him who was conceived by the woman of vice, by which, in a most blasphemous manner, Christ the LORD and his most innocent mother are understood</note>. <margin>XXIV. He is called a gruesome or abominable God.</margin>

**Twenty-fourthly**, he is called <term>אלהי תועבות (Elohé toëfóth, or toëfos)</term>, that is, a God of abominations, or a gruesome and abominable God. This blasphemy stands in the old *Nizzáchon* <note>Sefer Nizzachon Yashar, a medieval Jewish apologetic and polemical work written to counter Christian claims</note>, page 83, where concerning the words of Isaiah 5:20, **"Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness,"** the following is written: 

<term>אותם שמחלפים את אלהי השמים באלהי תועבותם שמים חושך לאור ד"ל שמים את יש"ו שירד לגיהנם לאור :</term> 

That is: These (namely the Christians) are those who exchange the God of Heaven for their God of abomination, who make darkness out of light; that is, those who place Jesus, who has descended into Hell, into the light (and say of him that he is and sits in Heaven) or who hold and recognize him as the light.

<margin>XXV. He is also called Ben Chárja, that is, a Son of Dung.</margin>
**Twenty-fifthly**, he is named <term>Ben Chárja (בֶּן חַרְיָא)</term>, that is, **a Son of Dung**. This arises through a malicious alteration of the name Maria (which in Hebrew is *Mirjam*) into the mocking word *Chárja* <note>original: "Chárja" (חַרְיָא), an Aramaic word for excrement or filth. Eisenmenger argues this is a deliberate pun on the name Mary</note>. This appears very often in the old *Nizzáchon* <term>Nizzáchon: Likely referring to "Sefer Nizzachon Vetus," a medieval Jewish polemical work written to provide arguments against Christian missionary efforts</term>, of which some mention has already been made previously; on page 66, regarding the words of Jeremiah 17:9, "**The heart is a deceitful and yet oppressive thing; who can know it?**" it is written as follows: 

<note>original Hebrew: עקבות מיליהם שאומרים את אלהי השמים אנו יראים ואין בפיהם נכונה כי סוף סוף המה אומרים שאלוהיהם ר"ל ישו נולד מחריא הנה אנוש הוא ואני יי" חוקר לב וגו' ר"ל מכל מקום אני יודע שמאמינים בישו שהוא בן חריא</note> 

The words of those (meaning the Christians) who say, "we fear the God of Heaven," are deceitful, and there is no truth in their mouths; for ultimately they say that their god, namely Jesus, was born of the *Chárja*: see, then he is but a man. (From this follows in the 10th verse,) **I the Lord can search the heart** etc., which is as much as to say: I know well that they believe in Jesus, the son of the *Chárja*. Similar passages can be seen on pages 96 and 164, and elsewhere. 

Thus also on page 46, regarding the Holy Virgin Mary and the words of Numbers 17:8 (or according to others, verse 23), "**And behold, the rod of Aaron, of the house of Levi, sprouted,**" it is written: 

<note>original Hebrew: אומרים המינים שזה רמז על חריא ר"ל מריה שהיתה בתולה כשילדה את ישו ותפח רוחם כי סוף מראות עיניהם ומחשכיל לבותם כי חריא משבט לוי לא היתה</note>

That is: **The heretics say that this refers to the Chárja, that is, Mary, who was a virgin when she gave birth to Jesus. Let their spirit burst, for their eyes are sealed so they cannot see, and their hearts so they cannot understand, since the Chárja was not from the tribe of Levi.**

<margin>XXVI. He is also called Cheláh, that is, a scum.</margin>

It follows from this that all members of the High Council must have had their influence from the Devil.

### Chapter III of Part I of *Judaism Unmasked*

The stones of the place of Markólis <term>Markólis: A corruption of the name "Mercurius" (Mercury). In Jewish tradition, this referred to a type of idolatry involving the arrangement of stones, likely a reference to the Roman "herm" or stone heaps dedicated to Mercury</term> are arranged so that one is on this side, the other is on that side, and one lies on top of them. Through the word *Kólis*, *Markólis* is understood, as Rabbi Salomon Jarchi <note>Also known as Rashi (1040–1105), the most famous medieval commentator on the Talmud and the Hebrew Bible.</note> writes in his commentary on it, and as can be seen in the *Tosephóth* <note>original: "Tósephos"; these are medieval additions and commentaries on the Talmud.</note>. In the Talmudic tractate *Sanhédrin*, folio 60, column 2, it is written: <note>original Hebrew: הזורק אבן למרקוליס זו היא עבודתו</note> that is: **He who throws a stone at Markólis (commits an act of idolatry), for this is the way in which he is served.** It is thus to be seen from this that the idolatry of *Markólis* was performed with stones.

<margin>Refutation of the blasphemy that Christ is said to have practiced idolatry.</margin>
However, that Christ is supposed to have committed such idolatry is once again a devilish fabrication; for as we read in Luke 4, verse 8, he said to Satan: **"Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve."** So also did the Evangelist and Apostle John say in 1 John 5, verse 21 <note>The text says verse 22, but it is 1 John 5:21.</note>: **"Little children, keep yourselves from idols,"** which he learned from Christ. Indeed, idolatry is presented as an abominable sin throughout the New Testament, which contains the teachings our Savior gave to his disciples. The spirit of Paul was provoked within him when he saw the city of Athens so given to idolatry, as can be read in Acts 17, verse 16. Likewise, Paul forbade in 1 Corinthians 5, verse 11, that one should even eat with anyone who is an idolater; and in chapter 6, verse 10 of the same book, he teaches that idolaters will not inherit the kingdom of God. How then could Christ himself have practiced idolatry, since he said that one must worship God and serve Him alone? And those who followed his teaching have so earnestly forbidden idolatry upon the loss of eternal salvation?

<margin>Concerning the two opinions on how Christ performed his miracles.</margin>
We must now also examine by what means Christ, according to the teaching of the godless Jews, is said to have performed his miracles. It is important to know that they are divided into two opinions on this matter: for some teach that he performed them through the *Shem Hammephorash* <term>Shem Hammephorash: Literally the "Explicit Name" or "Set-apart Name." Others, however, say they were done through pure sorceries.

<margin>Description of the Shem Hammephorash.</margin>

...has power to bring the same to pass, except for GOD; and the (true) prophets are distinguished from those who do evil by this privilege. These are the words of the aforementioned Rabbi Menasseh <note>Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel (1604–1657), a famous Portuguese-Dutch rabbi and diplomat.</note>.

Therefore, those who dare to say in a godless manner that Christ performed His miracles through sorcery—and consequently raised the dead through sorcery—were unskilled donkeys. They did not even know that, according to their own Talmud, such a thing could not be true; or perhaps the Devil, the sworn enemy of Christ, so hardened their minds that they were unable to think of it. It is also well worth noting what Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel reports: that no one but the true prophets of God have done such things, and that by this, false prophets and evil men are distinguished from the true prophets. From this, it follows irreducibly that Jesus—who, as is reported even in the little book *Toledoth Jeschu* <term>Toledoth Jeschu<gloss>A medieval Jewish text that presents a satirical and hostile counter-narrative to the life of Jesus.</gloss></term>, raised several from the dead—must at the very least have been a pious and true prophet. Furthermore, since in the 72nd Psalm, verse 18, it is said of God that He alone performs wonders, and He must therefore have performed the wonders attributed to Christ, it would follow blasphemously that God thereby helped Christ to carry out His "deceptions" away from the path of righteousness, to introduce all kinds of error, and to bring about a shameful idolatry. Such wicked things are blasphemously said of our most innocent Savior by His sworn enemies, the Jews.

Now that we have seen from the preceding text what abhorrent vices the godless Jews, at the instigation of the Devil, attribute to Christ the Lord, we shall now also consider what they further write of Him out of false impulse, and how He is said to have fallen into the hands of His enemies.

<margin>How Christ is said to have fallen into his enemies' hands.</margin>
The history of the New Testament teaches us that when the time of His suffering, which was determined from eternity, drew near, Satan entered into Judas Iscariot, who was one of His disciples, and who betrayed Christ; whereupon He was seized and led away captive, as can be read in Luke, chapter 22. But the Devil, in the blasphemous book *Toledoth Jeschu* inspired by him, presents this quite differently, mixed with gruesome lies, merely to make the New Testament suspect—as if the matter were presented therein quite differently than it actually happened. However, so that one may see the Devil's shameful tricks within it, I will set down here everything found there regarding this; from page 8 to page 17, the words read as follows:

<margin>Continuation of the blasphemous little book Toledoth Jeschu.</margin>

> And it happened on the fifth day that bad news came to Jerusalem, the Holy City, and they told them all that Jesus had done. And the lawless ones rejoiced with great joy. But the elders, the pious, and the wise burst into great weeping, and the Great Sanhedrin and the Small Sanhedrin <note>The Great Sanhedrin was the supreme council of 71 sages; the Small Sanhedrin was a local court of 23.</note> entered into great mourning and said that they should send after them [him].

...after him, for they said in their hearts, "Perhaps we may prevail over him by the law and a sentence of death." They sent after him Anani and Ahiah, important men from the **Small Sanhedrin** <note>The Small Sanhedrin was a religious court of twenty-three judges appointed in various cities.</note>, and they came before him and bowed down to him to increase the trap for his downfall. He believed that they truly believed in him, so he received them with a friendly countenance and seated them at the head of his wicked company. They said to him: "Behold, the pious and important men of **Jerusalem** have sent us to you, that you should come to them, for they have heard of you that you are the **Son of God**."

Jesus said to them: "What you have heard is the truth. Behold, I will do all that you say, on the condition that they all come out to meet me—both the **Great Sanhedrin** <note>The supreme council of seventy-one sages in Jerusalem.</note> and the Small Sanhedrin, and even those who rejected me—and that they receive me as servants receive their masters. Then I will come to them." The messengers returned to Jerusalem and told them everything he had said. The elders and the pious men said: "Everything he has spoken, we shall do." The men returned and told Jesus: "Everything you have spoken, they will do." Jesus said to them: "I will go with you." 

And it happened when Jesus came to Nob, near Jerusalem, that Jesus said to them: "Do you have a fine and good donkey here?" They said: "We do." He said: "Bring it before me." They brought him a fine donkey, and he rode upon it to Jerusalem. When he arrived in the city, the entire city was in an uproar at his coming. Jesus raised his voice and said to them: "Regarding me, the prophet Zechariah prophesied: *Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and having salvation, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey* <note>original: "הנה מלכך יבא לך צדיק ונושע עני ורוכב על חמור ועל עיר בן אתונות" — See Zechariah 9:9.</note>." When they heard this, they wept with a great weeping and tore their garments. 

The pious men went to the Queen; she was **Queen Helena**, the wife of King Yannai mentioned previously, who reigned after the death of her husband <note>The text conflates the historical Queen Helena of Adiabene with the Hasmonean Queen Salome Alexandra.</note>. She was also called **Oleina**. Her son was King Monobaz, also called Hyrcanus, whom Herod his servant killed. They said to her: "This man is worthy of death, for he misleads people after him. Give us permission and we will catch him in our snares." The Queen gave them permission, saying: "Send for him that I may know his business." She thought to save him from their hands because he was a relative to her. 

The Sages understood her thoughts and answered her: "Our Lady Queen, do not let it enter your mind to seek his peace or his well-being, for he causes the people to stumble and misleads them through sorcery." They also told her the story of the **Ineffable Name** <term>Ineffable Name<gloss>The "Shem HaMephorash," the secret, powerful name of God which, in this tradition, Jesus is accused of stealing to perform miracles.</gloss></term>. They argued that his judgment should be brought to light because he was worthy of death, being a "bastard and the son of a menstruant" <note>original: "ממזר בן הנדה" — A common, highly derogatory polemical term used in this specific manuscript tradition to deny Jesus's divine or legitimate birth.</note>, and they told her the story of **Joseph Pandera** <note>In the Toledoth Jeschu, Pandera is named as the biological father of Jesus.</note>.

The Queen answered them: "I will listen to you in this matter as well. Bring him before me, and I will hear what he says and see what he does, for the whole world tells me of the great and terrible things he performs." The Sages answered her: "We will do as you wish." They sent for Jesus, and he came before the Queen. 

The Queen said to him: "I have heard of the terrible deeds you perform; do so before me." Jesus answered her: "I will do all that you say, only I request of you that you do not deliver me into the hands of those wicked men who say of me that I am a bastard." The Queen said to him: "Do not fear." Jesus said: "Bring me a leper and I will heal him." They brought him a leper; he placed his hand upon him, mentioned the **Great Name**, and the man was purified and his flesh became like that of a youth. Jesus said further: "Bring me a dead man." They brought him a dead man; he placed his hand upon him, remembered the **Name**, and the man lived and stood upon his feet. Jesus said: "Regarding me, Isaiah prophesied: *Then the lame shall leap like a deer...*" <note>See Isaiah 35:6.</note>. 

The Queen said to the Sages: "How can you say of this man that he is a sorcerer? Behold, I have seen with my own eyes that he performs deeds like a Son of God!" The Sages answered and said: "Let it not enter the Queen's heart to say such a thing, for surely he is a sorcerer." The Queen said: "Leave my presence, and do not speak such words before me again."

The Sages left the Queen’s presence with troubled souls. One man said to another: "Come, let us be wise against him so that he falls into our hands." One of the Sages answered: "If it seems good to you, let one of us also learn the **Name** and perform deeds like him; perhaps then we will catch him." The matter was good in the eyes of the Sages, and they said: "The man who learns the Name and refutes that bastard, the son of a menstruant, his reward shall be doubled in the world to come."

Perhaps God, in His mercy and great kindness, will deliver that bastard, the son of a menstruant, into my hands." They all answered and said: "The sin be upon us, only act and prosper!"

### Chapter III of the First Part of *Judaism Unmasked*

Judah spoke to the Queen and to all the people: "Do not let your hearts be troubled by all that this **bastard** <note>original: "Mamzer," a term for a child born of an illicit or adulterous union.</note> has done; for even if he makes his nest among the stars, I will bring him down from there." Jesus said to all the people: "Have you not always been a stiff-necked people from the day I first knew you?" Judah replied to him: "Are you still clinging to your impurity? You are a **bastard and the son of an impure woman** <note>original: "Mamzer ben ha-Niddah." This refers to the polemical claim that Jesus was conceived while his mother was ritually impure (Niddah).</note>. Did not our teacher Moses say of you: 'If your brother, the son of your mother, entices you saying...' and 'You shall bring that man out and stone him with stones, and he shall die, and you shall purge the evil'?"

The bastard and son of an impure woman answered him and said: "Did not my forefather Isaiah prophesy concerning me? And the Lord said to me: 'You are my son; today I have begotten you.' And another verse says: 'The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand.' And now I will ascend to my Father who is in heaven and sit at His right hand, and your eyes shall see it—but you, Judah, shall not come there."

Then Jesus pronounced the **Great Name** <term>Shem HaMephorash: the hidden, four-letter name of God, which in this legend Jesus stole from the Temple to perform miracles</term> and it carried him between heaven and earth. Judah also pronounced the Name, and the wind carried him likewise between heaven and earth, and they were both flying in the air of the world. All who saw it wondered greatly. 

Judah then came near and remembered the Name, attempting to seize Jesus to cast him to the ground; Jesus also remembered the Name to try and cast Judah to the ground, and they wrestled with one another. When Judah saw that he could not overcome the works of Jesus, he **discharged** <note>The original Hebrew text "hitach" suggests Judah urinated or discharged bodily fluid upon Jesus to ritually defile him, as the power of the Holy Name was believed to depart in the presence of impurity.</note> upon Jesus, and they both became impure and fell to the earth. They could no longer make use of the Name because they were defiled, until such time as they could immerse themselves in a ritual bath.

They then sentenced Jesus to a death sentence and said to him: "If you wish to be saved, do for us as you did before." But Jesus saw that he could not do it, and he lifted his voice in weeping and said: "My forefather David prophesied of me: 'For your sake we are killed all the day long.'" When his disciples and his wicked company saw this, they gave their lives over to death and fought with the elders of Jerusalem and the Sages, and they helped Jesus escape from them into the city. Jesus hurried and went to the Jordan River. He went further and took two millstones and made them float upon the surface of the water; he sat upon them and caught fish before his company, and they ate.

When the rumor reached Jerusalem, the pious and the Sages mourned and said: "Who is the man who will put his life in his hands and go and take the Great Name away from that bastard and son of an impure woman? We will be his guarantors to bring him to the life of the world to come." Judah said: "I will go." And they said: "Go in peace."

Judah went and disguised himself among the wicked ones. At midnight, God cast a deep sleep upon that bastard, for Judah had adjured the angel appointed over sleep. Judah came to the bastard's tent, took his knife, and cut the flesh of Jesus, and pulled out from it the parchment of the Holy Writing. 

Jesus awoke from his sleep and behold, a spirit terrified him. Jesus trembled greatly and said to his disciples: "Know that my Father in heaven wants to take me to Him, for He said to me: 'Your honor is not among men.'" His disciples said to him: "And what shall become of us?" He said to them: "Blessed are you and blessed is your portion if you listen to my voice, for you shall sit at my right hand with my Father in heaven." They lifted their voices and wept. Jesus said to them: "Do not weep, for there is a reward for your labor, but do not disobey my word." They answered and said: "All that you command, we will do; and any man who disobeys your word shall be put to death." 

Jesus said to them: "If you will listen to my voice, show me kindness and truth by coming with me to Jerusalem. I will disguise myself and come among you so that the people of Jerusalem will not recognize me." Jesus spoke these things with cunning so that he might enter Jerusalem in secret and go into the Temple to **learn the Name** <note>re-learn the pronunciation of the Tetragrammaton to regain his powers</note> again. They did not know his evil thought, and they all answered: "Everything you command us, we will do; we will not turn to the right or the left." He said to them: "Swear to me." And they swore to him, from the smallest to the greatest. They did not know that Judah was among them, for they did not recognize him.

After this, Judah said to the disciples: "Let us make for ourselves identical garments, lest it be known who our master is." The idea seemed good in their eyes, and they did so. They prepared their way to go to Jerusalem to celebrate the **Feast of Unleavened Bread** <note>Passover</note>. When the pious saw Judah, they rejoiced greatly. He said to them: "Tell us everything that happened," for he had gone out from the disciples in secret to the elders of the city and its Sages. Judah told them everything that had happened and how he had removed the Name from that bastard, and they rejoiced greatly. Judah said to them: "If you listen to my voice, I will deliver that bastard into your hands tomorrow." The Sages said to him: "Do you know his coming and going?" Judah said: "I know it. Behold, he will come tomorrow to the Temple to sacrifice the Passover sacrifice. I have sworn to him by the Ten Commandments not to deliver him into your hands. He has two thousand men with him, all dressed in the same garment. You must prepare yourselves tomorrow, and the man to whom I bow and prostrate myself—he is the bastard. You act like men of valor, fight against his company, and seize him." **Simeon ben Shetach** <note>A famous historical Pharisaic scholar and leader of the Sanhedrin, c. 120–40 BCE.</note> and all the Sages and elders rejoiced with great joy and agreed to do according to the words of Judah. And it happened on the next day...

It concludes with Judah plotting with Simeon ben Shetach to identify and arrest Jesus in Jerusalem during Passover.</summary>

The disciples saw this and wept, saying: "See the righteousness of our lord Jesus, that no tree will receive him!" But they did not know that he had placed an oath upon all the trees while the **Name** <note>The Shem HaMephorash, the stolen divine name Jesus used for magic in this legend</note> was still in his hand, because he knew his judgment—that they would judge him according to the Torah, as it is written: "If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree..." <note>Deuteronomy 21:22</note>. Judah saw that no tree would receive him, and he said to the Sages: "Observe the heart of the bastard, for he has sworn an oath to all the trees not to receive him. But look, there is in my garden a **cabbage stalk** <note>original: "kelach shel krow." This is a famous element of the legend where a giant cabbage is used because it is technically an herb/vegetable, not a tree, and thus not covered by Jesus's magical oath.</note>, a very large one, and I will bring it; perhaps it will receive him." The Sages said: "Go, do as you have spoken." Judah ran and brought the stalk.

**Fifthly**, it is claimed that Jesus was first stoned to death and only then hanged, which is a gross untruth, for according to Roman custom, he was nailed to the cross while still alive.

**Sixthly**, it is alleged that Jesus had placed a spell upon all wood while he still possessed the <term>Shem HaMephorash</term> <note>The "Explicit Name" of God, believed in some mystical traditions to grant the speaker power over nature.</note>, so that no wood would bear him, but would instead break under him; and that he was therefore hanged on a large **cabbage stalk**, which Judas brought from his garden. <margin>Why Jesus was condemned to death.</margin> Since it was also mentioned previously that Jesus was condemned to death and executed, we will also investigate, in concluding this chapter, the reasons why this supposedly happened according to the devilish teaching of the Jews; for it should be known that three such reasons are found in their books.

<margin>The first cause.</margin> The first is said to be because, according to their damned opinion, he practiced sorcery. But anyone who knows anything in his defense should come and declare it for him. But nothing was found for his justification, therefore he was hanged on the eve of the Passover feast."** And in the old *Nizzáchon* it reads on page 239: "But know that he was a sorcerer and..."

### Chapter III of the First Part of *Judaism Unmasked*
<meta>catchword: then</meta>

...for they will plague those who do not believe in him; but those who do believe in him will perish in the future world (that is, in eternal life). <note>This sentence completes the Jewish interpretation cited on the previous page, which argued that following Jesus leads to spiritual ruin.</note>

<margin>Refutation of the three causes mentioned above.</margin>
These, according to the wicked Jews’ godless teaching, are the alleged causes why Jesus was condemned to death. However, the claim that he was captured and executed because of committed **sorcery**, **idolatry**, and leading people astray onto false paths is a diabolical falsehood. For as the eternal Son of God and the true Savior of the world, he could commit no sin, as has already been proven above. How then could he have committed sorcery and idolatry, or turned people away from God? The testimony of the Jewish historian **Josephus** <note>referring to the *Testimonium Flavianum*, a passage in Josephus's *Antiquities of the Jews* that mentions Jesus</note> cited above in the second chapter, teaches exactly the opposite.

As for the accusation that he represented himself as a God: we read in **Matthew 26:63 and 64** that when the High Priest adjured him to say whether he was the Christ, the Son of God, he answered, "You have said it." This means as much as, "Yes, I am," as can be clearly seen from **Mark 14:62**. For this reason, the High Priest tore his clothes and said: "He has blasphemed God! What further witness do we need? See, now you have heard his blasphemy. What is your verdict?" And they answered: "He is worthy of death," as seen in **Matthew 26:65, 66** and **Mark 14:63, 64**. 

Christ, however, spoke quite rightly and well in this instance, for he is in truth the eternal Son of God and consequently true God, as will be proven with powerful evidence in the next-following fourth chapter. As noted previously, he did not wish to rescue himself from his enemies’ hands—even though, as an almighty God and Lord, he could easily have done so. Instead, he willingly submitted to the suffering for which he assumed human nature, so that poor sinful mankind might be redeemed from eternal damnation, and so that the **divine decree** <term>Rath-Schluß GOttes: the predestined plan of God</term> (as read in **Acts 2:23 and 4:28**) might be fulfilled. Thus also the holy Apostle Paul writes of him in the **Epistle to the Hebrews**, chapter 2, verses 9 and 10: "But him who for a little while was made lower than the angels, we see—that is Jesus—crowned with honor through the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone. For it was fitting for him, for whom all things exist and through whom all things exist, in bringing many children to glory, to make the **pioneer** <note>original: "Hertzogen," literally Duke or Leader; here referring to the "author" or "captain" of salvation</note> of their salvation perfect through suffering."

<summary>In this passage, Eisenmenger refutes Jewish accusations that Jesus was executed for sorcery or idolatry, arguing instead that his death was a voluntary act of divine sacrifice. He asserts that Jesus’s claim to divinity was true and necessary for the fulfillment of God’s plan for human salvation.</summary>
<keywords>refutation of sorcery, trial of Jesus, High Priest, blasphemy, divinity of Christ, divine decree, Josephus, Epistle to the Hebrews</keywords>

What is said to have happened to Christ after his death.
Aa 3 <note>This "Aa 3" is a signature mark, used by early modern printers to help the bookbinder assemble the pages in the correct sequence.</note>

# Chapter IV.

### In which is shown what is said to have happened to Christ, according to the cursed teachings of the godless Jews, after his suffering and death; and proven that he is the true Messiah, and not merely a human being, but also God: also reporting what is written about Christ in the Turkish Quran. <note>original: "Alcoran"</note>

<margin>What happened to Christ after his suffering according to the teachings of the New Testament.</margin>
The history of the New Testament teaches us that after Jesus gave up his spirit on the cross and passed away, Joseph of Arimathea, with Pilate's permission, placed his body in a new tomb hewn into a rock and rolled a large stone before the door of the tomb. On the next day, however, the high priests and Pharisees went to Pilate and asked him that the tomb might be secured by guards, so that no one could come and take Christ's body away from there, and his disciples would not have cause to say he had risen from the dead; in this, Pilate also complied with them, so that the tomb was well guarded and the stone upon it was sealed, as can be seen in Matthew 27, v. 57, etc. On the third day, he rose again from the dead (Matthew 28, v. 1, etc.; Mark 16, v. 1, etc.; Luke 24, v. 1, etc.; John 20, v. 1, etc.) and thereafter appeared to his disciples at various times and in different places, and spoke with them (Matthew 28, v. 16, etc.; Mark 16, v. 14, etc.; Luke 24, v. 13, etc.; John 20, v. 19, etc.); and after he had reinstated Peter—who had denied him—into his office (John 21, v. 15), and given his apostles the command to preach the Gospel in all the world (Matthew 28, v. 19; Mark 16, v. 15), he ascended into heaven publicly and visibly before the eyes of his disciples (Luke 24, v. 51; Acts 1, v. 9, 10), <note>original: "Actor." for the Latin "Acta Apostolorum," the Acts of the Apostles.</note> where he sits at the right hand of his heavenly Father (Ephesians 1, v. 20; Hebrews 1, v. 3), from whence he shall come again to awaken the dead (Philippians 3, v. 20, 21 and 1 Thessalonians 4, v. 14) and to judge the living and the dead, as is read in Matthew 25, v. 30, 31; Acts 17, v. 31; Romans 2, v. 16; and 14, v. 10.

However, because the malicious Jews interpret the aforementioned verse quite differently nowadays, seeking various excuses within it, they even dare to pretend that the word <term>Shevet</term> <note>Hebrew: שֵׁבֶט</note> does not mean a scepter here, but rather a rod, and the word <term>Mechokek</term> <note>Hebrew: מְחֹקֵק</note> means a staff. They insist that the Hebrew words must be interpreted thus: **The rod shall not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until the Messiah comes.** By this, they want it understood that the Jews will remain in *exilio* <note>Latin: exile</note> or misery, under the rod and the staff of other nations and must be plagued by them, until the Messiah comes, who will deliver them from such misery. 

When they say such things, one can stop their useless mouths by pointing out that in all three of the ancient Chaldean <note>The author uses "Chaldean" to refer to Aramaic</note> translations—which they call the *Targum* or *Targumim*—the word <term>Shevet</term> is taken to mean a royal scepter or worldly dominion, and the word <term>Mechokek</term> is taken to mean the lawgivers or scribes. For in the Chaldean translation of Jonathan, the son of Uzziel <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, a famous scholar of the 1st century</note>, they are translated as follows: <note>original Aramaic: לא פסקן מלכין ושליטין מדבית יהודה וספרין מאלפי אורייתא מזרעיה עד זמן די ייתי מלכא משיחא זעיר בנוי ובידיליה ייתמסון עממיא</note> **that is, Kings and rulers shall not cease from the House of Judah, nor scribes who teach the Law from his seed, until the time that the King Messiah comes, the youngest of his sons, and because of him the nations shall melt away.**

In the Jerusalem Chaldean translation <note>The Targum Yerushalmi</note>, the words read as follows: <note>original Aramaic: לא פסקון מלכין מדבית יהודה אף לא סברין מלפי אורייתא מבני בנוי עד זמן די ייתי מלכא משיחא ודידיה היא מלכותא וליה עתידין דישתעבדון כל מלכותא דארעא</note> **that is, Kings shall not cease from the House of Judah, nor the experts who teach the Law from his grandsons, until the time that the King Messiah comes, to whom the kingdom belongs, and to him all the kingdoms of the earth shall be subject.**

In the Chaldean translation of Onkelos <note>A famous 1st-century convert and scholar</note>, however, it stands thus: <note>original Aramaic: לא יעדי עבד שולטן מדבית יהודה וספרא מבני בנוי עד עלמא עד דייתי משיחא דדיליה היא מלכותא וליה ישתמעון עממיא</note> **that is, The ruler shall never depart from Judah, nor the lawgiver from his grandsons, until the Messiah comes, to whom the kingdom belongs, and to him the nations shall be obedient.**

The Jews dare not contradict these Chaldean translations, for in the book *Shalshelet HaKabbalah* <note>"The Chain of Tradition," a historical work by Gedaliah ibn Yahya ben Joseph</note>, it is written on folio 20, column 1: <margin>What they think of the Chaldean translations of the Holy Scripture.</margin> <note>original Hebrew: התרגום הוא קבלה למשה רבינו עליו השלום מסיני</note> **that is, The Targum, or the Chaldean translation, was received (and learned) by Moses, our teacher—upon whom be peace—from Mount Sinai.**

**Ninthly**, he was to begin preaching the Gospel in Galilee, as can be read in Isaiah 9:1–2. This occurred through JESUS, however, as is to be found in Matthew 4:12, 13, 14, 15, 23; Mark 1:14; Luke 4:14, 15; and John 4:43.

**Twelfthly**, although he performed so many and magnificent miracles, his preaching was nevertheless to be rejected by most Jews, as can be read in Isaiah 49:4 and 53:1. Because of this, according to the words of Isaiah 53:3, he was to be entirely despised and worthless, and according to Psalm 22:6, a mockery of the people and an object of contempt for the nation. Christ, however, though he performed very many miracles, was indeed despised by most Jews and his preaching rejected, so much so that those of Nazareth pushed him out of the city (Luke 4:16 etc.), the inhabitants of Jerusalem wanted to stone him (John 10:30), and he was finally executed as a supposed evildoer.

**Thirteenthly**, he was to be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to both houses of Israel, as was prophesied in Isaiah 8:14. JESUS, however, was such a person, by whom many were offended, as is to be read in Luke 2:34, Romans 9:32, and 1 Peter 2:8.

**Fourteenthly**, he was to make his entry into Jerusalem riding upon a donkey, as seen in Zechariah 9:9. This was fulfilled in JESUS, as taught in Matthew 21:2 etc. and John 12:14 etc.

JESUS, however, was buried as a rich man, in that a wealthy man—namely Joseph of Arimathea—had him placed in his own new tomb, which had been made for himself (Matthew 27:57, Mark 15:43, and Luke 23:50); from there he rose again on the third day and thus did not decay (Matthew 28:1 etc., Mark 16:1 etc., Luke 24:1 etc.); shortly thereafter he ascended to Heaven (Luke 24:50, 51, Acts 1:9) and sits at the right hand of God (Ephesians 1:20, Hebrews 1:3, 13, and 1 Peter 3:22).

### Chapter IV of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.
<meta>catchword: after-</meta>

Jehovah is not shared (or is not communicated to others) and His simplicity has no end. And in the book *Zohar Chadash* <note>The "New Zohar," a collection of Kabbalistic writings</note>, on folio 5, column 2, in the *Midrash Ne'elam* <note>The "Hidden Midrash," a specific section of the Zohar</note>, it is taught: <gloss>Rabbi Abhu said: "Come and see how much the Holy One, blessed be He, cared for the honor of His great name Jehovah; for this is His actual name; but the name Elohim is shared with the rest of the creatures."</note> <note>original Hebrew: אמר רבי אבהו בוא וראה כמה חשש הק"בה על כבוד שמו הגדול שהוא יהוד כי זהו שמו ממש אבל שם אלהים משותף הוא על יתר הנבראים</note> In this, Rabbi David Kimchi <note>A famous medieval Jewish biblical commentator and grammarian, also known as Radak</note> also agrees when he writes the following concerning the words of Hosea 12:6—**"But Jehovah is the God of Hosts; Jehovah is His name"**: <gloss>In this name He has no fellowship with any other.</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: בזה השם אינו משותף עם זולתו</note> So also Rabbi Joseph Albo <note>A 15th-century Spanish Jewish philosopher</note> in his *Sefer Ikkarim* (or *Ikkorim*), under the title *Ma'amar Sheni* <note>Second Treatise</note>, in the 28th chapter, folio 54, column 1, expresses himself in this way: <gloss>The name which is written with the Yod, He, Vav, He (that is, the name Jehovah) is that which is called **Shem HaMephorash** <term>Shem HaMephorash</term> <note>Meaning the "Explicit" or "Distinct" Name; the unique, four-letter name of God known as the Tetragrammaton</note>, which is to say, the separated name, etc. The meaning of **Shem HaMephorash** is thus a name that is separated from others and is unique to the Blessed One among all names. This occurs because the other names are spoken of the Blessed One and also of others, since they are names given to the Blessed One either in view of certain works or in view of another consideration, without the necessary consequence of the Divine Being. Such a one is the name **Elohim**, which indicates power or authority; therefore it is spoken of Him and of others, for the angels and the judges are also called **Elohim**. Likewise, the name **Adonai**, which signifies a lordship, is given to Him and to others.
