afterwards (by others) be said. But the name of four letters (that is, the name Jehovah, which in the Hebrew language is written with four letters, namely Yod, He, Vav, and He) can impossibly belong to any other in any way, because it is a name which is given to GOD in respect of the necessary consequence or result of His (divine) essence. These are the words of Rabbi Joseph Albo. Thus also teaches Rabbi Isaac Abarbenel <note>A prominent Portuguese Jewish statesman, philosopher, and Bible commentator (1437–1508)</note> in his little book *Miphalóth* (or *Miphalos*) *Elohím* <note>original Hebrew: מפעלות אלהים, meaning "Works of God"</note>, folio 79, column 4, at the end, and folio 80, column 1, where he reports: <gloss>The name Yod, He, Vav, He will be spoken of in no way by anyone else except by the First Cause (that is, GOD).</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: שם יוד ה' וא' ה' לא יאמר כי אם על הסבה הראשונה</note> And this is likewise proven at length in the book *Móre Nevochím* <note>Maimonides' "Guide for the Perplexed," the most influential work of medieval Jewish philosophy</note>, in the first part, chapter 61, as well as in the two commentaries upon it, namely Ephodi and Shem Tov.

<margin>The origin of the name Jehovah shows that it belongs to no creature.</margin>
So also the origin of this name, namely the word *havà* <note>original Hebrew: הוה</note>, which means *to be*, shows that it cannot be appropriated by any creature; for by this it is not only taught that God gives all things their essence and makes them to be, as is written in the book *Reschith* (or *Réschis*) *chochma* <note>"The Beginning of Wisdom," a 16th-century kabbalistic moral treatise</note> under the title *Scháar hajira*, chapter 3, folio 11, column 1, where the words read thus: <gloss>GOD is called by this name Jehovah because He has given all things their essence.</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: השם הזה יהוה נקרא הוא יתברך מצד שהיווה כל ההויות</note> Rather, it also indicates the eternity of GOD; therefore, in the aforementioned book *Móre Nevochím*, folio 43, column 2, in the 61st chapter of the first part, it is read in the commentary of Shem Tov: <gloss>Know that the name Jehovah teaches that He was, is, and will be.</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: דע כי שם יי' יורה על שהוא היה והווה ויהיה</note> For this reason, Rabbi Bechai <note>Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish rabbi and commentator</note> also writes in his interpretation of the 5 books of Moses, folio 10, column 3, in the portion *Bereschíth*: <gloss>The *Shem hamjuchád*, or the proper name (namely Jehovah), gives witness to the eternity and the essence of GOD, blessed be He.</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: שם המיוחד מעיד על קדמותו ומציאותו יתברך</note>

<margin>The name Jehovah is signified in many ways.</margin>
Because of this, it is also called by the Rabbis *Shem hahávaja*, that is, **the Name of Essence**; *Shem haëzem*, that is, **the Name of Substance**; *Shem hannichbad*, that is, **the Glorious Name**; *Shem hannóra*, that is, **the Awesome Name**; *Shem haggadól*, that is, **the Great Name**; *Shem hannéelam*, that is, **the Hidden Name**; *Shem hammúfla*, that is, **the Wonderful Name**; *Shem hammjuchád*, that is, **the Proper or Unique Name**; and *Shem hammeülle*, that is, **the Praised Name**; also *par excellence* <note>original Greek: κατ' ἐξοχὴν</note>—that is, because of its glory—it is called simply *Haschém*, that is, **The Name**.

# Chapter 5.

### In which the question is discussed: whether by that Jesus, of whom mention is made in the Talmud in several places, our Savior JESUS Christ is understood by the Jews, or whether he was another person who was also named Jesus.

<margin>The Jews deny that Christ is that Jesus mentioned in the Talmud.</margin> When the godless Jews <note>Eisenmenger uses "godless" (gottlosen) in the polemical style of 17th-century Christian theologians who viewed Jewish rejection of Christ as a moral failing.</note> are confronted with the fact that our Savior JESUS is so greatly blasphemed and reviled in their Talmud, they usually take refuge and make their excuse by saying that the Jesus mentioned therein is not the same one whom Christians hold to be the true Messiah, but another. ### Of the First Part of Discovered Judaism, Chapter 5.

The sixth generation was Shemaya and Abtalion <note>The OCR "Saeiah Zabtion" refers to the famous "Pairs" (Zugot) of Jewish scholars, Shemaya and Abtalion, who led the Sanhedrin.</note>.

The seventh generation was Hillel and Shammai. They lived in the final years of King Herod. In those times, Jesus the Nazarene <note>Original: "Jeshua Notzri"</note> was born in Bethlehem in Judea. On this point, Christians and Jews agree. Thus, there are two generations or lifetimes between Joshua ben Perachiah—who is said to have been the teacher of the Talmudic Yeshu—and the time of Hillel and Shammai during the reign of Herod. According to this calculation, there must be over 150 years between Rabbi Joshua ben Perachiah and the birth of the Christian Messiah. If they were the same person, Jesus the Nazarene would have been over 150 years old when he was judged, yet it is known that he was no more than 33 years old. This is my strong proof that the Yeshu written about in the Talmud was a different person entirely.

He claims that from that time until the time Rabbi Jechiel held the Disputation with the convert Nicholas <note>Nicholas Donin.</note>, 1,472 years had passed, but according to the Christians' reckoning, only 1,240 years had passed. To this I answer that Rabbi Jechiel acted deceitfully here by stating that one was 232 years before the other, when in fact, according to Rabbi Solomon Zevi’s own reckoning (as shown on pages 234 and 235), no more than 130 years are said to have passed between the two, and Rabbi Joshua ben Perachiah lived only 207 years before the destruction of the Second Temple. Furthermore, the Jews do not believe our annual reckoning, as will be proven hereafter from Abraham ibn Ezra and Isaac Abarbanel; how then can Rabbi Jechiel appeal here to our chronology? Just as he acted craftily in this matter (as mentioned above on page 199) and alleged against his better knowledge that the Jesus who is said to be tormented in boiling filth in hell is not JESUS the Nazarene, but rather a "Jesus Gereda" <note>Eisenmenger argues this is a fictitious name invented by Jewish apologists to deflect the charge of blasphemy against Jesus.</note> according to Jewish teaching—though there was never anyone named Jesus Gereda—he has likewise here pushed the time in which Rabbi Joshua ben Perachiah lived far back and appealed to the Christian chronology, even though he knew full well that Rabbi Joshua did not live so long before, and that our chronology is considered false by the Jews.

<note>The text begins mid-sentence, completing a thought from the previous page.</note> ...fled; <note>The OCR "fen" likely completes "entloffen" or a similar verb meaning "fled."</note> thus Rabbi Joshua, the son of Perachiah, fled with his disciple Jesus to Alexandria in Egypt; but they later returned to Jerusalem, and he (Jesus) was hanged 269 years after the building of the Temple <note>According to the traditional Jewish counting of the Second Temple era.</note>, which occurred 151 years before the destruction <note>This Jewish chronology places the death of Jesus around 81 BC, much earlier than the Christian date of approx. 33 AD.</note>. Thus the sages who lived at that time, as well as his friends and relatives, gave witness to this: how then should we believe the opposite from the mouths of men (meaning the Christians) who did not know him, nor were present there? 

In order to be able to say that this belief was intentionally created—to prove that the Temple was destroyed because of the sin of killing Jesus the Nazarene—they (namely, the Christians) say that he was hanged shortly before the destruction of the Temple. We, however, do not wish to depart from the truth and the tradition <term>mündlichen Lehre</term> <note>Oral teaching or tradition, specifically referring to the Masorah or Talmudic tradition.</note> of our fathers, who did not falsify the matter, but recounted everything exactly as it happened, and added nothing to it, nor took anything away from it. These are the words of Abarbenel <note>Isaac Abarbenel (1437–1508), a Jewish statesman and commentator.</note>, from which it is well to note that he writes that the Jews learned from their fathers that Jesus Christ was in Egypt with his teacher, Rabbi Joshua, the son of Perachiah, and that the Christians are wrong when they say that Jesus was hanged only 42 years before the destruction of the Temple. Regarding the preceding, the same author writes further as follows: <note>original Hebrew: "אבל בעבור שיש לומר שהיה אותו תלמיד ישוע אחר לכן לא עשינו עקר מכל בזה הפסק וקבלנו דעתם בזה"</note> **However, because it can be said that this disciple (of Rabbi Joshua, the son of Perachiah) was another Jesus, we have therefore made no major issue of this dispute and have accepted their (the Christians') opinion in this matter.** 

Abarbenel does not intend to imply here that he has accepted the Christians' opinion as true, for he rejected it as false and untrue in the preceding text—otherwise, he would have contradicted himself. Rather, he only wanted to indicate that even if the Christians' statement were true, the calculation of the "seventy weeks" of Daniel <note>A reference to the prophecy in Daniel 9, often used by Christians to prove the timing of the Messiah.</note> still would not agree with it.

"And behold, these beliefs have evolved from error to error, as is seen from the words of our Sages (may their memory be a blessing) scattered throughout the Talmud, such as this which agrees with their words here in the margin. And even though in the whole Talmud only the name **Yeshu** <note>The Hebrew spelling י-ש-ו (Y-S-W), often interpreted polemically as an acronym for "may his name be erased."</note> is found, perhaps they intentionally omitted the [letter] *Ayin* <note>The final letter of the name Yeshua (י-ש-ו-ע).</note>. And in their writings, I found that they call him **Yeshua**. And he is called in our language 'the Nazarene' because he was from the city of Nazareth. For thus it is in the Jerusalem translation of those who sanctify and purify themselves and worship him, and they call him **Christ**, and after his name they are called **Christians**, and this is the term for 'Messiah' in the foreign tongue."

# Whether Mention is Made of Our Savior in the Talmud.

And in the Gospel <note>original: "Aven Gilyon," a derogatory pun used in the Talmud for the Greek *Evangelion*, literally meaning "Sheet of Iniquity."</note> it is written that his name was Yeshu the Nazarene <note>original: "Yeshu Notzri"</note>, and so forth. And in the Talmud, we find in the chapter "In Three Periods" <note>Referring to Tractate Taanit</note> that the men of the priestly watch would not fast on the first day of the week. Likewise, it is said in the chapter "Before Their Festivals" <note>Tractate Avodah Zarah</note>, according to the words of Rabbi Ishmael, that the day of the Nazarene <note>original: "Yom Notzri," referring to Sunday</note> is always forbidden. For he used to forbid trading with the Gentiles three days before their festivals and three days after, as well as the festival day itself. Therefore, according to his opinion, it was forbidden to trade with them at any time. And it became clear that this nation is called "Nazarenes" <note>original: "Nozrim," meaning Christians</note> after Yeshu the Nazarene.

Furthermore, it is written in the Gospel that Jeremiah spoke of them when he said: *For there shall be a day that the watchmen <note>original: "Nozrim"</note> upon the mount Ephraim shall cry* <note>Jeremiah 31:6</note>. They acknowledge that his name was Yeshu the Nazarene, just as it is written in the Talmud, and that they are called Nazarenes because they followed after him. And in the chapter "The Verdict is Finalized" <note>Tractate Sanhedrin</note>, they said that Yeshu was hanged on the Eve of Passover. This is also found in the Gospel, that he was hanged on the Eve of Passover, though there is some confusion among them; for one night before his hanging, he ate with his disciples and blessed the bread and wine according to the custom of Israel, telling them, "This is my body" and "The wine is my blood." Because of these words, the service of the wafer and their libation of wine became a practice among them.

However, a dispute arose among them: the Greeks make the wafer from leavened bread <note>original: "Chometz"</note>, while the Romans and those who follow them to the ends of the West—who are under the faith of the Pope and the law of his dominion—make it from unleavened bread <note>original: "Matzah"</note>. Because of this dispute, they hate one another, for each considers the other a heretic for disagreeing. The words of the Greeks seem more consistent with their own faith, for before the Eve of Passover, Israel does not yet eat unleavened bread, but rather leavened bread. I have already written that they do this so as not to follow our statutes, for we offer the meal offering as unleavened bread and not leavened.

They also disagree regarding their baptism <note>term: "Tevilah" - ritual immersion</note>. The Greeks immerse their whole bodies, while the Romans immerse only their heads. In this too, the Greeks are more correct according to their own faith, for when John <note>original: "Yochanan"</note> baptized Yeshu in the Jordan, he immersed his entire body, as mentioned in the Gospel.

Our Sages of blessed memory also said in the chapter "The Verdict is Finalized" that a herald went out before him for forty days, crying: "Yeshu goes forth to be stoned; let anyone who knows anything in his favor come forward and testify." There is a hint of this in their own practices, for they fast before Passover, abstaining from everything that comes from living creatures upon the earth, such as meat, cheese, and eggs. Their fast begins from the ninth hour of the day, because his hanging occurred at that hour. These days are called *Quadragesima* <note>original: "Koreshma," referring to the forty days of Lent</note>. Confusion has taken hold of them, for they intend this to mean forty, yet they fast for forty-nine days. Just as Israel observes a festival day after Passover, they begin their fasting seven weeks before Passover. This is an error even by their own logic, for they say that Yeshu fasted for forty days and grew hungry, and the Devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread." They claim they begin the fast forty days prior, plus six days to account for the six feast days within those forty when they do not fast, but they do not escape the confusion, for Yeshu intended to fast.

In that same mentioned chapter, our Sages of blessed memory said that Yeshu was sentenced to death because he practiced sorcery and enticed and led Israel astray. This is also stated in the chapters "Chelek" and "The Beheaded Heifer." Likewise, it is written in the Gospel that they claimed Yeshu performed deeds by the power of Beelzebub, which is the "Lord of Sorcery."

It is also written in the Gospel that a dispute arose among the Jews in Jerusalem. Some said that Yeshu was a fool and possessed by a demon, while others said, "He is no fool, and his deeds prove it." As Yeshu was walking in the Temple in Solomon’s Porch, the Jews said to him, "How long will you keep us in suspense? Tell us openly if you are the Messiah or not." Yeshu answered them: "What I tell you, you do not believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name testify of me, but you do not believe because you are not of my sheep. My sheep hear my voice; I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish, nor shall anyone snatch them from my hand. I and the Father are one." These are the words of Yeshu.

When they heard these words, they wanted to stone him. He said to them, "For which of the many good works I have shown you from my Father do you stone me?" They answered him, "We do not stone you for your good works, but for blasphemy; because you, being a man, make yourself God." Yeshu replied, "Is it not written in your Law, 'I said, you are gods'? If He called them gods to whom the word of God came, do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world that he blasphemes because he said, 'I am the Son of God'?" Thus far is written in the Gospel. It is also written that when Yeshu entered Jerusalem, many of the children of Israel, boys and girls, came out to meet him and honored him, saying to him:

### Chapter 5 of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked

...Hoshea said so. And likewise, when he was apprehended by the hands of Israel, the High Priest said to him: "Tell us if you are the Son of God." And he answered them and said: "Truly I say to you, the Son of Man shall sit at the right hand of God and come with the clouds of heaven." Then the High Priest tore his garments. And it is written there that they said to Caesar’s official, whose name was Pilate, that this man was liable for death according to the Law <note>The Torah</note> because he said he was the Son of God, and for this, they judged him to death.

Behold, they agree with the words of our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: "Zal," an abbreviation for *Zichronam Livracha*</note> that they handed him over by law and judged him with contempt because he was a "seducer" <note>original: *mesit*, a legal term for one who leads others to idolatry</note> who incited Israel to believe in him. And even though some confusion has fallen among them—for according to the words of our Sages, he did not make himself a god, but rather he set up a brick <note>original: *leveinah*; in some Talmudic accounts, this refers to an act of idolatry involving a sun-dried brick</note> and bowed down to it, misleading many of Israel into the worship of Mercury <note>original: *Markulis*, the Roman god Mercurius, often used in the Talmud to represent pagan stone-worship</note> as mentioned in the chapter "The Portion" <note>Tractate Sanhedrin, Chapter 11</note> and the chapter "The Beheaded Heifer" <note>Tractate Sotah, Chapter 9</note>—in the Gospel <note>original: *Aven Gilyon*, a pun on the Greek *Evangelion* meaning "Sheet of Iniquity"</note> nothing of this is mentioned, only that he said of himself that he was the Son of God. Nevertheless, because of the incitement to idolatry, Israel judged him to be killed, even according to their own words.

In the chapter "The Damages" <note>Tractate Gittin, Chapter 5</note>, they said that Onkelos raised Jesus by necromancy <note>original: *ov*, a medium</note> and asked him about the condition of Israel. He said to him: "Seek their good, do not seek their harm; whoever touches them touches the apple of His eye." Likewise, it is found written for them that Jesus said: "Whoever makes his fellow angry is liable for judgment; and whoever says 'Raca' <note>An Aramaic term of contempt meaning 'empty-head'</note> to him is liable to the court; and whoever calls him 'fool' is liable for Hell." And they also asked what his judgment was, and he replied—regarding what he truly thought—that it was not his intention that they should worship him with that service or recognize him through it, or that the priests should eat him <note>likely a polemical reference to the Eucharist</note>. Yet according to their error, he is judged in "boiling excrement" <note>A harsh theological punishment described in Tractate Gittin 57a for those who mocked the words of the Sages</note>. From this, it appears the Sages spoke of those things that remain hidden.

In the chapter "The Verdict is Finalized" <note>Tractate Sanhedrin, Chapter 6</note>, they said that Jesus the Nazarene had five disciples and all of them were killed. But they [the Christians] count twelve for him; however, they divided them, making four of them "Evangelists" because each of them wrote a Gospel <note>original: *Aven Gilyon*</note from the story of his teachings from the time of his birth until his hanging. The rest they called "Apostles" <note>original: *Apostolish*, meaning messengers or emissaries</note>. These are the ones mentioned in the Talmud: Mattai, Nakai, Netzer, Buni, and Todah; all were killed for the sake of Jesus, as mentioned there. And thus it is found written for them that his disciples were killed. This agrees with some of their own "confusions," for even from the words of his disciples in their Gospel, there is no agreement in all matters; there are contradictions among them, whether due to forgetfulness or an intentional desire to beautify the stories.

They say that he was born in Bethlehem Ephratah and boast of this because of what was said: *But you, Bethlehem Ephratah, though you are small among the thousands of Judah, out of you shall come forth to Me the one to be Ruler in Israel* <note>Micah 5:1</note>. It is true that this verse was said concerning the King Messiah, but it does not say he would be born in Bethlehem, only that he is of the lineage of the one who was born in Bethlehem—namely David son of Jesse, the Bethlehemite. This is why it is said, *whose goings forth are from of old*, meaning his lineage is from ancient days. If this were said of Jesus, how could it say he was a ruler over Israel? On the contrary, they ruled over him. Furthermore, the whole nation agrees on the matter of Jesus. 

They have further misinterpreted a teaching found in the Midrash on Lamentations, which says the King Messiah was born on the day of the Destruction in Bethlehem and his name was Menachem <note>meaning 'Comforter'</note>, and that winds and whirlwinds came and carried him away. All of this contradicts their words, for Jesus was born before the Destruction, his name was not Menachem, and winds did not carry him away; rather, he perished at the hands of Israel. In the words of our Sages, his place of birth is not explicitly stated, but since they called him "Jesus the Nazarene" and not "Jesus the Bethlehemite," and as it is written "Jesus of Nazareth," it implies he was born in the place of Nazareth, as written in the Jerusalem Targum.

They also say that because of fear, his mother fled to Egypt, and they misinterpret the verse: *Out of Egypt I called My son* <note>Hosea 11:1</note>, even though this verse was said regarding Israel, as the beginning of the verse indicates: *When Israel was a youth, I loved him*. So too it is written in the Torah: *Let My son go, that he may serve Me*. But there is a hint in the words of our Sages that he was in Egypt, and there he learned to perform his deeds, which Israel claimed he did by the power of Beelzebub, as stated in the Gospel. 

The hint found by the Sages in this matter is what they said in the chapter "The Builder" <note>Tractate Shabbat, Chapter 12</note>: Rabbi Eliezer said to the Sages, "Did not the son of Stada <note>A name used in the Talmud to refer to Jesus or a figure conflated with him</note> bring sorcery <note>original: *keshafim*</note> out of Egypt by a scratch on his flesh?" They said to him, "He was a fool." Behold, this agrees with the statement of the Gospel in three things: First, his coming to Egypt, which agrees with what they said in Chapter 8 <note>of Sanhedrin</note> that Jesus went to Egypt with Joshua ben Perachiah. Second, regarding the claim that he operated through sorcery by the power of Beelzebub. Third, that he was a fool <note>or "madman"</note>. This "Son of Stada" they spoke of appears to be the Jesus mentioned in the Talmud and the Gospel. Likewise, in the chapter "Four Deaths of the Court" <note>Tractate Sanhedrin, Chapter 7</note>, they say that Stada is Mary Magdalene <note>original: *Miriam Megadla Nashaya*, literally Mary the women's hairdresser</note>, and even though there is another Mary Magdalene mentioned in the Talmud in the first chapter of Chagigah, she is not the one who is the mother of Jesus called Stada...

For she lived during the time of the Talmud in the days of Rav Bibi bar Abaye, who was among the last of the *Amoraim* <note>The "Speakers" or "Explainers"—rabbis who lived roughly between 200 and 500 CE and composed the Gemara</note>. And in the chapter "One who Miscarries" <note>Tractate Niddah, Chapter 3</note>, it says that Rav Bibi bar Abaye lived in the days of Rav Yochanan, yet this occurred during the time of the Second Temple in the days of the first *Tannaim* <note>The "Repeaters" or "Teachers"—rabbis from the era of the Mishna, roughly 10–220 CE</note>. It is possible that there were two women with the same name, and they lived in different eras, because *Magdala Neshaia* means "the one who braids the hair of women." Their stories have become confused because they say that a relative of Jesus was named Mary Magdalene—they derived "Magdalene" from the word for "Tower" <note>Hebrew: *Migdal*</note> and applied this title to the relative because they shared the same proper name, Mary.

Likewise, our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: *Zal*</note> said that the adulterer <note>original: *Moel*</note> was named Pappos ben Yehuda. Even though it is recorded in the Talmud that Pappos ben Yehuda lived in the time of Rabbi Akiva, near the time of the Temple's destruction, perhaps this was a different man or he lived a very long life. They say in the *Aven Gilyon* <note>original: "Naughty Scroll," a derogatory Jewish pun on the Greek *Evangelion* or Gospel</note> that his betrothed was named Joseph. Perhaps they are one and the same, for at that time they nicknamed Joseph "Pappos." Whether his father's name was Yehuda, or Jacob as it is written in the Gospel, or some other name, confusion fell among them because they do not agree on his father's era. Eventually, later writers were forced to explain that Joseph’s father performed a levirate marriage with his brother's wife <note>A biblical practice where a man marries his deceased brother's widow</note>. Some attributed the son to the levir father, and others to the deceased brother.

They also said that the writers of the genealogy of Jesus suffered great difficulty because King Herod prevented the people from recording their genealogies. If this is true, it was because Herod was a slave <note>A common Talmudic claim that Herod the Great was of humble/servile Edomite origin</note>, as said in the first chapter of *Bava Batra*, and it was a great disgrace to him when the people of Israel could trace their ancestry back to their fathers while he himself had no Israelite lineage.

There in the Gemara <note>The commentary portion of the Talmud</note>, our Sages of blessed memory said that she became pregnant by Pandera <note>original: *Mendira*</note>, and therefore they called Mary "Stada," which is a contraction of *Stat Da*—"This one deviated" from her husband. They also say that Mary Magdalene was a prostitute who repented. While they <note>Christian authors</note> deny that this refers to the mother of Jesus, it actually strengthens the words of our Sages who make such claims about her. The point of agreement between us would be that "Mary the Hair-braider" was involved in adultery; the disagreement is whether she was the mother of Jesus or merely a relative. They claim that the mother of Jesus was never intimately known and remained a virgin before and after the birth. 

Regarding this Pandera, Maimonides <note>original: *Rambam*</note> wrote that he was a Gentile. It is well known from Talmudic laws that if a Gentile lies with a daughter of Israel—whether by force or by her own will, and even if she is married—the child is considered "kosher" <note>Legitimate/fit</note>. And she was forced, for it was the custom in Israel that a man was allowed to be secluded with his betrothed, as mentioned in the first chapter of *Ketubot*. For this reason, he could not claim the "plea of virginity" <note>A legal claim in Jewish law regarding the state of a bride</note>. This Joseph was accustomed to being alone with her every night upon leaving the house of study; one night Pandera came, and she thought he was her betrothed, and thus she conceived. In those days, Pandera was a carpenter. Nothing of this is mentioned in the Gospel, for they deny she was touched by any man, but in some of their books, it is written that Jesus himself was a carpenter.

This "Ben Stada" who is the "Son of Pandera" appears from the words of our Sages to be Jesus the Nazarene. Indeed, they said in Tractate *Avodah Zarah* <note>"Idolatry"</note>, Chapter 2: A story is told of Ben Dama, the nephew of Rabbi Ishmael, regarding how they do not conduct business with heretics <note>original: *Minim*, referring to early Christians</note> nor seek healing from them, even to save a life, for heresy is "alluring" <note>original: *deshani minut demashka*</note>. And this Jacob of Kephar Sechania, who was a heretic, was one of the disciples of Jesus. For it is said there in the first chapter: "What is the rule for using the hire of a harlot to build a latrine for the High Priest?" Jacob of Kephar Sechania said: "From the hire of a harlot she gathered it, and unto the hire of a harlot it shall return; from a place of filth it came, and to a place of filth it shall go." 

This "Jesus" whose name Jacob of Kephar Sechania invoked is Jesus the son of Pandera. So it is said in the Jerusalem Talmud: A story is told of Joshua ben Dama who was bitten by a snake, and Jacob of Kephar Sechania came to heal him in the name of Jesus son of Pandera. There is another similar story in the Jerusalem Talmud where a heretic whispered a charm in the name of Jesus son of Pandera. This agrees with what is written in the Gospel, where he told them that in his name they would cast out demons, drive away harmful spirits, take up serpents in their hands, and if they drank any deadly poison it would not hurt them, and they would lay their hands on the sick and they would recover. It appears that this Jacob of Kephar Sechania never saw Jesus but followed his faith. From all this, it appears that Ben Stada, who is the son of Pandera, is the Jesus the Nazarene of whom our Sages spoke in agreement with the Gospel...

# Chapter VI.

### In which it is shown in what manner God the Holy Spirit is blasphemed by the godless Jews, and proven against them that He is God.

Just as God the Father and God the Son—by virtue of what was shown in the preceding chapters—are terribly blasphemed and reviled by the wicked Jews through the instigation of the troublesome Devil, so too is God the Holy Spirit not left unattacked. Instead, he is called the "unclean spirit," <note>original: "Ruach Tumah." This is a derogatory inversion of "Ruach Ha-Kodesh" (the Holy Spirit).</note> and indeed for this reason: because we consider him the third person of the Most Holy Trinity <term>Trinity: the Christian doctrine that God exists as three persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—while remaining one being.</term>; therefore in the old *Nizzachon* <note>original: "Sefer Nizzachon," a medieval Jewish polemical work written to counter Christian missionary arguments.</note> page 12, regarding the words of Genesis 18:2, **And behold, three men stood before him**, it is written thus:

<margin>The Holy Spirit is called the unclean spirit.</margin>

**The heretics** <note>original: "Ha-Minim," a term used in Jewish texts to refer to sectarians, often specifically Christians.</note> **(namely the Christians) say: he saw three and prayed to one, and these are the Father, and the Son, and the unclean spirit—meaning the Holy Spirit; he saw these three as one and prayed to him.** <note>original: "Ha-Minim omrim re’eh gimmel ve-hitpalel le-echad..."</note> And on page 13, it follows: **But if they wish to persist in their error, that it was the Father and the Son, as well as the unclean spirit—which they call the Holy Spirit—(then one can ask them) why did he then place food before them? Does God then eat and drink?** <note>This Jewish argument seeks to disprove the divinity of the "three men" (angels) visited by Abraham by pointing out that they consumed food.</note> Furthermore, in the said book on page 59, regarding the words of Joshua 22:22, **The mighty God, God the LORD, the mighty God, God the LORD knows**, it is written: **Here the shaven ones** <note>original: "Gelachim," literally "the shorn ones," a derogatory term for tonsured Catholic priests or monks.</note> **say that these three names (El, that is, the mighty God; Elohim, that is, God; Jehovah, that is, the LORD) have a reference to the Father, Son, and the unclean spirit.** Further, on page 142 of the same, the following is read: **It is written among them in the Gospel of Luke: Whoever sins against the Father shall find forgiveness; against the Son shall find forgiveness; but against the unclean spirit, he shall not find forgiveness, neither in this world nor in the world to come. And if all three are one, why shall he not find forgiveness for the unclean spirit?** <note>original: "Ketiv lahen be-Sefer Lukash..." This references Luke 12:10, though the author of the Nizzachon uses the derogatory "unclean spirit" and questions why the Holy Spirit's sin is singled out if the Trinity is truly "One."</note>

# Chapter VI.
### In which it is shown in what manner God the Holy Spirit is blasphemed by the godless Jews, and proven against them that He is God.

Just as God the Father and God the Son—according to what was shown in the preceding chapters—are terribly blasphemed and reviled by the wicked Jews through the instigation of the wretched Devil, so also is God the Holy Spirit not left unattacked. Instead, he is called the "unclean spirit," <note>The Hebrew term used is *Ruach Tumah*, a deliberate parody of *Ruach Ha-Kodesh* (Holy Spirit).</note> specifically for the reason that we hold Him to be the third person of the most Holy Trinity. Therefore, in the old *Nizzáchon* <note>The *Sefer Nizzachon Yashar*, a medieval Jewish polemical work written to counter Christian missionary efforts.</note> on page 12, regarding the words of Genesis 18:2, **And behold, three men stood before him**, it is written thus:
<margin>The Holy Spirit is called the unclean spirit.</margin>
**The heretics (namely the Christians) say: See, he saw three and prayed to one; and these are the Father, the Son, and the unclean spirit—by which they mean the Holy Spirit. He saw these three as one, and prayed to him.** And there follows on page 13: **But if they wish to persist in their error, that it was the Father and the Son, as well as the unclean spirit (which is called the Holy Spirit by them), then one can ask them: why then did he set food before them? Does God then also eat and drink?** Furthermore, in the thought-of book on page 59, regarding the words of Joshua 22:22, **The mighty God, God the LORD, the mighty God, God the LORD knows**, it is written: **Here the shaven ones <note>term: "shorn" or "shaven" (Hebrew: *Gelahim*). A derogatory Jewish term for Christian priests, referring to the tonsure (the practice of shaving the top of the head).</note> say that these three names (El, that is, the mighty God; Elohim, that is, God; Jehovah, that is, the LORD) signify the Father, Son, and the unclean spirit.** Further, on page 142 of the same work, the following is read: **It is written for them in the Gospel of Luke: Whoever sins against the Father shall find forgiveness; whoever sins against the Son shall find forgiveness; but whoever sins against the unclean spirit shall find no forgiveness, neither in this world nor in the world to come. And if all three are one, why is there no forgiveness for the one who sins against the unclean spirit?** That is: **It stands written among them in the Gospel of Luke: He who sins against the Father finds forgiveness: he who [sins] against the Son**

...and the words sound in this manner: <note>original: "רבי פנחס אומר שרתה רוח הקודש על יוסף מנעוריו ועד יום מותו..."</note> that is, **Rabbi Pinchas says: The Holy Spirit dwelt upon Joseph from his youth until the day of his death, and guided him in all matters of wisdom, just as a shepherd who leads his sheep; as it is said (Psalm 80:2): "Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock." It should also be noted here that the Holy Spirit is called the "Shepherd of Israel" by Rabbi Eliezer; however, the Shepherd of Israel is the Lord God, as can be read in Psalm 23:1, Jeremiah 31:10, and Micah 7:14. Likewise, Isaiah 63:10 states that the Israelites embittered the Holy Spirit, which is said of God in Psalm 88:40.** <note>Eisenmenger cites Psalm 88:40, though the biblical verse describing the Israelites' rebellion in the desert is Psalm 78:40; this may be a printer's error in the original text.</note>

<margin>The Holy Spirit is called Shekhinah.</margin>
But it is also clearly to be proven from the Jews' own books that the Holy Spirit is God, for He is called by them <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>Hebrew: שכינה, referring to the "Divine Indwelling" or Presence of God on earth.</note>, which word signifies the Divine Dwelling and God Himself. For this reason, in the book **Pardes Rimmonim** <note>The "Orchard of Pomegranates," a major Kabbalistic work by Moses Cordovero (1522–1570).</note>, in the preface, in the first column, as well as in the book **Tikkunei ha-Zohar** <note>A collection of seventy commentaries on the first word of the Torah, belonging to the Zohar literature.</note>, folio 6, column 2, where the Law is discussed, it is written thus: <note>original: "כל אלין דלא משתדלין בה לשמה..."</note> that is, **Upon all those who do not diligently apply themselves to it (namely, the Law) for its own sake (and do not study it more vigorously and observe it), for its own sake (that is, for the honor of the Law), the Holy Spirit—which is the Shekhinah—does not dwell or rest.** And in Rabbi Elijah’s little book which is called **Tishbi** <note>A dictionary of Hebrew words by the famous grammarian Elijah Levita (1469–1549).</note>, under the <term>root</term> <note>original: "Radice"</note> or stem-word **Shakhan** <note>Hebrew for "to dwell."</note>, it says: **Our Rabbis of blessed memory have called the Holy Spirit "Shekhinah" because He rests upon the prophets.** Likewise, in the book **Neveh Shalom** <note>"Abode of Peace," a philosophical and homiletic work by Abraham Shalom (d. 1492).</note>, folio 97, column 2, in the eighth chapter of the fourth <term>Ma’amar</term> <note>A Hebrew term for a "treatise" or "discourse."</note>, it is taught that He is called Shekhinah.

<margin>However, by Shekhinah, God is understood.</margin>
That God is understood by the word **Shekhinah** is taught in the book **Avodat ha-Kodesh** <note>"Service of Holiness," a classic Kabbalistic text by Meir ibn Gabbai (1480–1540).</note>, in the first part, which is called **Chelek ha-Yichud** <note>"The Portion of Unity."</note>, in the fifth chapter, folio 11, column 1, where the words read as follows: <note>original: "חס ושלום שיהיה הדבר הנקרא שכינה..."</note> that is, **Heaven forbid that that which is called Shekhinah, or Kavod (that is, the Glory), should be a created thing outside of the glorious and blessed God, etc. For in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory, there are many things which prove that the name Shekhinah signifies the blessed God Himself.**

# Chapter VII.

### In which it is shown how the Jews maliciously despise and scorn the Holy Scripture of the New Testament, as well as the holy Evangelists and Apostles.

<margin>God has promised to make a new covenant and to give a new law.</margin>
We read in the Prophet Jeremiah, in the 32nd chapter <note>In modern English Bibles, this famous prophecy of the New Covenant is found in Jeremiah 31:31-33.</note>, in the 31st, 32nd, and 33rd verses: "Behold, the time is coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah; not like the covenant that I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt, which covenant they did not keep, and I had to compel them, says the Lord: I will put my law in their hearts and write it in their minds; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God." From these words, it is clearly to be seen that God the Lord promised to establish a new and much more glorious covenant and to give another law, in place of that covenant which He made through <term>Moses</term> <note>The central prophet and lawgiver in Judaism.</note> on Mount Sinai with the children of Israel after their departure from Egypt through the proclamation of the Law. This new law, as seen in Isaiah 12:3, Micah 4:2, and Psalm 110:2, was destined to come forth from Mount Zion and the city of Jerusalem. This prophecy was fulfilled through our most precious Savior Jesus Christ, the true <term>Messiah</term> <note>From the Hebrew "Mashiach," meaning "Anointed One."</note>, as can be read in the 8th chapter of the Epistle to the Romans. He abolished the old Mosaic Law, insofar as it concerns the ceremonial and judicial statutes, and taught the law of the New Covenant—namely, the Covenant of Grace. He also had this law recorded in writing by His holy Evangelists and Apostles, so that through reading and hearing it, mankind might learn the way to salvation and be instructed in the mysteries of God.

But Rabbi Elias <note>Elijah Levita (1469–1549), a famous Hebrew grammarian and lexicographer.</note> writes in his *Tischbi* under the word *Gillájon* about this as follows: <note>Hebrew: הנוצרים קורין לתורה חדשה שלהם אוונגליון והוא בלשון יון בשורה טובה ורבותינו ז"ל הפכו שמו</note> **The Christians call their new law "Evangelium," which in the Greek language means "good news," but our Rabbis, of blessed memory, inverted its name...**

### Chapter VII of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.

...its name is a scroll of iniquity, and it is not right <note>original: "שמו און גליון והוא לא נכון"; This is a Hebrew wordplay on the word "Evangelium."</note>; that is, the Christians call their new law **Gospel**, which is, in the Greek language, a "good message": but our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have inverted its name and made from it **Avon gillájon** <note>Hebrew: עוון גליון; literally "Sin of the Scroll."</note>, which is not right.

<margin>and Avon gillájon.</margin>
But they also call it **Avón gillájon**, that is, a sin of the book, or a book in which sinful things are written. Thus it is named in the old **Sepher Nizzáchon** <note>The "Book of Victory," a 12th-century Jewish polemical work written to counter Christian missionary claims.</note> on page 186, where it is written: **In their (namely the Christians') Avon gillájon, which they call the Evangelium, it is written where the genealogy of JESUS is recounted, that he was descended from kings.** <note>original: "כתוב בעוון גליון שלהם שהם קורין אותו אוון גליון שהם מספרים תלדות ישו שיצא ממלכים"; This refers to the genealogies found in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke.</note> And on page 15 of the mentioned old **Nizzáchon**, regarding the words of **Genesis** 18, verse 2, **"And behold, three men stood before him,"** it is read thus: **In the Avon gillájon, I mean to say, the Gospel, it is said that he saw three and prayed to one.** <note>original: "אומרים בעוון גליון ר"ל באוונגליון ג' ראה ולאחד התפלל"; This is a common medieval Jewish critique of the Christian interpretation of the Trinity in the Old Testament.</note> It is also called this by Rabbi **Lipmann** <note>Yom-Tov Lipmann-Muhlhausen, a 14th-century philosopher and polemicist.</note> in his **Sepher Nizzáchon**, number 347, page 192, where he writes: **Is it not written for you in your Avon gillájon that JESUS did not come to overturn the Law, but to fulfill it?** <note>original: "הלא כתיב לכם בעון גליון שישוע לא בא להפוך התורה אלא למלאותה"; This refers to Matthew 5:17.</note> And it is also named thus by Rabbi **Abraham Zacuto** in his **Sepher Juchasín** <note>The "Book of Genealogies," a historical work written in the early 16th century.</note>, folio 148.

<margin>Where the Jews learned such shameful contempt.</margin>
This godless contempt for the glorious and comforting **Gospel**, which is quite common among all Jews, they learned from their great book of lies and blasphemy, the **Talmud**, where in the tractate **Shabbat** (or **Schabbas**) folio 116, column 1, after mention is made that the books of the heretics should not be saved from a fire, it is read: **The school of Rabbi Meir called it Aven gillájon; but the school of Rabbi Jochanan called it Avon gillájon.** <note>original: "דבי מאיר קרי ליה און גליון: דבי יוחנן קרי ליה עון גליון"; "Aven gillájon" means "Scroll of Idolatry" or "Vanity," while "Avon gillájon" means "Scroll of Sin." Both are phonetic puns on the Greek "Evangelion."</note> And Rabbi **Solomon** <note>Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the most famous medieval commentator on the Talmud.</note> writes in his explanation of this: **The school of Rabbi Meir calls the books of the heretics Aven gillájon because they call them Evangelia.** <note>original: "דבי מאיר קרי לספרי המינין און גליון לפי שהם קורין אותן אוונגליא"</note>

<margin>How the Apostles and other saints are mockingly named. The disciples of Christ are called heretics.</margin>
As for the holy disciples and apostles of **Christ**, and other saints, they are also greatly despised and mocked. The Apostle **James** is called in the Talmudic tractate **Avoda Zara** folio 27, column 2, **Min**, that is, a heretic, as was already indicated above in the fifth chapter, page 262. And likewise, in the tractate **Chagiga** folio 5, column 2, in Rabbi **Solomon’s** explanation, all the disciples of **Christ** are called heretics, where the

### How the Jews despise the New Testament, the Evangelists, etc.

...the words thus read: **that is, the disciples of Jesus are heretics because they do not acknowledge the words of the Sages.** <note>original: "מינא הלמידי ישו שאינן מודים לדברי חכמים"; The Hebrew term "Minim" (heretics) is being applied specifically to Christians.</note> They are likewise titled in the tractate *Bava Batra* <note>A tractate of the Talmud dealing with civil law and property.</note> folio 25, column 1, where the aforementioned Rabbi Solomon <note>Referring to Rashi, the preeminent medieval commentator on the Talmud.</note> writes concerning the word **Mine** (that is, **Heretics**): **that is, the disciples of Jesus teach that one should pray toward the rising of the sun.** <note>original: "הלמידי ישו מורין הוראה להתפלל למזרח"; Praying toward the East was a common practice in the early Church, which the Rabbis here contrast with Jewish practice.</note> The Apostle Peter is insultingly called **Peter Chamor**, <note>original: "פטור חמור"; This is a pun. In Hebrew, "Petur Chamor" refers to the "firstling of a donkey" which must be redeemed according to the Law of Moses.</note> that is, <margin>Pater chamor, that is, the firstborn of a donkey.</margin> **a firstling of a donkey** (about which one may read in Exodus 34:20) **or a donkey that breaks the mother** <note>This refers to the "opening of the womb."</note> through an *allusion* or hint at the name Peter or Petrus. Thereupon Peter spoke to him: "Since future things are known to you, you are God; why then have you not shown it to me before now?" To this Jesus replied to him: "Tell no one that I am God, for since the time that I left the law of my birth, I have been rebellious against my Creator and His law."** <note>original: "כתוב להם שישו אמר לפטור חמור... ונגד תורתו"; This is a fictional polemical narrative created by the author of the Nizzachon to depict Jesus confessing to sin and apostasy.</note> Here it is to be seen how the wretched devil perverts the Holy Scripture through the Jews and attributes to it unheard-of, palpable lies so that he may make Jesus hated; for not the slightest bit of this is to be found in the entire New Testament. Furthermore, on page 240, the following stands: **that is, it stands written in the book of Simeon, the son of Cephas (who is called Peter), that Jesus said to Peter Châmor: "Satan seeks with all diligence to kill you, etc."** <note>original: "כתוב בספר שמעון בן כיפא... להמיתך וגו'"; Simon bar Jonah (Peter) is here called "Simon son of Cephas," using a mock-genealogy.</note> Further on page 164, it is read: **that is, and if you wish to say that Jesus is God because of the miracles he performed before the people (then I say in opposition): Did not Moses also perform many miracles? Likewise, Elijah ascended to heaven in a whirlwind in the sight of all, which Jesus did not do; for at his ascension, no man saw him, except that they say that Chuia, Magdalena, and Peter Chamor (here they mention the name of the holy Peter in a derogatory manner and call him a donkey) saw and testified of him that he ascended.** <note>original: "ואם תאמר מפני האותות... שעלה"; "Chuia" likely refers to Joanna, and "Magdalena" to Mary Magdalene. The text argues that Christian witnesses were insufficient or unreliable compared to the biblical prophets.</note> for during his ascension—

# Chapter VII of the Second Part of Judaism Unmasked.
<meta>catchword: לו</meta>

...[no] man has seen him, except that they (the Christians) say that **Charja Magdalena** <note>original: "Charja Magdalena"; A derogatory wordplay on Mary Magdalene. In Hebrew and Aramaic, *kharya* means excrement or filth.</note> (here the shameful word *Charja* appears again before Mary, which was mentioned above in the second chapter on page 141, and which signifies filth) and **Peter Chamor** <note>original: "Peter Chamor"; A pun on the name of Saint Peter. In Hebrew, *Chamor* means a donkey.</note> (here they—meaning the Jews—shamefully name Saint Peter and call him a donkey) have seen it and testified to it. In this manner, a converted Jew named Peter is also called **Peter Chamor** in Rabbi Lipmann’s *Sefer Nizzachon*, number 348, page 193: <note>original: "פיטר חמור"; Peter the Donkey.</note>

<margin>Paul is maliciously called *Kadesh*, meaning a fornicator, instead of *Kadosh*, which means holy.</margin>
The holy Apostle Paul is called **Kadesh** (meaning a fornicator or scoundrel) instead of **Kadosh** (which means holy) in the old *Nizzachon* on page 225, through a distortion of the word, where the words read: <note>original: "ועוד ראייה לדבר שאין הבשר יודע כלום מזה שאמר פאולוס קדש שלהם באיון גיליון"; "And further proof of the matter—that the flesh knows nothing—can be proven from what Paul, their 'Kadesh,' said in the Gospel."</note> That is: Thus the matter—that the flesh knows nothing—can also be proven because Paul, their *Kadesh* (fornicator or scoundrel), says in the Gospel <note>The author uses the term "Gospel" here to refer generally to the New Testament writings.</note> that the soul at all hours incites the body to sin.

<margin>Similarly, the Saints are mockingly called *Kedeschim* (fornicators) instead of *Kedoschim* (holy ones).</margin>
Similarly, deceased Saints are contemptuously called **Kedeschim** (meaning fornicators or scoundrels) instead of **Kedoschim** (holy ones), as can be read in the aforementioned old *Nizzachon* on page 128, where it is written: <note>original: "מה שאומרים שמפילים תחנה ובקשה לפני הקדשים פגרים מתים כדי שיתפללו עליהם לפני האלהים : תשובה והא כתיב לא המתים יהללו יה"; "Regarding what they say, that they cast supplication and request before the 'Kedeschim'—dead carcasses—so that they might pray for them before God: The answer is: It is written (Psalm 115:17): 'The dead shall not praise the LORD.'"</note> That is: Since the heretics <note>The text uses "Minim" (heretics) to refer to Christians.</note> say they offer their prayer and petition to the **Kedeschim** (fornicators or scoundrels) and **Pegarim methim** (or *Pegorim mesim*), which means dead carcasses, so that they might intercede with God for them: O answer them, for it stands written in Psalm 115, verse 17: **The dead shall not praise the LORD.** And on page 130 of the same book, it is written: <note>original: "המינים שואלים אותנו ואומרים מדוע אינכם מבקשין פני גדול כמו שאנו עושין שהם מבקשין לקדשים : השיב להם שוטים כל מה שאתם מבקשים ועושים להקציף הק"בה הוא וגו'"; "The heretics ask us and say: 'Why do you not seek the face of a Great One as we do? For they seek the Kedeschim.' Answer them: 'Fools! Everything you request and do only serves to anger the Holy One, Blessed be He,' etc."</note> That is: The heretics (meaning Christians) ask us and say: "Why do you not seek the face of a Great One (who might pray for you) as we do? For they pray to the **Kedeschim** (fornicators or scoundrels)." Answer them: "You fools! Everything you ask and do only results in you angering the Holy and Blessed GOD," etc.

<margin>Further proof that the deceased Saints are called *Kedeschim*.</margin>
Furthermore, in the mentioned book on page 141, regarding the words of Psalm 146, verse 3—**Put not your trust in princes, they are men who cannot help**—it is written in this way: <note>original: "פירוש הקדישים שהחנזבו את עצמם : למות על יראת ישו אל תבטחו בהם שיתפללו בעדכם כי אין תפילה לאחר מיתה בבן אדם שאין לו"; "The interpretation: The 'Kedeschim' who sacrificed themselves to die for the fear of Jesus—do not trust in them to pray for you, for there is no prayer after death for a son of man who has no [power...]"</note>

# How the Jews despise the New Testament, the Evangelists, etc.

...[to him is] no salvation; also, do not trust in Jesus, who is a son of man. <note>original Hebrew: "לו תשועה, גם אל תבטחו בישו שהוא בן אדם"</note> That is: **The meaning of these words is: do not rely on the *Kedeschim* <term>Kedeschim: A derogatory pun. While *Kedoshim* means "holy ones" or "saints," *Kedeschim* refers to male cultic prostitutes or "sodomites" in biblical Hebrew.</term>, that is, whoremongers or shameful rogues, who have voluntarily given themselves to death for the sake of the religion of Jesus, [believing] that they will pray for you; for after death, no prayer helps a man who cannot help himself. Also, do not rely on Jesus, who is a man.** They are also called thus in the Talmudic tractate *Sanhedrin*, folio 63, column 2, in the *Tosafot* <note>The *Tosafot* are medieval commentaries on the Talmud, often found in the margins of the text.</note>, where it is written: "In this time they (the Christians) all swear by their *Kedeschim* or whoremongers, and do not regard them as gods." <note>original Hebrew: "בזמן הזה כולן נשבעין בקדשים שלהן ואין תופסין בהם אלוהות"</note> And in the second part of the Prague *Machsor* <note>A Jewish prayer book for festivals.</note>, folio 31, column 1, under the title *Yotzer le-parashat ha-chodesh*, in the prayer that begins with "This sign of the month" <note>original: "אות זה החדש" (Oth zeh ha-chodesh)</note>, the Jews pray: **"And in it, let the *Kedeschim* or whoremongers fall"** (meaning in the month of Nisan or March). The word *Kedeschim*, however, is explained in the commentary as **"the nations and their idols or false gods."** <note>original: "האומות וגלוליהם"</note> Likewise, the saints are called *Kedeschim* in the little book *Shevet Yehuda*, folio 84, column 1. Just as the holy men are called *Kedeschim*, they also call the holy women *Kedeschoth* <note>original: "קדישות"</note>, that is, **whores.** From this we see that the convert Hieronymus de Santa Fe <note>Jerónimo de Santa Fe, a 15th-century Spanish physician and convert from Judaism who wrote *Adversus Iudaeos*.</note> wrote the pure truth in the fifth chapter of his second book when he reports that the Jews call the holy apostles and martyrs of Christ **whoremongers**, and the holy women **whores**.

<margin>
They also call Christ's [followers] *Taschmidim*, that is, "the annihilated ones," instead of *Talmidim*, that is, "disciples."
</margin>
Therefore, it is also easy to believe that they call the disciples of Christ—who in Hebrew are called *Talmidim*, that is, **disciples**—by the name *Taschmidim* to their greatest mockery. This word comes from the root *Shamad*, which means to destroy, disturb, and root out, and thus means **the annihilated ones.** Converted Jews—such as Antonius Margarita in his *Entire Jewish Faith* in the section on the prayer *Vela-malshinim al tehi tikvah*, page 242; and Johann Adrian in his *Epistle*, page 29; and Dieterich Schwabe in his *Jewish Cover*, at the end of the 6th chapter of the first part; as well as Friedrich Samuel Brentz in his *Jewish Snake-Skin* in the second chapter—all unanimously testify to this.

<margin>
They are, however, commanded to give such perverse and shameful names.
</margin>
It is not to be wondered at that they give such mocking names to the holy apostles, who were born Jews and accepted the teaching of Jesus Christ, for they are commanded to do so. Hence, in the *Sefer Hasidim* <note>A central 12th/13th-century Hebrew text on Jewish ethics and piety.</note>, number 191, it is written: "A Jew who converts and goes to serve idols, a nickname is given to him, as it is said: 'Those who make them shall be like them'; therefore one must give him a nickname, such as if his name is Abraham..." <note>original Hebrew: "יהודי שהמיר והלך לעבוד עבודת אלילים מכנין לו שם שנא' כמותם יהיו עושיהם: במוהם יש לכנות לו כגון אם שמו אברהם"</note>

### Part I of Judaism Unmasked, Chapter VII.

"Abraham is called Afram and so on in like manner." <note>original Hebrew: "אברהם נקרא אפרם וכן כיוצא בזה"</note> This is to say: when a Jew changes his religion and goes to practice idolatry, they give him a (shameful) nickname, as it is said (Psalm 115:8 and 135:18): *Those who make them (namely the idols) are like unto them.* One must give these (apostates) nicknames, just as nicknames are given to the idols themselves (which are called *Gillulim* <term>Gillulim: A derogatory term for idols, literally meaning "pellets of dung."</term>, that is—saving your presence—dung-gods; and *Elilim*, that is, worthless gods, etc.). 

For example, if he is named Abraham (which means "exalted father of a multitude of people"), then he shall be called Afram (that is, "dust," for *Afar* <note>עפר</note> means dust), or he is given another name in such a fashion. From this we learn the reason why the Apostle Peter is called *Peter Chamor* <term>Chamor: Hebrew for "donkey" or "ass."</term>, Paul is called *Kadesh* instead of *Kadosh* <note>meaning "sodomite" or "male prostitute" instead of "holy."</note>, and the converted Friedrich Samuel Brentz is called *Sammael* (which is the name of the prince of devils) instead of Samuel by Rabbi Salman Zevi in his book *Jewish Theriac*. Furthermore, the holy *Kedoshim* and *Kedoshoth* <note>Male and female saints.</note> are called *Kedeschim* and *Kedeschoth* <note>Male and female cultic prostitutes.</note>, and the disciples of Christ are called *Taschmidim* <term>Taschmidim: A pun on *Talmidim* (disciples), changing the root to mean "destroyed ones" or "those to be exterminated."</term> instead of *Talmidim*. 

Likewise, the aforementioned Friedrich Samuel Brentz reports in his *Snake-skin* <note>A reference to Brentz's 1610 work "Schlangenbalg," written after his conversion to Christianity to expose Jewish anti-Christian polemics.</note>, in the second chapter, that they call a rural, city, or chancellery scribe *Kofer* (that is, a denier of God or a heretic) instead of *Sopher* (which means a scribe); and I can bear witness for him that he has reported the truth in this matter, for I have found this myself in their written letters which were provided to me to read.

<margin>
* John the Baptist is called a godless man.
</margin>

Holy John the Baptist must also suffer this; he is called *Rasha* or *Rosho*, that is, a godless man, in the old *Nizzachon* <note>The "Sefer Nizzachon Yashar," a medieval Jewish polemical work.</note> on page 58, where it is written: **The heretics ask: what is the sign that Moses did not bring the Israelites into the land of Canaan until Joshua came and led them across the Jordan? And they say that this signifies the Law given by Moses, which was not profitable or suitable to bring them into Paradise until Jesus came—who is named Joshua—and led them through his hand; that is to say: they were baptized by the hand of the godless John.** <note>original Hebrew: "המינים שואלים מה רמז הוא שמשח לא הכניס את ישראל לארץ כנען עד שבא יהושע והעבירם את הירדן ואומרים שזה רמז על התורה שנתן משה לא הועילה להכניסם לגן עדן עד שבא ישו ששמו יהושע והעבירם בידו כלומר : שנטבלו ביד יוחן רשע"</note> 

Here it should be observed that he is not called *Jochanan Ha-Rasha*, that is, John the godless, but *Juchan Rasha* or *Rosho*—words found in Isaiah 26:10, which mean: *Let favor be shown to the wicked.* He is called this for his greater mockery, through the distortion of his name <note>The author argues the name "Jochanan" (John) is deliberately shortened to "Juchan" to match the phrasing in the biblical verse about the wicked.</note>.

### How the Jews cast suspicion upon the New Testament, the Evangelists, etc.

The Jewish historian Josephus, however, gives him <note>John the Baptist</note> a different testimony in the 18th book of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, in the seventh chapter <note>In modern editions, this is Book 18, Chapter 5</note>, writing of him thus: **"It was a common saying among the Jews that Herod's army was destroyed by the righteous judgment of God because of John, who is called the Baptist, whom Herod had killed. For Herod the Tetrarch <term>Tetrarch: A governor of one of four divisions of a province; here referring to Herod Antipas.</term> had put this pious man to death, who exhorted the Jews to all kinds of virtues, and especially to the fear of God and justice, led them to baptism, and said that their baptism would only be pleasing to God if they not only abstained from one or two sins, but first purified the heart through righteousness, and afterwards also the body."** These are the words of Josephus. How then could the godless villain who wrote the old *Nizzachon* <note>original: "Nizzachon," a medieval Jewish polemical work titled "The Book of Victory."</note> call the pious John a godless man?

<margin>The holy Apostles are also called *Bene Parizim*, that is, Breakers.</margin>
The holy Apostles are also flippantly called בני פריצים **Bene parizim**, that is, **Breakers**, who are said to have "broken through" the laws and rights and acted against them. The words of Daniel 11:14, **"Also the breakers of thy people shall exalt themselves,"** are interpreted by them in this way. Thus, Rabbi Aben Esra <note>Abraham Ibn Ezra, a prominent medieval Spanish rabbi and scholar.</note> writes concerning these words: <note>original Hebrew: "ובימים ההם יקומו פרוצים מישראל ואלה היו בימי האדם שהוא אלהי העולם"</note> that is, **"And in those same days, breakers shall arise from Israel: these were in the times of that man (namely Jesus) who is the God of the uncircumcised."** <note>The German translates the Hebrew *Elohei Ha-Olam* (God of the world) as "God of the uncircumcised," reflecting the common Jewish polemical reference to Christians.</note> In Abarbanel's <note>Isaac Abarbanel, a 15th-century Portuguese Jewish statesman and philosopher.</note> book *Mayene Yeshu'ah* <note>The Wells of Salvation.</note>, on folio 73, column 2, in the eleventh *Mayan*, in the fifth *Tamar*, it is also written: <note>original Hebrew: "כיון בו על תלמידי ישו אשר שחו בשמים פיהם להעמיד חזון ונכשלו כולם ומתו בחרב ובחליה"</note> that is, **"He (the Prophet Daniel) had in view the disciples of Jesus, who opened their mouths against heaven to establish a false vision and prophecy; they all fell, and perished by the sword and the strangulation."**

<margin>How the Jews despise the New Testament and those who wrote it.</margin>

# Chapter Seven of the First Part of *Judaism Unmasked*.

**"The intention is to make it known that the Gospel <note>original: "Ha-A"G" (הא"ג), an abbreviation for *Ha-Avongelyon*, the Hebrew term for the Gospel.</note> is not the teaching of Jesus, as the Christians say, and even less is it the teaching of God, as they claim. Rather, it is a corrupt work by empty and reckless men who were not skilled in the Holy Scriptures or the meaning of the verses. Therefore, their words do not agree with each other in many matters, and in most places, they cannot be interpreted or reconciled with the words of the prophets."** 

That is: The preface is directed toward this end: to make it known that the **Gospel** is not the law of **Jesus**, as the Christians claim; much less that it is God’s law, as they pretend; but that it is a corrupted work which comes from loose and frivolous people who were not experienced in the Holy Scripture and did not understand the purpose of the verses. Therefore, their words do not agree with each other in many points and cannot be explained or clarified in many places according to what the prophets have said. They are of no help or benefit to them, for the prophets (upon whom be peace), in those sayings from which the Christians bring proof for their faith, did not intend their foolish opinion, nor did what they [the Christians] invent from their own hearts ever enter their [the prophets'] minds. Sometimes they add to the words of the prophets, and sometimes they subtract things from the prophetic sayings that are against them. Sometimes they write something as proof for their faith, saying it is a prophetic word, and that thing is not found in the books of prophecy at all. And likewise, sometimes even in matters of narrative—that is, in things that are not for proving their faith—they err in writing prophetic sayings differently from how they are written in the books of prophecy. All of this indicates that their law is not divine, but is the guidance of empty and reckless men, smearers of lies, who were not at all skilled in the words of the Torah and the prophets, and even less in knowing the meaning of the sayings."** 

That is: When you (Christians) wish to know whether you are right or wrong, you must carefully consider and look into those same places which those who wrote the **Gospel** cite from the words of the **Prophets** (upon whom be peace) as proof of their statements, and see whether the words of the prophecy fit their proof or not. When you then pay attention through rational reflection, you will see and understand from what precedes and follows that the words of prophecy which those who wrote the **Gospel** cite to prove their faith do not teach in the slightest what they want to prove, and thus help or benefit them nothing. # How the Jews despise the New Testament, the Evangelists, etc.

<margin>Refutation of the Jewish slander that the New Testament was written by ignorant and unskilled people.</margin> We thus see from what was previously reported, how godlessly the stubborn and malicious Jews despise and mock the New Testament, and in what manner they disdain and defame the holy Evangelists and Apostles in a slanderous way. They even dare to quite presumptuously claim and assert that these were ignorant and unskilled men who did not understand the Holy Scriptures of the Old Testament at all, citing them incorrectly and backwards here and there, and not paying attention to what comes before or what follows. They also claim they do not agree with one another, and that they added to or subtracted from them as they pleased, even bringing forth proofs from the Prophets that are not found therein. 

However, since the Lord God promised through the Prophet Joel, in the 2nd chapter, in the 28th verse, that in the last times He would pour out His Holy Spirit over all flesh, saying: *And after this (that is, in the last days, as seen in Acts 2:17), I will pour out my Spirit over all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your elders shall have dreams, and your young men shall see visions.* By "the last times," the times of the Messiah are understood, as Rabbi David Kimchi <note>Also known as Radak (1160–1235), a prominent medieval Jewish grammarian and biblical commentator from France.</note> teaches in his exposition of Isaiah 2, verse 2, where he writes as follows: "Everywhere where mention is made of the last days, there the days of the Messiah are understood." <note>Original Hebrew: *Kol maqom shenne'emar be-acharit ha-yamim hu yemot ha-Mashiach.*</note> With this, Rabbi Aben Esra <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167), a distinguished Spanish Jewish scholar, poet, and philosopher.</note> also agrees in his exposition thereof, when he says: "Behold, he (the Prophet Isaiah) speaks: In the last times, which signifies the times of the Messiah, as these are the last times of the world." <note>Original Hebrew: *Ve-hinneh amar be-acharit ha-yamim ve-hem yemei ha-Mashiach she-hem acharit yemei 'olam.*</note>

The aforementioned prophecy was fulfilled especially in the holy Evangelists and Apostles (who must have been adorned with extraordinary gifts above others, so that through the wholesome preaching of the Holy Gospel, they might bring to the right path of true salvation those poor humans who were completely astray in the way of sin and stripped of all soul-comfort) with the rich outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the distribution of His glorious gifts, as is to be read in Acts 2, verse 4, where it is written: *And they (namely the Apostles) were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to preach with other tongues, according as the Spirit gave them utterance.* Furthermore, in the second Epistle of Peter, Chapter 2, verse 12 <note>The author likely intended to cite 2 Peter 1:21, which discusses how men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit; 2 Peter 2:12 usually refers to "irrational animals."</note>, it is taught that those who proclaimed the Gospel did so through the Holy Spirit. How then could such highly enlightened men be called, with any ground of truth, ignorant, unskilled, falsifiers of the Holy Scriptures of the Old Testament, and liars...

<margin>It is of no significance even if some things in the New Testament seem to contradict each other.</margin> Moreover, it is of no significance if the holy Evangelists and Apostles seem to disagree with one another in some places, for many things also occur in the Old Testament which seem to contradict each other. And in Genesis 8:13, it is found that on the first day of the first month, the waters of the Flood were dried up from the earth; conversely, it says in the following fourteenth verse that the earth became dry on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. Many such discrepancies could still be brought forward from the Old Testament. # Chapter VIII.
### What the Jews Teach Concerning Their Talmud, and What is to be Thought of It.

<margin>The Jews consider the Talmud to be God’s Word.</margin>
Because it was shown in the preceding chapter in what manner the godless Jews maliciously despise and slander the New Testament, and consider the holy Evangelists and Apostles to be ignorant and unintelligent men who, in order to prove this or that, are said to have falsely cited the Holy Scriptures of the Old Testament: therefore I have deemed it necessary to write this chapter immediately following regarding their Talmud (namely, the Babylonian Talmud, for the Jerusalem Talmud is used very little by the Jews and is a small work compared to the Babylonian) which they foolishly dare to present as God’s Word. This is despite the fact that many horrible blasphemies, tasteless fables, and gross, palpable lies, ridiculous and irrational citations and interpretations of the Holy Scripture, and many things which directly contradict God’s Word are found therein. Also, some of the Talmudic teachers were godless and frivolous people who led a wicked and scandalous life: all this is provided so that one may see the great blindness and hardening of heart of this people, who so greatly despise the pure and holy teaching of the New Testament, and conversely recognize the nonsensical and false teaching of the Talmud as God’s Word.

<margin>They say that they have a twofold Law, namely a written and an oral one.</margin>
To proceed to the matter itself, it should be known that the Jews teach they have a twofold Law: namely, a written one, which consists of the five books of Moses and was set down in writing by Moses, and for that reason is called by them *Torah Shebiktav* <note>original: "תורה שבכתב" (Torah Shebiktav); the Written Law.</note>; and then an oral-written one <note>The author uses the term "Münd-Schrifftliches," likely to describe a law that was spoken but eventually recorded in writing.</note>, which is the Talmud, and is called *Torah Shebe'al Peh* <note>original: "תורה שבעל פה" (Torah Shebe'al Peh); the Law which is on the mouth, or the Oral Law.</note>. Regarding these two Laws, it is read as follows in the Talmudic tractate *Shabbath* (or *Shabbas*) folio 31, column 1:

<note>original Hebrew: "תנו רבנן מעשה בנכרי אחד שבא לפני שמאי אמר לו כמה תורות יש לכם אמר לו שתים תורה שבכתב ותורה שבעל פה אמר לו שבכתב אני מאמינך ושבעל פה איני מאמינך גיירני ע"מ שתלמדני תורה שבכתב גער בו והוציאו בנזיפה בא לפני הילל גייריה יומא קמא אמר לו א"ב ג"ד למחר אפיך ליה אמר ליה והא אתמול..."</note>

Shammai scolded him and sent him away with a rebuke. The man then came before Hillel, who converted him. The man said to him: "But yesterday..."**

<margin>The entire Talmud consists of the Mishnah and Gemara. When and by whom the Mishnah was written.</margin>
The entire Talmud consists of two parts, namely the **Mishnah** and the **Gemara** (or Gemoro). The Mishnah is the text of the Talmud, while the Gemara is the commentary upon it. The Mishnah was first recorded in writing, organized into an order, and divided into six **Sedarim** (or Sedórim), that is, Orders, during the time of the Emperor Antoninus Pius—which was three hundred and fifty years after the birth of Christ <note>Modern scholarship generally dates the redaction of the Mishnah earlier, to approximately 200 CE.</note>—by **Rabbi Judah the Prince** (Rabbi Jehuda hannási). Because of his pious and holy conduct, he is called **Rabbenu HaKadosh**, which means "Our Holy Rabbi." He compiled it from all sorts of notes that had been written down and brought together from various places. These six *Sedarim* were further divided into sixty **Massichtoth** (or Massichtos), which are separate treatises. The entire book is called the **Mishnah**, or **Mishnayoth**, because it is intended to be a "repeated law"; for *Mishnah* comes from *Shanah*, which means "to repeat." Alternatively, as Rabbi Bechai reports in his commentary on the Five Books of Moses, in the section *Tissa*, folio 115, column 4: <note>original: "לפי שהיא שניה לתורה שבכתב ורובה לשון הקודש צח כתורה שבכתב"</note> That is: Because it is the *Torah Shenia*, the "Second Law" after the Written Law, and it is mostly written in pure Hebrew, just like the Written Law. He claims that no blasphemies or other unseemly things are to be found within it. ### Of the Jews' Talmud.

...[fir]st Part, folio 30, column 2, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: "רבי יהודה הנשיא הנ"ל כשראה אורך הגלות ושהתלמידים והלבבות היו מתמעטים ואזלת יד החכמה והקבלה ותל עד מאור תורה שבעל פה הנה אף על פי שדברים שעל פה אי אתה רשאי לאמרן בכתב כדאיתא בפרק הניזקין מ"מ סמך רבי על העת לעשות ל"י הפרו תורתך ואסף וקבץ כל ההלכות ודינים ודברי החכמים שכתבו כל אחד לעצמו ממה שלמדו בית דין בכל דור ודור מימי הזקנים והנביאים ואנשי כנסת הגדולה וחכמי המשנה"</note> That is: When Rabbi Judah, the Prince (of whom mention was made above), saw that the exile or misery was lasting a long time, and the disciples as well as the hearts [of men] were diminishing, and wisdom and the <term>Kabbala</term><note>Here used in its literal sense of "tradition" or "that which is received," specifically referring to the oral transmission of the law.</note> (or oral tradition and teaching) were passing away, and the Oral Law was also greatly declining, this Rabbi undertook to set down in writing those things which had been learned orally—even though (as may be read in the fifth chapter of the Talmudic tractate <term>Gittin</term><note>A tractate concerning the laws of divorce.</note>, folio 60, column 2) it is not permitted. Notwithstanding this, he held to that which is written in Psalm 119, verse 126: **It is time for the LORD to act: they have made void Your law.** And he collected and brought together all the <term>Halachoth</term><note>The collective body of Jewish religious laws derived from the Written and Oral Torah.</note> (or rulings), judicial statutes, and sayings of the sages which each individual had recorded for himself, and which the judges in every generation (or age) had taught from the times of the Elders, the Prophets, and the Men of the Great Synagogue, as well as the Sages of the <term>Mishnah</term><note>The first major written collection of the Jewish oral traditions.</note>, up until his own time. He wrote these down in six <term>Sedarim</term><note>Literally "Orders," the primary divisions of the Mishnah.</note> or arrangements, which are: 

<margin>Into how many Sedarim or Orders the Mishnah is divided, and what they are called.</margin> 
*Zeraim*, concerning the seeds and fruits of the earth; *Moed*, concerning the festivals; *Nezikin*, concerning damages; *Nashim*, concerning women; *Kodashim*, concerning holy things; and *Tohoroth* or *Tohoros*, concerning purities. This is also stated, though with some variation, in the book <term>Juchasin</term><note>A famous 16th-century work of Jewish history and genealogy.</note> folio 160, column 1, which was authored by Rabbi Abraham Zacuto. 

<margin>The Mishnayoth were accepted by all Jews as soon as they were completed.</margin> 
All Jews accepted this book of the <term>Mishnayoth</term><note>The plural form of Mishnah, referring to the individual paragraphs or the work as a whole.</note> immediately after it was completed, as the aforementioned Rabbi David Gans reports in his book *Zemach David*, in the first part, under the year 979 of the fourth millennium after the creation of the world.

<margin>What the Gemara is.</margin> 
Concerning the **Gemara** (or Gemoro), it contains the disputations of the Jewish doctors over the aforementioned Mishnayoth, which were held in the Promised Land as well as in Babylonia, and their *decisiones* or decisions which were issued regarding them. Contained within it are many foolish fables, shameless and coarse lies, false interpretations, and perversions of the Word of God, as well as those blasphemies which were cited above in the first, second, third, fourth, and fifth chapters from the Talmud.

Thus it is found that from the time the Mishnah was finished until the time of the completion of the Talmud, three hundred and eleven years had passed.**
