# 768 The First Part of Judaism Unmasked, Chapter 17.

Rabbi Samuel, the son of Nachman, said: there is an oral tradition (or teaching) that <term>Achum</term> <note>original: "ע"ום" - Akum, an acronym for "Worshippers of stars and planets," frequently used in these texts as a coded reference to Christians</note> shall fall by no hands other than those of the children of Rachel. This is what is written in **Jeremiah 49:20**: **The least of the flock shall drag them away.**

<margin>XVIII. It is also called simply "The Kingdom."</margin>

Eighteenthly, it is also called simply **Hammalchúth** (or *Hammalchus*), that is, "The Kingdom." As seen in Rabbi Isaac Karo’s explanation of the Five Books of Moses, titled **Toledóth Jizchak** (or *Toledos Yitzchak*, meaning "The Generations of Isaac"), on folio 20, column 2, in the section **Lech Lechá** <note>The weekly Torah portion beginning at Genesis 12:1</note> regarding **Genesis 14:1**, where it reads: <note>original Hebrew: "אמרו ז"ל מלך שנער זו בבל..."</note> **Our Sages, of blessed memory, say: The King of Shinar signifies Babylon (or the Babylonian Empire). The King of Ellasar signifies the Medes; Chedorlaomer the King of Elam signifies Greece; and Tidal the King of the Heathens signifies the *Malchúth* (or *Malchus*), that is, "The Kingdom," by which the Roman or Christian Empire is understood.** 

However, in my own copy, a Jew has written the word **harescháa** <note>Hebrew: "the wicked"</note> in the margin after *Malchúth*, so that one might know Christendom is meant; which, as mentioned on page 765 under the eleventh name they give it, is called **Malchúth harescháa**, that is, the **Wicked Kingdom**. 

Likewise, it is written in **Pesikta Rabbetha** (or *Rabbesa*) <note>An ancient collection of Jewish homilies or Midrashim</note> on folio 27, column 2, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: "המלכות היא מכתבת טירוניא..."</note> **The *Malchúth* or Kingdom issues tyrannical decrees before all nations.** 

In the **Prague Machsor** <note>A festival prayer book</note>, however, in the second part, on folio 54, column 2, the commentary reads instead: <note>original Hebrew: "מלכות אדום כותבת טירוניא..."</note> **The *Malchúth Edom*, or the Edomite Kingdom, issues tyrannical decrees over all nations.** 

And in the Talmudic tractate **Rosh Hashanah**, the following is found on folio 19, column 1: <note>original Hebrew: "גזרה המלכות גזרה שלא יעסקו בתורה..."</note> **The *Malchúth* or Kingdom had once issued a decree that they (namely the Jews) should not study the Law, nor circumcise their young sons, and should desecrate the Sabbaths. What did Yehúda ben Schamóa and his companions do? They sought counsel from a certain noblewoman, with whom all the great lords of Rome were acquainted. <margin>XXI. They also call the same the Scepter or Staff of Wickedness.</margin>
**Twenty-first**, they call the same *Shevet haresha* <note>original Hebrew: שבט הרשע</note>, that is, the Scepter of Wickedness, or also *Matteh resha* <note>original Hebrew: מטה רשע</note>, that is, the Staff of Wickedness; the former is taken from Psalm 125, verse 3, and the latter from Ezekiel 7, verse 11. <note>original Hebrew: כתיב כאשר שמוע למצרים יחילי כשמוע צור, וזה מפורש שבדמיון גאולת מצרים תהיה : גאולתנו העתידה שהרי צור מלכות אדום היא לפי שהוא חסר ואומר צר כתיב . ודרשו ז"ל כל צר שבמקרא חסר זו במלכות הרשעה הכתוב מדבר וכל צור מלא בצור המדינה הכתוב מדבר :</note>

That is: **It is written (Isaiah 23, verse 5): "As at the report (or cry) of *Zor*, they shall be in pain, as at the report of *Egypt*." And this is explained thus: that our future redemption shall be like the redemption from *Egypt*; for behold, *Zor* signifies the *Edomite* Reich** <note>Edomite Reich: In medieval Jewish literature, "Edom" became a frequent code name for the Roman Empire and subsequently for the Christian world</note> **because it is written incompletely (namely, without the *Vau Cholem*). And our Sages—blessed be their memory—have taught that wherever צר *Zor* stands in the Scripture without the *Vau Cholem*, the Scripture speaks of the wicked kingdom; but where צור *Zor* is found written fully, it makes mention of the city of *Tyre*.** 

The same is also found in the aforementioned book on folio 57, column 4, and in the little book *Afkáth* (or *Afkas*) *Róchel* <term>Avkat Rochel: "The Merchant's Powder," a 16th-century work concerning the end times</term>. Likewise, in the book *Pesikta Rábbetha* (or *rábbesa*) <term>Pesikta Rabbati: A collection of midrashic homilies</term> folio 32, column 4, it is taught thus: 

<note>original Hebrew: אמר רבי אליעזר כל צור שבמקרא הכתוב מדבר וכל צר חסר במקרא ברומי הרשעה הכתוב מדבר :</note>

That is: **Rabbi Eliezer has said, that wherever *Zor* stands completely, the Scripture makes mention of the city (or the province) of *Tyre*; but where *Zor* is found in the Scripture incompletely, it makes mention of *Romi harescháa*, that is, wicked Rome.** 

And such is also found in *Bereschith rábba* <term>Genesis Rabbah: An ancient commentary on the Book of Genesis</term> folio 55, column 3, at the end of the 61st *Parashah* <term>Parashah: A section of the Torah or its commentary</term> where only *Romi*, that is, *Rome*, is read instead of *Romi harescháa*, that is, the wicked *Rome*; and in *Schemóth rábba* <term>Exodus Rabbah: An ancient commentary on the Book of Exodus</term> folio 103, column 3, at the end of the 9th *Parashah*, where *Malchúth harescháa*, that is, the wicked Reich, stands in place of *Rome* or the wicked *Rome*; as can also be found in the *Jalkut Schimóni* <term>Yalkut Shimoni: A massive medieval compilation of Jewish interpretations of the Bible</term> concerning the prophet *Isaiah*, folio 45, column 3, number 291, in which place אומה זאת *Umma soth* (or *sós*), that is, **this (understand the Christian) people**, is written in place of *Rome* or the other aforementioned names. 

But in the *Jalkut chadásch* <term>Yalkut Chadash: A 17th-century collection of Kabbalistic and midrashic teachings</term> folio 186, column 1, number 103, it is read: 

<note>original Hebrew: כל צור האמור בתורה מלא בצור הכתוב מדבר וכל צר חסר בעיר חייבת והיינו רומי הכתוב מדבר :</note>

<note>original Hebrew: פרשו רבותינו כל צר שבמקרא חסר זו רומי הרשעה ורומי נקראת צר שנאמר כי יען זאת על צר המעטירה ;</note>

That is: **Our teachers have explained that every *Zor* which is incomplete in the Scripture refers to the wicked *Rome*; and *Rome* is called *Zor*, as it is said: "Because she has said this against *Zor* the crowning city..."**

# How Christendom is named by the Jews.

But you will find in the entire Law <note>The Torah</note> no one who mentions this beast by its name, except our teacher **Moses**, peace be upon him, and the psalmist **Asaph**; the latter (**Asaph**) makes a clearer mention of it by clearly indicating the name of the people and the name of its city, which is **Rome**. This is what he says in Psalm 80, verse 14: **The wild boar will root it up** <note>original: *Chazir mi-yaar*. In Jewish tradition, the "boar from the forest" is a frequent symbol for the Roman Empire</note>; and you will find the letter *Ayin* in the word מיער <term>miyáar; "from the forest"</term> suspended above the others, so that (if one omits this letter *Ayin*) the letters רומי <term>Romi; "Rome"</term> remain. For this reason, when **Moses** mentions the tenth chief in Genesis 36, verse 43—the chief **Magdiel** (which, according to the figurative interpretation of our Rabbis of blessed memory, is a reference to **Rome**) —he adds an explanation and says: "the chief עירם **Iram**." The letters of this word **Iram** are the same letters as the word מיער **miyáar** in the Hebrew language, only rearranged. This indicates that the chief **Magdiel** is the **wild boar**. 

The Scripture also gives witness to this name through its letters in Numbers 24, verse 19, where it is written: **And he shall destroy what remains מעיר Meír, that is, from the city**, which is the city of **Rome**. For the word מעir <note>original: *me’ir*</note> has the exact same letters in Hebrew as the word מיער <note>original: *miyáar*</note>; and when the letter *Ayin* is cast away, only the three letters מיר **MIR** remain, which, when rearranged, make רומי **Romi**, that is, **Rome**. In this same way, the prophet **Isaiah** mentions in chapter 25, verse 2: **You make מעיר meír, that is, out of the city, a stone heap; and a fortified city a ruin**; which is said of **Rome**. Furthermore, the letters of the word מעיר <note>original: *me’ir*</note> are also (in the Hebrew language) the letters of the word יירם <term>jirám; "He will thunder"</term>, of which **David** (peace be upon him) says in Psalm 18, verse 14: **The Lord will thunder in the heavens; the Most High will let His voice be heard with hail and glowing coals.** For the holy and blessed **God** will utterly destroy that same city (**Rome**). Thus **Daniel** also prophesied against it in chapter 7, verse 11: **Until the beast was slain, and its body destroyed, and thrown into the fire.**

It is then to be known that the *Radix* or the root word **Chasar** <note>original: "חזר"</note> in the Chaldean as well as the Rabbinic language means to "come back," to "go back," as well as to "wallow." From this, a swine is called *Chasir*, because even when it has been washed, it immediately returns to the filth and wallows therein. Regarding this, Rabbi *Mosche bar Nachman* <note>Also known as Nachmanides or Ramban (1194–1270), a leading medieval Jewish scholar.</note> also teaches in his commentary on the five books of *Moses*, folio 91, column 3, in the section *Parascha Acharé moth*, where he writes concerning the supreme devil *Sammaël* <note>In Jewish lore, Sammael is often the guardian angel of Edom/Esau and a figure of severity or evil.</note> as follows: <note>original Hebrew: הוא העילה לכוכבי החרב והדמים והמלחמות והמריבות והפצעים והמכות והפירוד והחרבן והכלל נפש לגלגל מאדים וחלקו מן האומות עשו שהוא עם היורש החרב והמלחמות ומן הבהמות השעירים והעזים ובחלקו עוד השדים הנקראים מזיקין בלשון רבותינו ובלשון הכתוב שעירים כי כן יקרא הוא ואומתו שעיר</note> that is: "He is the cause of the stars of the sword, and of blood, and of wars, and of disputes, and of wounds, and of blows, and of separation, as well as of devastation: to put it briefly, he is the soul of the planet *Mars*. Among the nations, however, *Esau* belongs to his portion, which is the people that inherits the sword and wars: and among the animals, the goats and she-goats are his part. Likewise, the devils are included in his portion, who in the language of our Rabbis are called <term>Mafsikim: likely a corruption of *Mazikin*, meaning 'injurers' or harmful spirits</term>, and in the language of the Scripture are called *Seïrim* <note>often translated as 'satyrs' or 'he-goats'</note>; for thus he and his nation (namely, Christendom) are called *Saïr*, that is, a goat, or a devil (since the Hebrew word means both)." This also stands in the book *Toledóth Jizchak* <note>'The Generations of Isaac,' a commentary by Isaac Caro.</note> folio 76, column 1, in the section *Acharé moth*, and in Rabbi *Bechai's* commentary on the five books of *Moses*, folio 139, column 1, in the said section *Acharé moth*, and in his book *Cad hakkémach* <note>'The Jar of Flour,' an alphabetically arranged book on ethics and faith.</note> folio 24, column 3; and from this it is clearly to be seen that Christendom is called *Saïr*, that is, a goat and a devil, about which more can be found below in the 2nd chapter of the second part.

XLII. It is also called the ten horns.

Forty-secondly, it is also called **Keranóth éser**, that is, **the ten horns**, a name taken from Daniel chapter 7, verse 7, where it is read that the **fourth beast** (which, as shown above, is intended to signify the Roman Empire) has ten horns; for this reason, Christendom is also named thus. That it is called such can be seen in the Prague *Machsor* <term>Mahzor: A festival prayer book containing the special liturgy for Jewish holidays.</term>, in the first part, folio 84, column 2, under the title *Schácháris schel jom kippur* <note>The Morning Service for the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur).</note>, in a prayer which begins *Ajúmma bachár* <note>Hebrew: "The Awesome One chose..."</note>, in which the Jews pray thus: **He (namely God) will uproot the ten horns to honor those who are planted in His house** <note>meaning the Israelites</note>. These words are explained in the commentary as follows: <note>original: קרנות עשר פירוש מלכות הרשעה שהיא קרן לשון מלכות ופשוטו מלכות הרשעה מכנה בשם קרנות ע״ש דכתיב בדניאל ז׳ וארו חיווא רביעאה וגו׳ וקרנין עשר לה וגו׳ והיא מלכות אדום הרשעה בגלות אחרון</note> That is: The ten horns signify the **Malchúth harescháa**, or **the wicked kingdom**; for the word "horn" signifies a kingdom. However, according to the simple (and literal) understanding, the wicked kingdom is called by the name "horns" because it is written in Daniel 7:7: "And behold, a fourth beast, etc. And it had ten horns, etc." by which the wicked kingdom in this final exile is to be understood.

And in the second part of the said *Machsor*, they pray on folio 66, column 2, in a prayer that begins *Appik rénen veschírim* <note>Hebrew: "Bring forth joy and songs."</note>, under the title *Józer lejóm schéni schél Pésach* <note>The morning prayer for the second day of Passover.</note>, in such a manner: **I will break the ten horns and subdue the nations under you.** These words are illustrated in the commentary upon them in such a manner: <note>original: קרנות עשר זו מלכות אדום דכתיב בדניאל וקרנין עשר לה</note> That is: The ten horns signify the Edomite Reich, for it stands written in Daniel 7:7: "And it had..."

So it is also called Duma for yet another reason, because the four kingdoms are compared to four beasts, and all the prophets together mention all the beasts by their names; except for the fourth beast, whose name they never mention by name, etc.

# The Seventeenth Chapter of the First Part of Discovered Judaism.

...interpret this captivity in which we now find ourselves, which is the Edomite captivity <term>Edomite captivity: A term used in Jewish thought to describe the long period of exile and life under Roman and later Christian rule, following the biblical identification of Rome with Edom.</term>; and he (the prophet) called it Duma, because we remain silent within it, for we do not know when the end of these wonders shall be, as was known in the Egyptian captivity, the time of which the holy and blessed God had set at four hundred years. It was also the same with the Babylonian captivity, in that Jeremiah promised them (namely the Jews in *Jeremiah* 29:10): When seventy years (of the desolation of Jerusalem) are completed, I will visit you. But the end of our (current) captivity is not set for a known day. Alternatively, Duma signifies a waiting and a tarrying (from דמם *Damám*, which means to wait), as it is said in *Psalm* 37:7: Rest in the Lord, and wait patiently for Him; this is to indicate that even if the captivity lasts a long time, we should nevertheless wait for Him.

<margin>XLIV. They also call the same "Haf haf," that is, "give, give."</margin>
Forty-fourthly, the same is called הבהב *Haf haf*, that is, Give, Give, which name is taken from *Proverbs* 30:15. Regarding this, Rabbi Abraham writes in his book *Tzeror HaMor* <note>Rabbi Abraham Saba (1440–1508), a Sephardic kabbalist and commentator; the title means "A Bundle of Myrrh."</note> folio 120, column 2, in the portion *Chukkath* concerning Edom (that is, Christendom), as follows: <note>original: כתיב לעלוקה שתי בנות הב הב : כונת הב הב והעלוקה הוא רמז ליצר כי כן דרכם לשאול מישראל מסים וארנוניות וכל עולם הם שואלים הב הב והרע הוא אדום</note> that is: **It stands written (*Prov.* 30:15): The leech has two daughters, (who say) Haf haf, that is, Give, Give; for such is their (the Christians') custom, to demand tribute (or tax) and customs from the Israelites, and they are always demanding (and saying) Haf haf, that is, Give, Give. The leech, however, signifies the evil nature, which is Edom.** Something regarding this can also be read in Rabbi Bechai's <note>Bahya ben Asher (13th century).</note> commentary on the five books of Moses, folio 220, column 4, in the portion *Nitzavim*. The Jews also pray in their *Selichot* <term>Selichot: Penitential prayers recited during fast days and the period leading up to the High Holy Days.</term>, under the title *Tzom Gedaliah* <note>The Fast of Gedaliah, observed after Rosh Hashanah.</note>, in a prayer that begins: *Esrachi me’ever hannahaar* (The native from beyond the river), in such a manner: <note>original: הב כי עליך משליכים יהב</note> that is, **Deliver your people from the Haf haf (that is, Christendom), for upon You they (the Israelites) cast their burden.**

<margin>XLV. It is also called Madhéfa.</margin>
Forty-fifthly, the same is called מדהבה *Madhéfa*, which name is taken from *Isaiah* 14:4, where it is spoken of Babylon; and the same comes from the Chaldean word דהב *dehab*, which means gold, and is interpreted by some as "greedy for gold" or "gold-collecting," but by others as "gold-tax" or "tribute." # Chapter XVIII of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked. 802

The word *Edom*—which stands explicitly in the book of *Isaiah*—has been changed to *Greece*; however, in the old Venetian print, it will read differently. In such a way, in Rabbi *Meir Arama’s* explanation of the Psalms, which is called *Meir Tehillôth* <term>Meir Tehilloth: "Light of the Psalms," a commentary by the 15th-century philosopher and scholar Meir ben Isaac Arama</term>, on *Psalm* 80, verse 14, it is read: <gloss>יכרסמנה חזיר מיער הוא ין</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: "Yekharsmenah hazir mi-ya'ar hu Yan [Javan]"</note>; that is, "A wild boar will tear it apart"; this (wild boar) signifies *Javan*, that is, Greece, even though by the wild boar, Christendom is understood, as can be seen above on page 778, etc. <note>In Christian-Jewish polemics of this era, the "wild boar" of Psalm 80 was often interpreted by Jewish commentators as a symbol for Rome, and by extension, the Christian Church.</note>

<margin>Babylon.</margin>
As far as the name *Babel* <note>Babylon</note> is concerned, it is read in the *Benschbuch* <term>Benschbuch: A popular book containing the Grace After Meals and various blessings, from the Yiddish "benshen" (to bless)</term> folio 15, column 1, under the title *Semirôth lejôm Schabbath* <note>Songs for the Sabbath Day</note>, in a prayer which begins <gloss>דרור יקרא לבן עם בת וגו'</gloss> <note>original: "Derôr jíkra lebén im bath" — Freedom shall be proclaimed for son and daughter</note>, etc., in which the Jews pray thus: <gloss>פורה בתוך בצרה וגם בכל אשר גברה נתוץ צרי באף ועברה</gloss>; That is, "Tread the winepress in the midst of *Bozra*" (that is, in *Rome*, as was indicated above on page 731) "as also in *Babel*, which has become mighty. Destroy my enemies in wrath and anger." But that *Babel* here is understood as *Edom*, that is, Christendom, is clearly to be seen from *Isaiah* 63, verses 1, 2, and 3, where the treading of the winepress in **Edom** is mentioned. Thus, in the Prague *Machsor* <term>Machsor: A prayer book used for the Jewish High Holy Days and festivals</term> in the second part, folio 79, column 1, the word *Adúna* is explained through *Edom*, by which Christendom is understood; but in the Wilmersdorf *Machsor*, in the 1st part, folio 196, column 2, it is explained through *Babel*.

<margin>Syria.</margin>
The name *Aram*, that is, *Syria*, is often read in the *Rabbôth* <note>The Midrash Rabbah, a collection of ancient homiletic interpretations of the Torah</note> printed at Wilmersdorf in place of *Edom*; and it is written in *Bereschîth rabba* <note>Genesis Rabbah</note> folio 4, column 4, in the 43rd *Parascha* <term>Parascha: A designated weekly section of the Torah</term>, regarding *Genesis* 15, verse 9, in such a way: <gloss>עגלה משולשת זו בבל וגו' ועז משולשת זו מדי וגו' ואיל משולש זו יון וגו' ותור וגוזל זו ארם תור הוא אלא שגזלן هو :</gloss> That is, "The three-year-old heifer signifies *Babel*; the three-year-old goat signifies *Media*, etc. The three-year-old ram signifies Greece, etc. *Vetor vegôsal*, that is, but the turtle-dove and young pigeon signify *Aram*, that is, *Syria*. It is a turtle-dove, but it is a *gaslan*, that is, a robber." Thus, with the word *gaslan*, which means a robber, the word *gôsal* is alluded to and aimed at, which signifies a young pigeon. So too, immediately following on folio 41, column 1, twice, and in *Vajikra rabba* <note>Leviticus Rabbah</note> folio 146, column 3 and 4, in the text and the commentary, *Aram* is found six times in place of *Edom*.

<margin>Land of the Moors.</margin>
As for the name *Cusch*, that is, the *Land of the Moors* <note>In this period, "Mohrenland" or Cush generally referred to Ethiopia or the regions of sub-Saharan Africa</note>, it stands in the thick *Tephilla* <term>Tephilla: A common term for the Siddur, or daily prayer book</term> folio 44, column 3, under the title *Józer leschabbáth haggadól* <note>A liturgical poem for the "Great Sabbath" immediately preceding Passover</note>, in a prayer which reads as follows: <gloss>כשמע מצרים משא דומה כמשא : ממצרים נפרעת מפתרוס בתכלית מכח עשירית באדום תפרע בתכלית קרן עשירית</gloss>; That is, "Let the cry of *Cusch*, that is, the *Land of the Moors*, be heard, just as the cry of *Egypt* was (when it was visited with the ten plagues...

From there the nations were divided into 70 nations, as it is written: 'And from these the nations were divided on the earth,' etc. And regarding this, Moses our teacher said: 'When He separated the sons of man,' etc., that they are 70 according to the number of the children of Israel, who were 70 souls," etc.</note>; that is: "It is known that there are seventy nations in the world, which have all come from seventy men who all sprang from the loins of Noah; and from there the heathens were divided into seventy nations (which they call <term>Ummóth</term> *Ummóth* or *Ummós*, that is, Nations, and..."

In this manner, there are seventy nations of the world, and with Israel, seventy-one. This is all a likeness of the seventy angels who are above and surround the Throne of Glory, who, together with the Lord, the God of Israel, make seventy-one; they are called His Council. The same can also be found there in *folio 162, column 2*, in the <term>Parashat Behaalothecha: The Torah portion 'When you set up' (Numbers 8:1–12:16)</term>.

These seventy angels are said to have been signified by the seventy palm trees mentioned in Exodus 15, verse 27, about which **Rabbi Menachem of Recanati** <note>Menachem Recanati (1250–1310), an Italian kabbalist who sought to explain the mystical meaning of the Torah.</note> teaches in his commentary on the Five Books of Moses, *folio 74, column 4*, in the <term>Parashat Vayeshev: The Torah portion 'And he dwelt' (Genesis 37:1–40:23)</term> in this way: <margin>These 70 angels are said to have been signified by 70 palm trees.</margin> <note>original Hebrew: יש כבוד למעלה מכבוד והתחתונים רמו לעליונים ושבעים נפש רמזים לשבעים מלאכים הסובבים כסא הכבוד הממונים על האומות וזהו שנ' ושם שתים עשרה עינות מים ושבעים תמרים</note> That is: There is one glory above another glory, and the lower things have significance for the upper things. The seventy souls (of which mention is made in Exodus 1, verse 5) have a significance regarding the seventy angels who surround the Throne of Glory and are set over the nations; and this is what is said (Exodus 15, verse 27): "There were twelve wells of water, and 70 palm trees." **Rabbi Bechai** <note>Bahya ben Asher (c. 1255–1340), a Spanish rabbi and scholar known for his commentary on the Torah which incorporates literal, philosophical, and mystical interpretations.</note> also writes about this in his commentary on the Five Books of Moses, *folio 82, column 4*, in the <term>Parashat Beshallach: The Torah portion 'When he let go' (Exodus 13:17–17:16)</term> as follows: <note>original Hebrew: ושבעים תמרים הם ע' מלאכים הסובבים כסא הכבוד וממונים על ע' אומות שבעולם כל אחד ואחד ממונה על אומתו</note> That is: The seventy palm trees signify the seventy angels who surround the Throne of Glory and are set over the seventy nations of the world, and each one is placed over his own people.

As for the time when the aforementioned seventy angels were set over the seventy nations, it is said to have happened at the time of the dispersion during the building of the **Babylonian Tower** <note>The Tower of Babel.</note>, regarding which it is written in **Rabbi Menachem of Recanati's** commentary on the Five Books of Moses, *folio 41, columns 3 and 4*, in the <term>Parashat Noach: The Torah portion 'Noah' (Genesis 6:9–11:32)</term>, concerning the words of Genesis 10, verse 5: <margin>From what time these 70 angels have been set over the 70 nations.</margin> **"By these were the islands of the Gentiles divided"** as follows: <note>original Hebrew: בפסוק זה נרמז כי בדור הפלגה נתן לכל אומה חלקה מן הארץ ושר אחד למעלה עליה : וכן כולם שבעים והם שבעים ענפים מן האילן העליון שבעים שרים הסובבים כסא הכבוד והם הנקראים בשיר השירים השומרים הסובבים בעיר כי על ידיהם באים הגזירות של מעלה והם שומרים ומליצים כל אחד על אומתו ונשאר חלק יי' מן האומות שנ' כי חלק יי' עמו כי יעקב חבל לו יה וכתיב חלקי יי' אמרה נפשי , העם בחר לנחלה לו ומן הארצות ארץ ישראל שאין עליה שר ומושל רק השם יתעלה ויתברך זהו סוד כי שמך נקרא על עירך ועל עמך</note> That is: In this little verse it is indicated that at the time of the division (of the nations during the building of the Babylonian Tower), to every nation its portion of the earth was given, as well as a Prince above over the same...

### How many Nations are in the World, and who governs them.

<margin>over whom they are set.</margin>
<note>original Hebrew: שרים הממונים על ע' אומות השרים האלה הם הנקראים אלהי העמים והשם הנכבד הוא אלהי האלהים והוא שרן של ישראל והם עמו ונחלתו</note> The princes who are appointed over the seventy nations; these princes are those called the "gods of the peoples," and the Honored Name <note>A common Jewish periphrasis for the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note> is the God of gods, and He is the prince of Israel, and they are His people and His inheritance. That is: From the seventy branches hang the seventy princes—who are set over the seventy nations—one with another; and these same princes are called the "gods of the nations," but the praiseworthy **God** is a **God** of gods, and the Prince of the Israelites, and they are His people and His inheritance. Rabbi Menachem Zion <note>Menachem Zion bar Meir (14th century), a kabbalist known for his commentary on the Torah.</note> teaches in his interpretation of the Five Books of Moses, folio 105, column 1, in the section *Haazinu*, concerning this also in such a manner: <note>original Hebrew: דע כאשר הובדלו ע' לשונות לע' אומות בזמן הפלוגה איש איש ללשונו למשפחותם לגוייהם נתן השם ית' חלק לכל אומה ואומה מכדור הארץ שהם שבע אקלימים כפי מאמר חכמי שמים וכל אקלים נחלק לעשרה שהם ע' נתייחדו או הגוים והארצות כל אחד לשר ידוע והם נקראים אלהי עמים וכן נחלקו ע' אומות לע' שרים ולא נמצא האל ית' חלק בכולם לפי שהוא טהור על כן אינם בני גילו ומין במינו אבל יעקב חבל נחלתו וימצא טהור את טהור וכן נאמר כי יעקב בחר לו יה וגו'</note> That is: Know, that at the time of the separation <note>Referring to the Tower of Babel, when humanity was divided into seventy languages.</note> when the seventy languages were distinguished among the seventy nations, and every nation was set apart according to its language, according to its families, and according to its people, that the blessed **God** gave to every nation a portion of the globe of the earth. According to the statement of the observers of the heavens (or astrologers), this globe consists of seven climates <note>term: climates (climatibus). In ancient geography, these were latitudinal zones of the earth.</note>, and every climate is divided into ten parts, which according to the seven climates makes seventy parts. At that time, every nation and land was assigned to a certain prince, and these same (princes) are called the "gods of the nations." Thus the seventy nations were divided among the seventy princes, and the blessed **God** found no portion in all of them, because He is pure: therefore they are not children of His likeness, and no species of His species; but Jacob is the portion of His possession, and one who is pure has found another who is pure; and thus it is said (Psalm 135, verse 4): "For the **Lord** hath chosen Jacob unto himself." For such a reason they are also called *Elohim*, that is, "gods," as may be seen in the small *Yalkut Reubeni* <note>A 17th-century collection of Kabbalistic midrashim by Reuben Hoeshke.</note>, under the title *Zakhut* (or Merit), number 5, and in the *Zioni*, folio 49, column 4: and it is forbidden for the Jews to curse them, as may be read in the *Yalkut Chadash*, folio 78, column 1, number 32, under the title *Chattaim*. Thus they are also called <note>original Hebrew: אלהים אחרים</note> *Elohim acherim*, that is, "other gods," in the interpretation of Rabbi Moshe bar Nachman <note>Also known as Nachmanides (1194–1270), a leading medieval Jewish scholar.</note> on the Five Books of Moses, folio 59, column 3, in the section *Jethro*.

...in the translation of Jonathan concerning Genesis 11, verses 7 and 8, the following is also found regarding the confusion of languages: <note>original Hebrew: אמור י"י לשבעין מלאכיא דקיימין קומוי אתון : נחות ונבלבלה תמן לישנהון דלא ישמעון אינש לשון חבריה ואתגלי מימרא די"י עלוי קרתא ועמיה שבעין מלאכיא כל קבל שבעין עממיא וכל חד וחד לישן עממיה וטופס כתביה בידיה ובדינון מתמן על אנפי כל ארעא לשבעין לישנין ולא הוה ידע חד מה דימר חבריה והוו קטלין דין לדין ופסקו מלמבני קרתא</note> "That is, God said to the seventy angels who stand before Him: 'Come now, and let us go down, and there confuse their language, so that none understands the language of his companion.' <margin>There are said to have been people who understood all seventy languages.</margin>
Mordechai is said to have understood all seventy languages, concerning which it is written in the Talmudic tractate *Megilla*, folio 13, column 2, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: מרדכי מיושבי לשכת הגזית היה והיה יודע בשבעים לשון</note> "That is: Mordechai was one of those who resided in the court built of hewn stones (in which the judges of the great Sanhedrin <term>The supreme judicial and religious council of ancient Israel</term> or Council stayed) and understood the seventy languages." Something about this is also to be found in the tractate *Shekalim*, folio 7, column 1. Likewise, in the tractate *Sotah*, folio 36, column 2, and in Rabbi Bahya's <term>Bahya ben Asher (1255–1340), a Spanish commentator</term> explanation of the five books of Moses, folio 21, column 1, in the section *Noach*, it is read of Joseph that he understood the aforementioned seventy languages. And in the *Maase-Buch* <term>A popular collection of Jewish legends and folktales, literally the "Story Book"</term> it is written in the 143rd chapter that Rabbi Channina also knew all such languages, which he had learned from a spirit who stayed with him in the form of a frog. Similarly, it is reported in the 193rd chapter of the mentioned *Maase-Buch* that another learned the mentioned seventy languages, as well as the languages of animals and birds, from the Leviathan, the king of the fish, and immediately thereafter spoke with two ravens, one of whom is said to have revealed a great treasure to him.

<margin>The aforementioned seventy angels are also said to move the celestial globes or spheres.</margin>
These seventy princes are also said to move the *globos cœlestes* <note>Latin: "celestial globes"</note> or heavenly spheres, concerning which it is written in Abarbenel's <term>Isaac Abarbenel (1437–1508), a Jewish statesman and philosopher</term> book *Ma'ayanei HaYeshu'ah* <note>Hebrew: "Springs of Salvation"</note>, folio 69, column 4, in the second *Tamar* of the eleventh *Ma'ayan*, where these princes are discussed: <note>original Hebrew: הרא"בע פירש בענין השרים האלה שהם הכוכבים והמזלות כי יש לכל אומה ולשון ולכל עיר ועיר מזל לו משפיע עליו כפי ההשגחה הכוללת. ויותר נראה דעת הרמ"בן בפירוש התורה שהשרים האלה הם שכלים נבדלים נקראים מלאכים רוחניים המניעים את הגלגלים וגו'</note> "That is: Rabbi Aben Esra <term>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167), a Spanish polymath</term> explained regarding these princes that they are the stars and constellations, for every nation and language and every city has its constellation that influences it according to general providence. But the opinion of Ramban <term>Nachmanides (1194–1270), a leading medieval Jewish scholar</term> in his commentary on the Torah seems more likely: that these princes are separate intellects called spiritual angels who move the spheres, etc."

# The Eighteenth Chapter of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.

...often by these princes, interpreting them to be the stars and planets, since every nation, every language, and every city has a star that rules over it and exerts its influence, as is commonly understood. However, I prefer the opinion of *Rabbi Mosche bar Nachmans* <note>Also known as Nahmanides, a leading medieval Jewish scholar</note> in his commentary on the Law (or the five books of Moses), which suggests that such princes are *Intelligentiæ separatæ* <note>original Latin: "separated intelligences"</note>, or detached spirits, who are called spiritual angels and move the (heavenly) spheres, etc. For this reason, in the commentary of *Rabbi Menachem von Rekanat* on the five books of Moses, folio 206, column 1, in the *Parashah Shofetim* <term>Parashah: a weekly portion of the Torah read in Jewish services</term>, they are called the souls of such spheres, with these words: <note>original Hebrew: הודענו כי יש למזלות שרים ינהיגו אותם והם נפשות לכדורי הגלגלים</note> that is, "We have already indicated that the constellations have princes who govern them, and these are the souls of the spheres of the globes." Likewise, in the commentary of *Rabbi Bechai* on the five books of Moses, folio 9, column 3, in the *Parashah Bereshith* <note>The first portion of the Book of Genesis</note>, it is read: <note>original Hebrew: המלאכים הם נפש לגלגלים</note> that is, "The angels are the soul of the spheres."

<margin>
Each of them is also said to give his people their sustenance and to provide for them.
</margin>
Furthermore, it is said of the mentioned seventy princes that each one provides for his people, giving them their sustenance and rest, and that on the New Year's Day <note>Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year</note> judgment is held over them and their subordinate nations; as well as that they were all once bound. Regarding how each one provides for his people and procures their sustenance, it is written thus in the book *Avodáth* (or *Avódas*) *hakkódesch* <note>A work on Kabbalah</note>, in the twelfth chapter of the third part, which is called *Chélek hattháchlith*, folio 70, column 2: <note>original Hebrew: כל זמן שישראל עושין רצונו של מקום אין הנהגתם על ידי אמצעי כי אם בכבודו ובעצמו מנהיגם ומשגיח עליהם: ואם לשאר האומות יש שרים וכל אומה מתנהגת ומושגחת על ידי השר שלה הכל בכח שם יתברך שהוא הפרנס הגדול המפרנס ומחלק להם כדי פרנסתם והם מפרנסים שאר האומות שהם ממונים עליהם</note> that is, "As long as the Israelites do the will of God, they are not governed by a mediator, but GOD Himself governs and provides for them. Although the other nations also have princes, and every nation is governed and provided for by its prince, all of this happens through the power of the Name of the Lord, the great Sustainer (or Preserver), who maintains them and distributes to them their sufficient sustenance, after which they nourish the other nations over which they are appointed." That these [princes], together with their subject nations, are judged on the New Year's Day is taught in the book **Sha'are Orah** <note>original: "Gates of Light," a foundational 13th-century Kabbalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla</note> printed in **Mantua**, **folio 65, column 1**, as follows:

> That is: **Know** and believe that all the nations, together with their princes, who are called **Elohim** (that is, gods), come at the beginning of the year (or on the New Year's Day <note>Rosh Hashanah</note>), so that they may be judged before the blessed **God**; and when the nations have not conducted themselves properly, their princes are smitten, and the abundance (of sustenance) and the good, which the blessed **God** has given them, is diminished (or withdrawn). When also a nation's prince is smitten, the nation falls; and this is what the prophet (**Isaiah 24:21**) says: "The Lord will punish the host of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth." And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: "No nation falls unless its prince falls first." The reason is that according to the judgment passed on the prince of that nation, so his nation receives, for good or for evil, etc. And for all the sins the nations of the world commit, their princes are smitten for their transgressions. And this is what the prince of Abimelech, king of the Philistines, said: "And I also withheld you from sinning against me." <note>Genesis 20:6</note> The word *mechato* <note>meaning "from sinning"</note> is written without the letter *aleph*, as if the prince said to him: "Know that from the hour you sinned by taking Sarah, Abraham's wife, they judged me in the heavenly court and thrust needles (*machatim*) and thorns into me, and I am in great pain." For this "God" <note>Elohim</note> who spoke with Abimelech was the prince of Abimelech.

<margin>They are also called Keliphoth, which means shells or rinds.</margin>
These same entities are also called <term>Keliphoth</term> <note>original Hebrew: קליפות, meaning "shells," "husks," or "rinds." # Chapter XVIII of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked.

<margin>Why they are called Kliphoth.</margin>
Princes / who are the outermost <term>Kliphoth<note>original: "Kelifóth." In Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), these are the "shells" or "husks" of impurity that represent the forces of evil that surround and conceal the divine light.</note></term> or shells / who reside outside the holy sphere / for the godless walk in a circle. So it is also written in the book *Ma'arekhet HaElahut* <note>original: "Maarécheth haëlahúth," a 14th-century work that systematically explains the Sephirot (divine attributes).</note> (or *Ma'arekhes HaElohus*) folio 60, column 1, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: קליפות שהם שרי האומות סביב לארץ</note> "The Kliphoth, who are the princes of the nations, are all around the earth."

They are called *Kliphoth*, that is, shells or rinds, for this reason: because they are on the outside surrounding heaven, just as a shell is around a fruit; therefore, in the book *Sha'are Tzedek* <note>original: "Scháare Zédek," meaning "The Gates of Justice," a 13th-century Kabbalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla.</note> folio 2, column 4, it is read: <note>original Hebrew: והשם יתברך שוכן בהיכל הפנימי והשרים מקיפים כמו כדמיון הקר : והקליפות</note> "The blessed LORD dwells in the innermost palace / and the princes surround His throne / just as the shell surrounds the fruit." And in the great *Yalkut Reuveni* <note>A 17th-century anthology of mystical Midrashim.</note> it is taught on folio 70, column 2, in the <term>Parashah<note>A weekly Torah portion read in synagogue services.</note></term> *Vayeshev*, from the aforementioned book *Sha'are Tzedek*: <note>original Hebrew: דע כי יש שבעים שרים ממונים על שבעים אומות ואותן שבעים שרים סובבים חוץ לכסא הכבוד והם נקראים סוד הקליפה</note> "Know that there are seventy princes appointed over the seventy nations / and these same seventy princes circle outside the Throne of Glory, and they are called the 'Secret of the Shell.'" <margin>Why he is called Sammael.</margin>
Regarding the origin of the name Sammael, it is written in the 30th chapter of the second part of the book *Moreh Nevukhim* <note>The "Guide for the Perplexed" by Moses Maimonides.</note> folio 109, column 1, in the commentary *Shem Tov* <note>A commentary by Shem Tov ben Joseph ibn Shem Tov.</note>: **סמאל שמסמא האדם ומעוותו מהדרך הנכונה :** <note>original Hebrew: "Sammael she-mesamma ha-adam u-me'avvato me-ha-derekh ha-nekhonah"</note> that is, **Sammael is so named (from *Simma*, which means to blind) because he blinds man and turns him from the right path.** This is also stated there in the commentary *Ephodi*. Rabbi Isaac Karo <note>A 15th-century Spanish scholar and uncle of Joseph Karo.</note> teaches in his interpretation of the five books of Moses, *Toledot Yitzchak*, folio 76, column 1, in the *Parashah Akarei Mot* (or *Mos*), the following concerning this: **שסמאל יודה שמו על שמו שהוא סם המות ועוד שעומד לשמאלו של אדם ועוד שגור מלשון סומא לפי שמקבל שוחד** <note>original Hebrew: "She-Sammael yodeh shemo al shemo she-hu sam ha-mavet ve-od she-omed li-semalo shel adam ve-od she-gar mi-leshon suma lefi she-mekabbel shokhad"</note> [that the name Sammael testifies about itself: that he is the **Poison of Death** (*Sam Ha-mavet*); and furthermore, that he stands at the **left side** (*Semol*) of man; and also that the word is derived from **blind** (*Suma*), because he takes bribes...]

# How many nations there are in the world, and who rules them.

**And it is written: "A bribe blinds";** <note>original Hebrew: "וכתוב השוחד יעור" (v’khathuv ha-shochad ye’aver)</note> that is: Know that the name of **Sammael** indicates his nature; for he is **Poison of Death** <note>original: "Sam hammáveth" (or "hammóves")</note>—that is, a poison of death (or a deadly poison). He also stands on the **left side** <note>original: "Semól"</note> of man. Furthermore, he is named from the word **Blind** <note>original: "Sóme"</note> because he takes bribes; for it is written (*Exodus 23:8* and *Deuteronomy 16:19*): **A bribe makes one blind.** More on this subject can also be found in the <term>Parashah<note>The weekly portion of the Torah read in the synagogue.</note></term> *Acharei Mot*. Regarding the fact that he accepts bribes, this will be discussed in the following sections.

<margin>The Satan.</margin>

<margin>The evil nature.</margin>

But here (*Job 2:6*) it is written: "But spare his soul" (that is, spare his life). # Chapter XVIII of the First Part of Judaism Unveiled.

When he brings a charge against someone (stating that they have incurred debt or have sinned), he is called **Satan** (which means an **Adversary**). But if he takes someone’s life, he is named **Malach hammaveth** <note>original Hebrew: מַלְאָךְ הַמָּוֶת</note>, which is to say, the **Angel of Death**. These three names are also given to him in Rabbi Bechaye’s <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish kabbalist famous for his commentary on the Torah.</note> commentary on the five books of Moses, folio 13, column 1, in the <term>Parashah<note>The weekly portion of the Torah read in the synagogue.</note></term> *Acharei Mot*.

<margin>The Old Serpent, or the Serpent.</margin>
### **Fourthly**, he is called **Nachasch hakkadmoni** <note>original Hebrew: נחש הקדמוני</note>, that is, the **Old Serpent**; and **Nachasch bariach** <note>original Hebrew: נחש בריח</note>, that is, the **straight or evil serpent**; or also simply **Nachasch** <note>original Hebrew: נחש</note>, which means the **Serpent**. The name *Nachasch hakkadmoni*, or the Old Serpent, appears in the book *Ziyoni* <note>A 14th-century kabbalistic commentary by Menahem Zioni.</note>, folio 85, column 4, in the *Parashah Korach*, with these words: **The Old Serpent is Sammael.** <note>original Hebrew: נחש הקדמוני הוא סמאל</note> Likewise, in the book *Zeror Hammor* <note>"A Bundle of Myrrh," a commentary by Abraham Saba.</note> folio 46, column 2, in the *Parashah Vayishlach*, it is said of Jacob: **Because he delayed on the way, the Old Serpent bit him, which is the Satan, the evil nature <note>original German: "die böse Art," referring to the *Yetzer hara* or evil inclination.</note>, the hunter, and Sammael.** <note>original Hebrew: שהיה מתאחר בדרך נשכו נחש הקדמוני הוא שטן הוא סמאל</note> The name *Nachasch bariach*, that is, the straight <note>In biblical Hebrew, this often refers to a "fleeing" or "slanting" serpent, but the author translates it as "straight" or "bad/evil."</note> serpent, is found in the book *Emek Hammelech* <note>"The Valley of the King," a 17th-century kabbalistic work by Naphtali Herz ben Jacob Elhanan.</note> folio 84, column 3, at the beginning of the 14th chapter, under the title *Shaar Kiryath Arba*, where the words read as follows: **Sammael is called the straight serpent, etc., but Lilith (or Lilis) is called the crooked serpent.** <note>original Hebrew: סמאל נקרא נחש בריח וגו' ולילית נקראת נחש עקלתון</note> This is also found on folio 22, column 2, in the aforementioned book *Emek Hammelech*, in the 36th chapter, under the title *Shaar Olam Hatohu*, though with slightly altered words; as well as in the book *Pardes Rimmonim* <note>"Orchard of Pomegranates" by Moses Cordovero.</note> folio 185, column 4, under the title *Shaar Hechele Temuroth*. The name *Nachasch*, that is, the Serpent, is read in the book *Zeror Hammor* folio 143, column 2, in the *Parashah Ki Tetze*, where it is written: **That Hater (or enemy, mentioned in Proverbs 25:21) signifies Sammael, who is the Serpent, the Satan, and the evil nature, who seduced the first man and lures all creatures after him through his smooth words—which are smoother than oil—into human deeds and pleasures.** <note>original Hebrew: שונא הוא רמז לסמאל הוא נחש הוא שטן הוא יצר הרע : והטעה לאדם הראשון ומשעה הבריות כולם אחריו רכו משמן בענייני האנשים והתענוגים</note> In the same manner, he is called this in the *Yalkut Chadash* <note>A 17th-century collection of midrashic and kabbalistic teachings.</note> folio 87, column 2, number 78, under the title *Jacob*, and in Rabbi Menachem of Recanati’s <note>A 13th-14th century Italian kabbalist.</note> commentary on the five books of Moses, folio 149, column 2, in the *Parashah Metzora*.

# How Many Nations are in the World, and Who Governs Them.

In the book *Zeror Hammor* <note>original title: "A Bundle of Myrrh," a 15th-century commentary by Abraham Saba.</note>, folio 111, column 1, it is read: **The *Ruach hattuma* <note>original Hebrew: רוח הטומאה</note> or unclean spirit is the evil nature <note>original Hebrew: יצר הרע (*yetzer hara*), the internal inclination toward evil.</note> and the Angel of Death.** This same sentiment is found in Rabbi Menachem of Recanati’s <note>A 13th-century Italian kabbalist.</note> commentary on the five books of Moses, folio 149, column 1, in the <term>Parashah<note>The weekly Torah portion.</note></term> *Kedoshim*, with these words: **Do not wander after the work of the old serpent, which is called the *Ruach mesa'ava* <note>original Hebrew: רוח מסאבא</note>, that is, the unclean spirit.**

So too is he said to have appeared in the form of Esau, regarding which it is read in the large *Yalkut Reubeni* folio 62, column 2, in the *Parashah Vayishlach*, from the *Zohar*: <note>original Hebrew/Aramaic: כי חמא יעקב לסמאל מקטרגא בהאי לילה חמא ליה בהאי דיוקנא דעשו ולא אשתמודע עד דסליק צפרא כיון דסליק צפרא ואשגח ביה חמא ליה באנפין סתימין ואתגליין אסתכל בההוא דיוקנא דהוה כדיוקנא דעשו וזהו וזהו ראיתי פניך כראות פני אלהים דחמי דאינון בדיוקנא דאתחזי ליה סמאל</note> **When Jacob saw the accuser Sammael in that same night, he saw him in the form of Esau, and did not recognize him until the dawn broke; and when he had contemplated him, he saw him with a hidden face. **Twenty-firstly**, he is called <term>Kez kol basar</term> <note>original Hebrew: קץ כל בשר</note>, which means **The End of All Flesh**, words which are found in Genesis 6:13. **Twenty-thirdly**, he is called <term>Sáraf meófef</term> <note>original Hebrew: שרף מעופף</note>, which means **the fiery flying serpent**, as can be seen in Rabbi Bechai’s <note>Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century commentator.</note> explanation of the Five Books of Moses, folio 180, column 4, in the section *Balak*, where he is named: <note>original Hebrew: המקטרג הגדול שיש לישראל בשמים והוא שר המדבר שרף מעופף ונפש גלגל מאדים</note> that is: **The great accuser whom the Israelites have in heaven, who is the Prince of the Wilderness, the fiery flying serpent, and the soul of the sphere or globe of (the planet) Mars.**

# How many nations there are in the world / and who governs them. 829

"What is this that you have given me to eat, so that my teeth have become blunt <note>The German word *stumpff* mirrors the Hebrew *qahah*, referring to a dull or set-on-edge sensation in the teeth, symbolizing the bitter onset of mortality.</note>?" Thus, the teeth of all creatures also became blunt. All of this can be found in greater detail in the Talmud printed in Amsterdam, in the <term>Tractate Avot of Rabbi Nathan</term> <note>A secondary work of the Talmud that expands on the 'Ethics of the Fathers,' containing various ethical teachings and legends.</note>, folio 1, column 2; and in the chapters of <term>Rabbi Eliezer</term> <note>The *Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer*, an 8th-century collection of biblical exegesis and legends.</note>, in the 13th chapter; as well as in the <term>Sêpher habbáhir</term> <note>original: "Book of Brightness," one of the earliest works of Kabbalah (Jewish mysticism).</note>, folio 12, column 3 and 4. In this last book, it is taught that Satan pushed Eve against the tree with force; and because she touched it in such a manner and did not die, he said to her: "Just as you did not die from touching it, you will also not die if you eat from it." Thereupon, she ate of the fruit and gave some to her husband as well.

<margin>All animals are also said to have eaten from the forbidden fruit / except for the Phoenix bird</margin>
It is also read in the <term>Medrasch Schemuël</term> <note>A homiletic commentary on the Books of Samuel.</note> folio 55, column 3 and 4, in the twelfth <term>Parascha</term> <note>A section or chapter of the text.</note>, that she gave all the animals some of it to eat, except for the bird <term>Phœnix</term>, which refused to eat of it. The words are as follows: <note>original Hebrew: הכל שמעו לחוה... "All obeyed Eve and ate from that tree; as it is written: 'and she also gave to her husband with her and he ate.' She also fed the cattle, the wild beasts, and the birds, except for one bird named Chol, of which it is written: 'Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the Chol (sand/phoenix).' Rabbi Jannai said: It lives a thousand years; after a thousand years, a fire comes from its nest and consumes it, and something like an egg remains of it, and it grows limbs again and lives."</note> This is to say: Everyone obeyed Eve and ate from that same (forbidden) tree. This is what is written in Genesis 3:6: **And she gave some to her husband also / and he ate.** She also gave it to the cattle, the wild animals, and the birds to eat, except for one bird which is called <term>Chol</term>, that is, the <term>Phœnix</term>. This is what is written in Job 29:18: **I thought / I will die in my nest / and make my days as many as the Chol,** (that is, according to the foolish opinion of the Jews, like the bird <term>Phœnix</term>; yet it should actually mean 'like the sand,' for <term>Chol</term> in the Hebrew language signifies sand and not such a bird). It stands written: "like the <term>Chol</term>" etc. Rabbi Jannai said: It lives a thousand years; after the thousand years, a fire goes out from its nest and consumes it, and something like an egg remains therein, and its limbs grow back, and it becomes alive again. This is also found in the <term>Jalkut Schimôni</term> <note>A massive medieval compilation of midrashic interpretations of the Hebrew Bible.</note> regarding Job, folio 152, column 1, number 517; and in the book <term>Emek hammélech</term> <note>The "King’s Valley," a 17th-century Kabbalistic text.</note> folio 83, column 1, in the 8th chapter, under the title <term>Schâar Kirjáth árba</term>. Rabbi Salomon Jarchi <note>Also known as Rashi, the preeminent medieval French commentator on the Bible and Talmud.</note> also writes of this in his interpretation of the quoted words of Job 29:18, **And will make the days many like the Chol**, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: עוף ושמו חול... "There is a bird named Chol, and the punishment of death was not decreed upon it because it did not taste from the Tree of Knowledge; at the end of a thousand years, it renews itself and returns to its youth."</note> This is: **It is a bird / which is called Chol / and the same was not punished with death / because it did not taste of the tree**

<margin>What the Jews further write regarding Sammael's envy and jealousy which he harbored against Adam.</margin>
Regarding the aforementioned envy and jealousy, it is written as follows in the commentary of the mentioned <term>Rabbi Menachem of Recanati</term> <note>An Italian rabbi and kabbalist (c. 1250–1310) known for incorporating mystical traditions into his Torah commentaries.</note> on the Five Books of Moses, folio 29, column 2, in the <term>Parashah Bereshit</term> <note>The first section of the Torah, covering the creation of the world.</note>, derived from the <term>Midrash Ruth</term> <note>A homiletic commentary on the biblical Book of Ruth.</note>:

> <note>original Hebrew: "כשברא הק"בה..."</note> When the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create the first man, He built him from the Temple; He took dust from the site of the Temple and created him. Once He had created him and he stood upon his feet, all creatures came to bow down before him. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He took him from there and placed him in Paradise, and made for him ten wedding canopies, after the likeness of those ten wedding canopies which the Holy One, blessed be He, will make for the righteous in Paradise in the time to come. And the ministering angels descended and made merry before him; God gave him the highest wisdom. But when <term>Sammael</term> <note>In Jewish tradition, the primary accuser or archangel of death, often associated with the serpent in Eden.</note> descended from the heights of heaven and saw Adam’s glory—that the ministering angels were serving him at his wedding—it displeased him <note>literally: "his eyes were evil before him," an idiom for jealousy.</note>. What did he do? He took a serpent, which had the form of a kind of camel, and rode upon it, and came down and seduced him until he had transgressed the command of his Creator. 

That is: When the holy blessed God wished to create the first human, He built the same from the Temple, and took from the dust of the Temple, and created him. After He had now created him, and he had stood upon his feet, all creatures came to bow before him. What did the holy blessed God do? But when Sammael came down from heaven, and saw Adam's glory, and that the ministering angels served him at his wedding, it displeased him. What did he do? He took a serpent, which had the shape of a camel, rode upon the same, and came down and seduced him, until he had transgressed the command of his Creator.

Regarding this Sammael, the Rabbis also write that he slept with Eve and fathered Cain, about which one may read in the *Yalkut Chadash* <note>original: *Jalkut chádasch*; a 17th-century collection of kabbalistic and midrashic teachings.</note>, folio 4, column 3, number 12, under the title "Adam," as follows: She was impregnated by Sammael, etc., and Eve saw the likeness of Cain, that he was not of the lower beings but of the upper beings, and she looked and said: "I have acquired a man from the LORD" (Genesis 4:1). <note>original Hebrew: בה נתעברה מסמאל וגו׳ וארהת חוה את דמות קין שלא היה מן התחתונים אלא מן העליונים והביטה ותאמר קניתי איש את יי׳ :</note> That is: Eve was made pregnant by Sammael and conceived Cain, etc. Now, when Eve saw Cain’s form and considered that he was not from the lower (creatures) but from the upper (beings), she said (Genesis 4:1): **"I have gotten the man from the LORD."**

It also stands in folio 4, column 4, number 43, in the aforementioned *Yalkut Chadash*: Sammael cast filth into Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain, and his appearance was not like the rest of the sons of men. <note>original Hebrew: סמאל על חוה הטיל בה זוהמא ואתעברת ואולדת ית קין וחזיו דיליה לא הוה דמי לשאר בני נשא :</note> That is: Sammael slept with Eve and cast a foulness <note>The Hebrew term *Zuhama* refers to a spiritual or physical impurity/venom left by the serpent.</note> into her, from which she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain, whose form was not like other human beings. Rabbi Menachem of Recanati <note>A 14th-century Italian kabbalist who wrote an influential commentary on the Torah.</note> writes in his explanation of the Five Books of Moses, folio 31, columns 1 and 2, in the portion *Bereshit* <note>The first section of Genesis.</note>, concerning the words of Genesis 4:1, **"And Adam knew his wife Eve,"** the following: Know that Cain was born from the impurity and the drop which the serpent cast into Eve, etc. Moreover, without the human seed of Adam being mixed with that impurity, it would not have been possible for that spirit to clothe itself in a human body and come forth into the air of the world; thus, Adam’s seed provided a place for it to be clothed. Therefore, he (Cain) became a murderer, as it is said (Isaiah 14:29): "From the serpent's root will come a basilisk," etc. For the attribute of [divine] judgment flows over him. And Jonathan ben Uziel <note>The Targum Pseudo-Jonathan, an Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Torah.</note>, peace be upon him, translated it thus: "And Adam knew his wife, who had conceived from the angel Sammael and was pregnant; and she gave birth to Cain, who resembled those above and not those below, and she said: I have acquired a man, the angel of the LORD." <note>original Hebrew: כי קין נולד מן הזוהמא והטפה שהטיל הנחש בחוה וגו׳ גם בלתי זרע אדם שנתערב באותה הזוהמא לא היה יכולת לרוח ההוא ללבוש גוף אדם ולצאת לאויר העולם וזרע האדם המציא לו מקום להתלבש בו ועל כן נעשה הורג כד"א משרש נחש יצא צפע וגו' כי מדת הדין שופעת עליו . וכן תרגם יונתן בן עוזיאל ע"ה ואדם ידע ית חוה איתתיה דהיא מתעברא מן סמאל מלאכא ועדיאת ית קין והוה דמי לעילאי ולא לתתאי ואמרת קניתי גברא ית מלאכא דיי' :</note> That is: Know that Cain was born from the uncleanness and the drop which the serpent cast into Eve; but because it was impossible for that spirit to be clothed in a human body and come out into the atmosphere of the world without the mixing of Adam’s seed with that same uncleanness, Adam’s seed provided a place for it to be clothed. For this reason, he (Cain) became a murderer, as is said in (Isaiah 14:29): **"Out of the serpent’s root shall come a basilisk,"** etc. For the quality of Judgment has its influence (or its influx) over him. His mouth is thus to be stuffed so that he cannot accuse them, because the gift given to him keeps him from it, which gift is said to have been given to him since ancient times.

# How many nations there are in the world, and who rules them. 835 #

<margin>...[Sammael] had already been given [this] in ancient times.</margin>
<margin>The sins of the Jews shall all be laid upon Sammael's people.</margin>
...mentioned in **Leviticus** <note>The OCR reads "vitici," a fragment of the Latin *Levitici*</note> 16, v. 21, 22, who is called **Azazel** <note>Often translated as the "scapegoat," representing a wilderness demon or a rocky precipice</note> there in v. 8. In the *Yalkut Chadash* <note>A 17th-century collection of Kabbalistic midrashim</note>, folio 101, column 3, number 21, the following is stated from the *Zohar* <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> regarding this: <note>original Hebrew: "כיון שמקבל סמאל השעיר וישראל מחזורין עונותיהם ובא סמאל ונעשה סניגור..."</note> That is: After **Sammael** receives the goat, and the Israelites have confessed their sins (upon the goat), then Sammael comes and becomes their **advocate** <term>Sanegor</term> <note>From the Greek *synegoros*, a legal advocate or defender</note> or intercessor (before God, and no longer accuses them because of the gift). Thereupon God speaks to all **seventy princes** <note>In Jewish tradition, these are the seventy celestial angels who govern the seventy nations of the world</note>: "Have you seen this one, who always accuses my children, and now, because of a single goat over which my children have confessed all their sins and given to him, he has become an intercessor (for them)?" Hereupon they all agree together that all the sins (of the Israelites) shall come upon the head of **his** (namely, Sammael's) **people**. And if the nations knew of this goat (and that the sins of the Israelites were thereby cast upon their own necks), they would (God forbid) not leave a single survivor of Israel in the world, not even for one day.

<margin>Through the gift which is given to Sammael, he is not to be served.</margin>
However, since the Jews could be accused of serving the Devil through such a gift, **Rabbi Isaac Karo** <note>A Spanish rabbi and physician, uncle of the famous Joseph Karo</note> teaches the following in his book *Toledot Yitzchak*, folio 76, column 1, in the *Parashah Acharei Mot* <note>The Torah portion "After the death," which describes the Day of Atonement rituals</note>, to refute this: <note>original Hebrew: "השוחד אינו עבודה כי העבודה באהבה ובטוב לבב..."</note> That is: The gift is no service <note>referring to divine service or worship</note>, for service happens out of love and a good heart; for everything that a servant gives to his king or his lord happens to the end that he may fulfill his will and do him good. But a human gives a **gift** <term>Shakhad</term> <note>Often meaning a bribe or protection money</note> to one of whom he is afraid that he might do him evil, so that he may not harm him. And this is what is meant by giving a gift to Sammael: and the Holy and Blessed God sends from His own table and from His own property to the power of (the planet) **Mars** <note>The text uses the Latin *Martis*; Sammael is traditionally associated with Mars, the planet of war and blood</note> (that is, to Sammael), so that he may do no harm to the Israelites. More on this is also found in **Rabbi Bechai's** <note>Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish commentator</note> commentary on the five books of Moses, folio 139, column 1, in the *Parashah Acharei Mot*, where he teaches among other things that when one gives a gift to the Devil, it is just as if one throws a piece of food to a dog so that it will not bite him.

# Chapter 18 of the First Part of Judaism Unmasked #

<margin>Job is said to have been plagued by Satan because he gave him no gift.</margin>
It is also said that Job was plagued by Satan because he gave him no gift, about which it is written in the *Yalkut Chadash* <note>A 17th-century Kabbalistic anthology</note> folio 40, column 2, number 35, under the title *Beth ha-Mikdash* <note>The Holy Temple</note>, from the *Zohar* <note>The primary text of Jewish mysticism</note> as follows: <note>original Hebrew: איוב כתיב העלה עלות מספר כולם ועולה כולה לגבוה סלקא ולא היה בה חלק לסטרא אחרא לכך שלט עליו השטן ואי לא היו כל קרבנותיו עולות והיה נותן חלק גם לשטן לא היה יכול לשלוט עליו</note> That is: Regarding Job it is written (Job 1:5): "And offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all." A burnt offering <note>original: *Brandopffer* / *Olah*</note>, however, rises entirely to the Highest alone (and is offered to God alone, and there was no portion therein for the *Sitra Achra* <term>Sitra Achra</term> <note>A Kabbalistic term meaning "the Other Side," referring to the realm of evil or the demonic</note>, that is, the other side—understand this as the impure and evil spirit); for this reason, Satan had power over him. If, however, his offerings had not been solely burnt offerings, and he had also given a portion to Satan, then he [Satan] would have had no power over him.

<margin>Why Abel's sacrifice was accepted by God, but Cain's sacrifice was not pleasing.</margin>
In the cited *Yalkut Chadash*, it is also taught on folio 6, column 1, number 72, from the *Zohar*, that Abel also gave something from his sacrifice to Satan, and the words read as follows: <note>original Hebrew: קרבנו של הבל נתקבל לפי שעיקר הקרבן עשה להק"בה אלא שנתן חלק גם לסטרא אחרא וקין עשה איפקא עיקר הקרבן לסטרא אחרא ויהי' הולקיה להק"בה לכך לא נתקבל</note> That is: Abel's sacrifice was accepted (by God) because he performed the main part of his sacrifice for the holy, blessed God, yet he also gave a portion to the *Sitra Achra* (that is, the other side, namely the Devil). Cain, however, did the opposite, because he gave the most prominent part of his sacrifice to the other side, and only a portion to the holy and blessed God; for this reason, it was not pleasing.

<margin>The people over whom Sammael rules are said to be the descendants of Esau.</margin>
Since Sammael is one of—and indeed the most prominent of—the aforementioned seventy princes who are said to rule the seventy nations, we must now also see what kind of people are subject to him. It is to be known that Esau—that is, the Christian people <note>In medieval Jewish literature, "Esau" or "Edom" was frequently used as a coded reference to the Roman Empire and, by extension, the Christian world</note>—is said to have been assigned to him, of which Rabbi Menachem of Recanati <note>A famous Italian Kabbalist, c. 1250–1310</note> writes in his commentary on the five books of Moses, folio 141, column 2 and 3, in this manner: <note>original Hebrew: צוה הק"בה ביום הכפור שנשלח שעיר במדבר לשר המושל במקומות החרבן והזא הראוי לו מפני שהוא בעליו מאצילות כחו יבא חרבן ושממון כי הוא העילה לכוכבי החרב והדמים והמלחמות והמריבות והמכות והפירוד והחרבן והכלל שהוא נפש מאדים וחלקו מן האומות הוא עשו שהוא עם היורש החרב והמלחמות</note> That is: The holy, blessed God commanded that on the Day of Atonement we should send a goat into the wilderness to the prince who rules in the places of desolation, and such is his due because he is the **Lord** over it. And in the book *Zeror Hammor* <note>"A Bundle of Myrrh," a 15th-century commentary</note> it is written on folio 46, column 2, in the portion *Vayishlach* <note>The weekly reading "And he sent"</note>: <note>original Hebrew: לפי שהיה מתאחר בדרך נשכו נחש הקדמוני שטן הוא יצר הרע הוא סמאל שרו של עשו</note> that is: **Because he (namely Jacob) delayed on the way, the ancient serpent bit him, which is the Satan, the evil inclination, the Sammael, and the Prince of Esau.** The scholar Isaac Abarbanel <note>A famous statesman and theologian</note> also writes in his commentary on the 65th chapter of Isaiah, folio 93, column 4, as follows: <note>original Hebrew: כבר ידעת שסמאל הוא שרו של עשו</note> that is: **You are already aware that Sammael is the Prince of Esau.** This is also found in the often-mentioned commentary on the Five Books of Moses by Rabbi Menahem of Recanati, folio 59, column 2, in the portion *Toledoth Jizchak*, and in the *Zijoni* folio 24, column 1, and in the small *Yalkut Reubeni* <note>A Kabbalistic anthology</note> number 46, under the title *Avoth Veimmahot* <note>Fathers and Mothers</note>, and in the large *Yalkut Reubeni* folio 53, column 3, and folio 54, column 3, in the portion *Vayeitze* <note>"And he went out"</note>, and folio 60, column 1, in the portion *Vayishlach*, and in the *Yalkut Chadash* <note>"The New Collection"</note>, folio 112, column 1, number 31, as well as in the book *Emek Hammelech* <note>"The King’s Valley," a 17th-century Kabbalistic text</note> folio 99, column 2, in the 81st chapter, under the title *Shaar Kiryath Arba* <note>The Gate of the City of Four</note>.

<margin>II. Esau’s Overseer.</margin>
**Secondly,** he is called <note>original Aramaic: ממונה דעשו</note> *Memuneh de-Esau*, that is, **Esau’s Overseer.** Therefore, in the large *Yalkut Reubeni* folio 60, column 2, in the portion *Vayishlach*, it reads as follows: <note>original Aramaic: אית מאן דלא ידע בושתי דא איהו ממונא דעשו שהיה יודע מעלתו דיעקב כמה הוא מעלייא ולא נתבייש ממנו</note> that is: **There is one who cannot feel shame, and such a one is the *Memuneh de-Esau*, that is, the Overseer of Esau, who knew the excellence of Jacob, how glorious he was, and yet was not ashamed before him.**

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Sammaël, the spiritual prince associated with Edom and Rome. Having previously established his role as the "Prince of Rome," the author now explores his identification with Amalek and the mystical "Shells" (Keliphot) that represent the forces of evil in Kabbalistic thought.</meta>

### How many nations are in the world, and who rules them.

The Prince of Amalek is the **Head** among the **Kelifóth** <note>original Hebrew: *Kelifot* (קליפות), meaning "shells" or "husks" which in Kabbalah represent the forces of spiritual impurity</note> (or Kelifos), which is to say, the **Shells** (by which, as already noted above, the evil spirits are understood). For this reason, he is called **Amaleck**, which are the letters of **Am kal** <note>original Hebrew: *Am kal* (עם קל)</note> (meaning a "light people," or a people of one hundred and thirty). This is because he (Amalek) came with one hundred and thirty hosts of Sammaël; for the word **Sammaël** <note>Samech (60) + Mem (40) + Aleph (1) + Lamed (30) = 131</note> amounts to the number one hundred and thirty-one, because he has one hundred and thirty hosts <note>The leader himself being the 131st</note>. And in the book **Schené luchóth habberith** <note>The "Two Tablets of the Covenant," a major work of Jewish law and mysticism by Isaiah Horowitz</note>, folio 307, column 1, we read: *Amalek is the essence of the unclean body itself, and Sammaël is its prince.* <note>original Hebrew: עמלק הוא עצם גוף הטמא ושרו הוא סמאל</note>

<margin>
IX. The Kelipha or Shell of Edom and Amalek.
</margin>
**Ninthly**, he is called **Kelifäth Edom va-Amaleck** <note>original Hebrew: קליפת אדום ועמלק</note>, that is, **the Kelifa or Shell of Edom and Amalek**. This is read in the book **Emek hammélech** <note>"The Valley of the King," a 17th-century Kabbalistic text by Naftali Hertz ben Jacob Elhanan</note>, folio 130, column 1, in the 11th chapter under the title **Scháar réscha díser änpin** with these **words:** *Sammaël appears above like an ox or a pig, especially during a time of plague (or the pestilence)—from which may God protect us—he appears to humans as a black ox; and certainly, whoever sees him will not be saved. Thus also the names Ox, Donkey, and Dog [found in the heart] prove that he is the Shell of Edom, Ishmael, and Amalek, which is a beast.* <note>original Hebrew: סמאל נראה כשור למעלה או כחזיר ובפרט בשעת המגפה בר מנן נראה לבני אדם כשור שחור ובאמת לא ינצל האיש הרואה אותו וגם ש"ור ח"מור ב"לב יוכח שהוא קליפת אדום וישמעאל ועמלק שהוא בהמה</note>

<margin>

-> ### How many nations there are in the world, and who rules them. <-

<note>original Hebrew: "אין לו אלוה ועל זה נאמר אותי עזבו מקור מים חיים לחצוב להם בארות בארות נשברים אשר לא יכילו המים׃"</note> He has no God, and concerning this it is said: **"They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, to hew out for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns that can hold no water."** <note>Jeremiah 2:13</note> That is, that which makes it true (and confirms) that this Angel was not one of the *abstract intelligences* <note>original: "Intelligentiis abstractis"; a philosophical term for beings existing purely as spirit without physical bodies</note>, (that is, of those angels who were created without bodies), is the statement of the same (namely, of Jacob), in which he says: **"May he bless the boys"** <note>Genesis 48:16</note>; and far be it from our holy father [Jacob], upon whom be peace, that he should have desired a blessing for his sons from an *abstract intelligence* <note>original: "Intelligentia abstracta"</note>, that is, an angel created without a body. For a blessing is not desired except from Him in whose strength and power it stands to bless, who is the only blessed **God**; and whoever desires a blessing from anyone else has no **God**, and of such a person it is said in Jeremiah 2, verse 13: **"They have forsaken Me, the living fountain, and made for themselves here and there hewn-out wells, which are nevertheless broken and hold no water."** If, therefore, no one but **God** can bless, why should Jacob have desired a blessing from a created angel?

Secondly, it is proven from this that this Angel was **God**, because Jacob said in Genesis 32, verse 30: **"And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my soul is preserved."** Since it was generally held by the Jews in ancient times that a man who sees **God** the Lord must die, as can be clearly seen in Deuteronomy 5, verses 24–25, Judges 13, verse 22, and Isaiah 6, verse 5; and Jacob here rejoiced that he had seen **God** and yet was preserved in life. But if he had believed that it had been a created angel, he would have had no cause to say such a thing.

Thirdly, it is maintained from Genesis 35, verses 9, 10, and 11, where the words read thus: **"And God appeared unto Jacob again, after he had come out of Mesopotamia, and blessed him, and said unto him: Thy name is Jacob; but thou shalt not be called Jacob any more, but Israel shall be thy name; and so he was called Israel. And God said unto him: I am God Almighty."** From which it is to be seen that the man or Angel who wrestled with Jacob and blessed him, and said to him in Genesis 32, verse 28, **"Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel; for thou hast struggled with God and with men,"** appeared to him here again, blessed him, and told him that he should no longer be called Jacob but Israel; and he also announced there that he was the almighty **God**.

Fourthly, it is confirmed because it stands written in Hosea 12, verse 4, that Jacob fought with the Angel and overcame him; as also, that

# How many nations are in the world / and who rules them. 849

He [the Angel] delivered him from all evil; therefore He (namely the Angel, Genesis 31, verse 13) said: **"I am the God of Bethel."** However, through a mystery—which I intend to explain in the following with the help of God—He is called an Angel. He is also the one of whom it is said (Exodus 3, verse 2): **"And the Angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the bush."** And because He is the Angel of His (meaning God's) Presence <note>The "Angel of the Presence" or "Angel of the Face" is a term used in theology to describe a being who represents God's very essence or person.</note>, and the face (of a man) is the man himself, Onkelos <note>A famous convert to Judaism (c. 35–120 AD) known for the Targum Onkelos, the authoritative Aramaic translation of the Torah.</note> translated it thus in his Chaldean translation: **"And the Angel of the LORD appeared,"** which is the same as if it had been said, **"And (Jehovah or) the LORD appeared to him,"** which is said of Abraham and Isaac (Genesis 18, verse 1 and 26, verses 2 and 24): and it is as much as if it were said: **"And God appeared to Jacob, etc."** This (Angel) is also necessarily the one of whom it is said (Exodus 14, verse 19): **"Then the Angel of God arose."** Thus, He is also necessarily the Angel of the Covenant.

Furthermore, the aforementioned Rabbi Meir ben Gabbai <note>A 16th-century Italian scholar and Kabbalist.</note> writes in the stated book *Avodat ha-Kodesh* <term>Hebrew: "Holy Service"</term>, in the 34th chapter of the fourth part, folio 136, column 4, that this Angel gave the Law from Mount Sinai, with these words:

<note>original Hebrew: "אפשר לומר עוד כי רבי יוחנן מודה שלא הגיעו הדברות לישראל על יד אמצעי כפשוטן של כתובים והמלאך שהזכיר אינו מן הנפרדים אבל הוא המלאך הגואל והוא שכתוב בו ויסע מלאך האלהים מלאך שהוא האלהים והוא המשמיע הדברות לישראל שנאמר וידבר אלהים:"</note>
that is: It can further be said that Rabbi Jochanan <note>Likely referring to Jochanan bar Nappaha, a leading rabbi of the 3rd century.</note> admits that the ten words (that is, the Commandments) did not come to the Israelites through a mediator, according to the literal sense of the Scriptures: and the Angel of whom he makes mention is not one of those angels who were created without bodies <note>Meaning he is not a "separate" or purely created intellect/spirit.</note>, but He is the *Malach ha-goel* <term>The Redeeming Angel</term>: and he is the same one of whom it is said (Exodus 14, verse 19): **"Then the Angel of God arose"**: the Angel who is God: and He is the same one who proclaimed the (ten) words (that is, the Commandments) to the children of Israel, as it is said (Exodus 20, verse 1): **"And God spoke."** We see, therefore, from the cited words of Rabbi Meir ben Gabbai, that the Redeeming Angel is God Himself. Since, then, the Angel who wrestled with Jacob was the Redeeming Angel, it follows indisputably that He is also God. How then can the nonsensical Jews <note>The author, Johann Eisenmenger, uses highly polemical and derogatory language typical of his 1700 work "Entdecktes Judenthum" (Judaism Unmasked).</note> make the devil Samael <note>In Jewish lore, Samael is often the figure associated with the angel of death or the adversary who wrestled with Jacob.</note> out of Him? However, God willing, the divinity of this Angel shall be treated by me more extensively in another book.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the angelic hierarchy and spiritual oversight of Israel.
